title: Associate Director, Program Management
description:
Revolution Medicines is a global, commercial-state oncology company dedicated to discovering, developing and delivering innovative medicines for patients with RAS-addicted cancers. Leveraging its differentiated RAS(ON) tri-complex inhibitor platform, the company is advancing a broad, integrated portfolio of oral RAS(ON) inhibitors designed to directly target the active, cancer-driving state of RAS. Founded on rigorous scientific inquiry and a willingness to challenge long-held assumptions, Revolution Medicines is committed to changing the trajectory of disease for patients with RAS-addicted cancers worldwide.

Our people are united by a shared way of working: follow the science, challenge assumptions, act with urgency and hold ourselves to a high standard of rigor—all in service of patients.

The Opportunity:

This is an exciting, high-profile, and highly visible Program Management opportunity to advance first-in-Class RAS(ON) Inhibitors through clinical development. The ideal candidate is a very proficient and self-motivated program manager with a solid understanding of drug development. The Associate Director (AD) acts as a connector across the program ensuring clarity of roles and responsibilities, decision making and accountability for deliverables. They routinely partner with the Lead Program Management and Sub-Team Leaders to translate program strategy into an efficient execution plan. They understand the objectives of the program team and the roles of sub-team members to facilitate productive discussions and decision-making. The AD manages cross-functionally to achieve program milestones. They also play a pivotal role in communications, making sure that teams have access to accurate and timely information regarding program decisions, assumptions, expectations and timelines.

Overall, the AD is responsible for program execution at the sub-team level. They not only care about the outcomes but how we get there. The successful candidate will draw upon their experience to:

  • Understand the program strategy, stakeholders and interdependencies and works with sub-teams to develop set priorities and execute against their plans.

  • Manage the integrated project plan and project assumptions (accounting for goals, key objectives, deliverables, risks) to enable accurate project, financial and portfolio analyses for business planning processes.

  • Identify critical path activities, resource constraints, risks, and conflicts that could impact the timelines or budget; work with subject matter experts to construct appropriate mitigation plans.

  • Contribute to scenario planning (comprising costs, timelines, risks, and project strategy) to inform stage gate, portfolio, budget and long-range planning.

  • Manage the preparation, review, editing and submission of project documents, presentations and communications.

  • Lead an efficient information flow within the project team and sub-teams, and prepare materials and reports for internal advisory and governance meetings.

  • Practice effective meeting and information management including, timely meeting agendas and minutes.

  • Facilitate project team meetings, follow up on action items, document meeting materials and decisions, and act as a primary contact for project team related information.

  • Partner with the sub-team leads to ensure the team achieves and maintains a high-level of sustainable performance. Identify and resolve issues related to efficient and effective team operation.

  • Recommend and implement opportunities for streamlining team and business processes.

  • Drive adoption of project management systems and best practices across the program team.

  • Onboard and train new team members on program structure, relevant stakeholders and program management resources (team site, project plan, RAID log, meeting calendar, etc.).

  • Support new programs and special projects as needed.

Required Experience, Skills, and Education:

Ideal candidate will have the following experience and be able to demonstrate the following:

  • B.A. or BSc. in Life Sciences and at least 5 years’ experience in the biotech/pharmaceutical industry with at least 2 years’ direct development project management experience managing cross-functional development teams.

  • Understanding of the clinical drug development process and regulations, coupled with strong proficiency in project management practices, tools, and methodology.

  • Expertise in developing and managing project scope, deliverables, risk & resource requirements including, schedule / timeline management, and risk management.

  • Excellent interpersonal skills, including clear, succinct, and timely communication and proven ability to foster important relationships with key stakeholders.

  • Outstanding verbal and written communication skills with the ability to summarize complex information into simple concepts; has the ability to effectively interact across team line functions as well as with external key stakeholders.

  • Proven track record of good decision making and exercising sound judgment.

  • Experience using Project Management software to manage project timelines and resources (e.g., MS Project, Smartsheet, OfficeTimeline, and OnePager Pro etc.).

  • Strong computer proficiency with MS Office suite, SharePoint and similar document archiving systems.

Preferred Skills:

  • MSc. or MBA or Ph.D. a plus.

  • PMP (Project Management Professional) or other PM certification or equivalent is a plus.

  • Experience in Oncology therapeutic area is strongly preferable.

Northampton, Northamptonshire, United Kingdom (relocation and sponsorship support available)

About the Opportunity

Our client is a leading manufacturer of innovative optical and photonic technologies, supplying products that support optical networking, data centres, advanced manufacturing and next- sensing applications. With a global presence across research and development, manufacturing and sales, they are at the forefront of technological innovation.

They are now seeking an experienced Senior Epitaxy Equipment Engineer to join their team at their UK site.

The Role

As Senior Epitaxy Equipment Engineer, you will provide technical and engineering support to the Epitaxy Shift Equipment Engineers and Technicians, ensuring the reliability, performance and availability of critical production equipment.

You will play a key role in maintaining and improving manufacturing equipment to include Veeco and Aixtron instruments and equipment, supporting day-to-day production activities, troubleshooting complex equipment faults to include bioreactors, and delivering continuous improvement initiatives. The position also involves working with process gas systems and hazardous materials, including the use of self-contained breathing apparatus (SCBA), with appropriate training provided where required.

Key Responsibilities

* Plan and coordinate daily maintenance activities in collaboration with Manufacturing and Process Engineering teams.

* Lead and support epitaxy equipment improvements, upgrades and installations.

* Provide technical input into new equipment procurement, commissioning and release to production.

* Maintain and troubleshoot MOVPE equipment, MOCVD equipment and associated systems to minimise downtime and maximise production efficiency.

* Carry out phosphorous-trap and gas cylinder changes using SCBA, following the required safety procedures.

* Oversee the management of chemicals, process gases, spare parts, chemical fills and waste disposal.

* Provide technical guidance and instruction to Shift Technicians on equipment procedures, safety requirements and engineering best practice.

* Support equipment relocation, cleanroom reorganisation, shipping and other logistical projects.

* Assist with planned shutdown activities, including occasional weekend overtime where required.

* Liaise with equipment suppliers, spare parts providers and specialist service companies, including supervising external contractors and field service engineers.

* Develop and implement preventative maintenance strategies to improve equipment utilisation, reliability and uptime.

* Maintain compliance with all site health, safety and environmental procedures.

* Support the site's emergency response function.

Qualifications and Experience

* HNC, degree or equivalent qualification in Electrical or Mechanical Engineering, or a time-served engineering apprenticeship.

* At least five years' experience in a semiconductor wafer fabrication or epitaxy engineering environment.

* Electrical qualifications, such as BS 7671 18th Edition, would be advantageous.

Essential Skills and Experience

* Strong electrical engineering knowledge, including experience working with low- and high-voltage systems.

* Extensive semiconductor equipment engineering experience, ideally involving MOVPE and/or MOCVD technologies.

* Experience working in a fast-paced semiconductor manufacturing environment.

* Comprehensive knowledge of vacuum systems, including high-vacuum principles, pumps and leak-checking techniques.

* Good understanding of pneumatic systems and PLC operation.

* Ability to interpret and understand electrical wiring diagrams and mechanical schematics.

* Familiarity with hazardous process gases and the associated safety requirements.

* Competent user of Microsoft Office applications.

* Strong problem-solving skills, with the ability to provide effective technical support in a production environment.

Interested?

If you have a strong background in semiconductor equipment engineering and experience supporting epitaxy manufacturing operations, this is an excellent opportunity to take on a technically challenging role within a specialist, high-technology manufacturing environment.

title: Shift Equipment Engineer — Wafer Fab and Epitaxy in NN12, Grimscote, West Northamptonshire
description:
Location: Northampton, Northamptonshire, United Kingdom (relocation and sponsorship support available)

About Our Client

Our client is a global leader in innovative optical and photonic products, enabling optical networking and commercial laser solutions worldwide. Their advanced technologies are integral to virtually every type of telecom, enterprise, and data centre network globally. The UK wafer fabrication facility in Caswell serves as a world-class centre of excellence for high-performance optoelectronic devices used in telecommunications and industrial systems.

Role Summary

As an Equipment Engineer / Technician, you will provide critical technical support for the operation, fault diagnosis, and maintenance of advanced wafer fabrication and epitaxy process tools. Working on a continental shift pattern, you will manage complex vacuum, pneumatic, mechanical, electrical, and RF systems within a highly specialised, safety-critical cleanroom manufacturing environment.

This is a hands-on, high-precision engineering role ideal for individuals with experience maintaining complex electro-mechanical systems in critical environments. We actively welcome applications from UK Armed Forces technical trades, aerospace, aviation, and defence engineering backgrounds. Direct semiconductor experience is advantageous but not essential, as comprehensive training will be provided.

Key Responsibilities

* Rapid Engineering Response: Deliver first-line engineering interventions to minimise tool downtime and maximise Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE).

* Asset Maintenance: Conduct precise repairs, fault diagnosis, and preventative maintenance on semiconductor processing equipment, including lithography, etch, PVD, PECVD, and MOVPE reactor systems.

* Safety & Compliance: Manage chemical and specialty gas supply systems in strict compliance with statutory, site safety, and environmental standards (including gas delivery, exhaust, and abatement systems).

* Inventory & Planning: Manage spare parts inventory to secure component availability and participate in production planning meetings to represent engineering performance metrics.

* Continuous Improvement: Support site continuous improvement initiatives (Kaizen, 6S, 8D) and maintain accurate documentation of actions and outcomes.

* Site Emergency Response: Support the site emergency function, including participation in the Site Emergency Response Team (training provided).

Qualifications & Experience

* An Apprenticeship, HNC, HND, or Degree in an Electrical or Mechanical Engineering discipline (or equivalent).

* Alternatively: A minimum of 5 years’ directly relevant experience in complex electro-mechanical system maintenance within high-reliability environments.

* Direct experience in high-tech manufacturing, aerospace, defence, automotive, pharmaceuticals, oil & gas, power , or military technical sectors is highly transferable.

Key Skills Required

* Proven fault-finding and diagnostic ability across electrical, electronic, and mechanical systems.

* Ability to work safely with hazardous gases and chemicals, adhering strictly to safety-critical protocols.

* Competence in documenting procedures, risk assessments, and method statements.

* Strong team-oriented communication skills and basic proficiency in Microsoft Office applications.

* Desirable: Previous experience within a semiconductor or cleanroom manufacturing environment.

Shift Pattern & Working Conditions

* Hours: 40.3 hours per week on a continental shift pattern (2 days, 2 nights, 4 off).

* Shifts: 12-hour shifts including weekends and bank holidays as part of the continental rotation.

* Environment: Work is performed within a cleanroom environment (cleanroom garments provided).

* Safety Requirements: The role requires the use of Self-Contained Breathing Apparatus (SCBA). Candidates must be able to meet the medical and respiratory protective equipment (RPE) face-fit requirements associated with SCBA use.

* Logistics: A full UK driving licence and access to own transport are essential due to the rural setting of the Northampton UK facility.

* Eligibility: Our client will support VISA/sponsorship and will also consider relocation assistance for the right candidate

title: Information Systems Security Officer (ISSO) III
description:
The Information Systems Security Officer (ISSO) II is responsible for ensuring the appropriate operational security posture is maintained for an information system and as such, works in close collaboration with the ISSM and ISO. The position shall have the detailed knowledge and expertise required to manage the security aspects of an information system and, in many organizations, is assigned responsibility for the day-to-day security operations of a system.

This will include physical and environmental protection, personnel security, incident handling, and security training and awareness. It will be required to work in close coordination with the ISSM and ISO in monitoring the information system(s) and its environment of operation to include developing and updating the authorization documentation, implementing configuration management across authorization boundaries. This will include assessing the security impact of those changes and making recommendation to the ISSM. The primary function is working within Special Access Programs (SAPs) supporting Department of Defense (DoD) agencies, such as HQ Air Force, Office of the Secretary of Defense (OSD) and Military Compartments efforts. The position will provide “day-to-day” support for Collateral, Sensitive Compartmented Information (SCI) and Special Access Program (SAP) activities.

Performance shall include:

  • Assist the ISSM in meeting their duties and responsibilities.

  • Prepare, review, and update authorization packages.

  • Ensure approved procedures are in place for clearing, sanitizing, and destroying various types of hardware and media.

  • Notify ISSM when changes occur that might affect the authorization determination of the information system(s).

  • Conduct periodic reviews of information systems to ensure compliance with the security authorization package.

  • Coordinate any changes or modifications to hardware, software, or firmware of a system with the ISSM and AO/DAO prior to the change.

  • Monitor system recovery processes to ensure security features and procedures are properly restored and functioning correctly.

  • Ensure all IS security-related documentation is current and accessible to properly authorized individuals.

  • Ensure audit records are collected, reviewed, and documented (to include any anomalies)

  • Attend required technical and security training (e.g., operating system, networking, security management) relative to assigned duties.

  • Execute the cyber security portion of the self-inspection, to include security coordination and review of all system assessment plans.

  • Identify cyber security vulnerabilities and assist with the implementation of the countermeasures for them.

  • Prepare reports on the status of security safeguards applied to computer systems.

  • Perform ISSO duties in support of in-house and external customers.

  • Conduct continuous monitoring activities for authorization boundaries under your preview.

  • Assist Department of Defense, National Agency and Contractor organizations with the development of assessment and authorization (A&A) efforts.

Experience:

  • 5+ years related experience.

  • 2+ years SAP experience required.

  • Prior performance in roles such as System, Network Administrator or ISSO.


Education:

  • Bachelor’s degree in a related area or equivalent experience (4 years)


Certifications:

  • IAT Level II ( Security+ CE, CCNA Security, etc) or IAM Level II - within 6 months of hire


Clearance Required to Start:

  • TS/SCI required

  • Must be able to Attain – TS/SCI with CI Polygraph


#AirforceSAPOpportunities

Security Clearance: Top Secret / SCI + Polygraph

Pfäffikon, Switzerland | 80–100% | Starting: Immediately or upon agreement

About CREATEQ

CREATEQ is a Swiss software engineering company with more than 30 years of experience in delivering custom software solutions and modernizing complex legacy systems. We work with leading international companies across industries such as banking and fintech, insurance, aviation and transportation, telecommunications, and energy.

We design, build, and run high-quality software solutions, combining strong engineering expertise, modern technologies, AI-enabled approaches, and proven delivery practices. In this role, you will win new clients, shape their entry into AI-driven software engineering, and turn it into long-term engineering engagements delivered by our teams.

Many companies still develop software the traditional way, mostly on Java and .NET. They want to benefit from AI-driven development but lack the know-how, processes, and capacity to do so. This is where you come in: you understand the client's starting point, develop the right approach together with them – from assessment and proof of concept to dedicated nearshore teams – and close the deal.

You will work closely with management, Business Development, and our engineering leads, and you will be the face of CREATEQ to CIOs, CTOs, and Heads of Engineering in Switzerland [and the DACH region].

This is a senior role with clear revenue responsibility. We are looking for someone who has successfully sold IT services before, brings a strong network in the Swiss market, and is equally credible in conversations with developers and with executive management.

You might be a great fit if you have:

· At least 8 years of experience selling IT services, software engineering, or nearshore/offshore capacity, including several years with personal revenue responsibility.

What we offer

· An offering that is high on clients' agendas: AI-driven software engineering, delivered by experienced engineering teams.

· A compensation package with a fixed salary and a performance-based component.

· Direct collaboration with management and short decision paths.

· Freedom to shape the role, bring your ideas, and make a visible impact.

· A long-term perspective in an international software engineering company with a strong presence in the European market.

Apply directly via LinkedIn.

title: Senior Algorithm Engineer - Radar Systems
description:
Why Castelion, Why Now

Castelion is moving incredibly fast to develop and deliver advanced defense systems at a time when execution matters more than ever. We believe focus, ownership, and excellence are decisive advantages - and we're building a world-class team to turn bold ideas into real capability.

This is a rare opportunity to join at an early stage, where you'll have significant ownership, collaborate with exceptional teammates, and make a direct, measurable impact on our mission and the future of the company - regardless of your function.

Senior Algorithm Engineer – Radar Systems

As an Algorithm Engineer on Castelion's Seeker Algorithm team, you will develop, implement, and maintain advanced algorithms responsible for the detection, localization, and identification of moving and stationary targets across land, maritime, and air environments.

This is an ownership-oriented engineering role. You will be responsible for taking algorithms from development through verification and production, ensuring solutions are accurate, computationally efficient, scalable, and compatible with existing system architectures. You'll work closely with software, firmware, simulation, and test teams to deliver high-quality algorithmic capabilities that support critical program milestones.

We are looking for engineers who enjoy solving complex technical problems, working with real-world test data, and taking ownership of their solutions from initial development through operational implementation.

Responsibilities

  • Develop, implement, and maintain Python-based algorithms for target detection, localization, and identification across multiple operating environments.
  • Own assigned algorithms throughout the development lifecycle, from initial design and implementation through verification, testing, and production deployment.
  • Create and maintain algorithm design documentation, verification artifacts, and supporting technical documentation.
  • Develop and maintain automated regression testing to identify defects and prevent unintended changes before code is merged into the primary development branch.
  • Conduct peer reviews of algorithm changes and ensure implementation quality, reliability, and consistency with engineering standards.
  • Troubleshoot, investigate, and resolve algorithm performance issues, defects, and integration challenges.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional engineering teams to establish verification environments, including simulation, hardware-in-the-loop (HWIL), flight testing, and test shots.
  • Analyze test data, evaluate algorithm performance, and communicate findings through clear, concise technical reports.
  • Ensure algorithms remain compatible with existing system architectures and processing requirements.
  • Partner with real-time software and firmware engineers to optimize computational performance, processing loads, and runtime requirements.
  • Identify opportunities for algorithm improvements and maintain a prioritized backlog of future enhancements.
  • Take ownership of existing algorithms, including partially completed implementations, and drive them to production-ready maturity.

Basic Qualifications

  • Experience developing algorithms for radar systems or related sensing applications.
  • Understanding of radar phenomenology and the underlying principles of radar signal behavior.
  • Experience analyzing, interpreting, and troubleshooting real-world test data.
  • Experience developing, maintaining, or working with radar simulations.
  • Working knowledge of software development processes, including testing, version control, and configuration management.
  • Basic proficiency in Python programming, with the ability to develop, maintain, and troubleshoot algorithm implementations.
  • Ability to work cross-functionally with software, firmware, systems engineering, and test teams.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to independently drive technical challenges to resolution.
  • Ability to communicate complex technical findings clearly and effectively.

Preferred Skills and Experience

  • Knowledge of probability theory, estimation theory, and statistical signal processing.
  • Experience with hardware-in-the-loop testing, flight testing, or other hardware-based verification environments.
  • Experience optimizing algorithms for real-time embedded processing environments.
  • Experience transitioning algorithms from research and development into production systems.
  • Experience with radar target detection, tracking, classification, or identification.

title: Senior Principal Reverse Engineer

Nightwing is supporting a U.S. Government customer to provide support for onsite incident response to civilian Government agencies and critical asset owners who experience cyber-attacks, providing immediate investigation and resolution. Contract personnel perform investigations to characterize the severity of breaches, develop mitigation plans, and assist with the restoration of services. Nightwing is seeking a Subject Matter Expert with hardware reverse engineering to support this critical customer mission.

The Subject Matter Expert Hardware Reverse Engineers will provide specialized expertise in hardware reverse engineering focused on operational technology (OT) and industrial control systems. This position requires deep technical knowledge of proprietary hardware systems, exploitation methodologies, and defensive strategies to support forensic investigations of compromised edge devices and systems where threat actors have embedded malware deeply within hardware components.

This position focuses on the analytical and investigative aspects of hardware forensics, with particular emphasis on operational technology and industrial control systems. The ideal candidates will have strong reverse engineering skills and deep understanding of threat actor methodologies targeting critical infrastructure.

- Conduct comprehensive hardware reverse engineering of OT and ICS devices

- Analyze network-edge devices and embedded systems compromised by advanced threats

- Perform deep-dive analysis of proprietary hardware targeted by adversaries

- Conduct reverse engineering, failure analysis, vulnerability analysis, and other research techniques to understand complex hardware systems, assess the functionality of components, and identify exploitation risks

- Identify and extract deeply embedded malware from hardware components

- Reverse engineer firmware and low-level software on embedded devices

- Collaborate with Nightwing research teams to leverage cutting-edge analytical capabilities

- Document exploitation methodologies and defensive countermeasures

- Develop standard operating procedures for hardware forensics workflows

- Train CSD analysts on hardware reverse engineering techniques

- Provide expert consultation on edge device security and vulnerabilities

- Support forensic investigations in environments lacking EDR visibility

- Analyze proprietary communication protocols and embedded systems functions

- Identify hardware backdoors, implants, and malicious modifications

- Document technical findings and intelligence for stakeholder dissemination

- Deep expertise in OT/ICS hardware platforms and vulnerabilities

- Ability to analyze novel or proprietary systems with limited documentation

- Strong communication skills for explaining complex technical findings

- Strong experience with firmware reverse engineering and analysis

- Proficiency with reverse engineering tools (IDA Pro, Ghidra, Binary Ninja)

- Deep understanding of ARM, MIPS, PowerPC, and other embedded processor architectures

- Experience analyzing network-edge devices (routers, switches, firewalls, IoT devices)

- Knowledge of hardware debugging interfaces (JTAG, SWD, UART)

- Excellent analytical and problem-solving abilities

title: Executive Director, Corporate Affairs Intercontinental (ICON)
description:
Revolution Medicines is a global, commercial-state oncology company dedicated to discovering, developing and delivering innovative medicines for patients with RAS-addicted cancers. Leveraging its differentiated RAS(ON) tri-complex inhibitor platform, the company is advancing a broad, integrated portfolio of oral RAS(ON) inhibitors designed to directly target the active, cancer-driving state of RAS. Founded on rigorous scientific inquiry and a willingness to challenge long-held assumptions, Revolution Medicines is committed to changing the trajectory of disease for patients with RAS-addicted cancers worldwide.

Our people are united by a shared way of working: follow the science, challenge assumptions, act with urgency and hold ourselves to a high standard of rigor—all in service of patients.

The Opportunity

As we expand globally, the Intercontinental (ICON) region represents a strategically important opportunity for clinical development, patient access and future commercialization. This is a unique leadership opportunity to establish and lead Revolution Medicines’ Corporate Affairs capability across Japan, Canada, Australia, Brazil and the broader ICON region. Reporting to the Senior Vice President, Corporate Affairs, with a dotted line to the Senior Vice President, Intercontinental (ICON), the Executive Director, Corporate Affairs, Intercontinental will shape the company’s external presence and help create the conditions for sustainable growth across the region.

Working as a partner to the ICON leadership team and country General Managers, this leader will be responsible for developing an integrated regional Corporate Affairs strategy across external and internal communications and corporate reputation. The role will help shape healthcare environments that improve cancer outcomes, strengthen healthcare systems and enable timely access to innovation. It will translate global priorities into locally relevant strategies while ensuring country perspectives inform enterprise decisions.

Success in the Role

Within the first 24–36 months, the successful leader will:

  • Establish an integrated ICON strategy and scalable Corporate Affairs network with clear country priorities, accountabilities and measures of impact.

  • Deliver coordinated corporate and launch communications, supported by effective stakeholder governance, issues management and crisis preparedness.

  • Build trusted relationships with industry associations, strengthening the company’s reputation and understanding of patient needs.

  • Support oncology innovation, clinical research and timely, equitable access to precision medicines.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic and Regional Leadership

  • Develop and execute the ICON Corporate Affairs strategy, aligning global objectives with country priorities, market maturity and launch timing.

  • Advise regional leaders and country General Managers on reputational developments; bring country insights into global planning and decision-making forums.

  • Set annual priorities, budgets and performance measures; build a lean operating model with clear responsibilities across global, regional and country teams.

  • Recruit and develop talent as needs evolve; select and manage specialist partners, setting expectations for quality, impact, budget discipline and ethical conduct. Equip countries with practical guidance and share effective approaches.

Corporate Communications and Reputation

  • Develop a coherent regional narrative connecting the company’s science, patient purpose and local contribution; adapt global messaging for local audiences across media, digital and company channels.

  • Partner with the Global Head of Communications to ensure ICON communications advance the global corporate narrative, scientific leadership and reputation priorities, while reflecting local market needs.

  • Build media relationships and lead proactive and reactive communications with Global Communications and country leaders. In partnership with Global Communications, coordinate spokesperson strategy and executive visibility through interviews, speaking engagements and opinion articles.

  • Coordinate communications around affiliate establishment, clinical milestones and launches, ensuring scientific accuracy and appropriate review. Partner with Global Corporate Affairs and Investor Relations on sensitive announcements and disclosure requirements.

  • Bring country and regional insights, trends and milestones into global communications; use stakeholder feedback and media monitoring to assess impact.

Launch Readiness

  • Jointly plan major announcements and launch communications with Global Communications, with clear responsibilities, review processes and escalation expectations across global, regional and country teams.

  • Represent ICON Corporate Affairs in relevant brand teams, asset leadership teams and launch taskforces; identify external opportunities and barriers.

  • Develop integrated campaigns with Medical Affairs, Market Access and Commercial teams. Maintain clear separation between corporate communications, disease awareness and promotional activities, with appropriate local review.

  • Support distributor-market readiness through agreed communications standards, partner responsibilities and escalation processes.

Internal Communications/Employee Engagement

  • Develop and execute regional/country internal communications plans in partnership with Global Executive & Enterprise Communications, regional leaders and HR, aligning employees around company strategy, regional priorities and patient impact.

  • Equip regional and country leaders with messaging and tools to communicate organizational change, affiliate growth and launch milestones consistently and effectively.

  • Ensure ICON internal communications align with global tone, cadence and key messages, while bringing regional employee perspectives and country examples into enterprise communications.

  • Connect employees to strategy and patient progress through leadership forums, town halls and channels aligned with global messaging.

Governance and Issues Management

  • Establish regional issues management and crisis communications preparedness aligned with global protocols and country requirements; coordinate timely responses with relevant global teams, Legal, Compliance, Medical Affairs and Government Affairs.

  • Uphold integrity, protect confidential information and build a culture of accountability, collaboration and patient focus across the Corporate Affairs network.

External Partnership

  • Partner on disease awareness, understanding of precision oncology and barriers to care; collaborate with Medical Affairs and Government Affairs on appropriate engagement with professional societies, research institutions and policy makers.

Required Skills, Experience and Education:

  • Degree in Communications, Life Sciences, Business or a related discipline; advanced degree preferred.

  • At least 15 years of relevant Corporate Affairs, Communications, or Public Affairs experience, including senior leadership responsibility in biopharmaceuticals.

  • Demonstrated success developing and executing integrated Corporate Affairs strategies across multiple countries.

  • Experience building corporate reputation, leading executive communications and managing sensitive issues or crises.

  • Ability to build capabilities and deliver through lean teams, agencies and global matrix organizations, with sound strategic judgment, prioritization and budget management.

  • Exceptional communication, storytelling and executive influencing skills, including translating complex science and policy for non-specialists; fluency in English.

Preferred Skills:

  • Oncology, precision medicine, biomarker-driven healthcare or rare diseases.

  • Affiliate establishment and international launch readiness in a high-growth or early commercial-stage biotechnology company.

  • Regional leadership across Asia-Pacific and Latin America, including direct experience in Japan, Canada, Australia or Brazil.

  • Distributor or partner-led markets, complex stakeholder partnerships and additional languages relevant to ICON.

Leadership Competencies

The successful candidate will demonstrate:

  • Strategic and enterprise thinking — sound policy judgment and courageous decisions.

  • Entrepreneurial leadership — build capabilities, develop people and prioritize for growth.

  • Collaboration and influence — executive presence, cultural awareness and adaptability.

  • Patient focus and integrity — accountability, transparency and meaningful patient outcomes.

Travel

  • This role requires regular international travel across ICON markets and to Revolution Medicines’ global offices.

Why Join Revolution Medicines

  • This is an opportunity to shape Revolution Medicines’ presence across a diverse and strategically important region. You will build a Corporate Affairs capability from the ground up, strengthen trusted partnerships, influence healthcare policy and help create the conditions for innovative precision medicines to reach patients with significant unmet medical needs.

  • Revolution Medicines is an equal opportunity employer committed to building an inclusive workplace where diverse perspectives drive innovation and improve outcomes for patients worldwide.

Revolution Medicines takes protection and security of personal data very seriously and respects your right to privacy while using our website and when contacting us by email or phone. We will only collect, process and use any personal data that you provide to us in accordance with our CCPA Notice and Privacy Policy. For additional information, please contact privacy@revmed.com.

These scams may appear as false job advertisements or unsolicited contacts through communication or chat platforms, email, phone, or text message.

Please note that Revolution Medicines does not extend unsolicited employment offers and will never ask candidates to provide financial information, purchase equipment, or pay fees as part of the hiring process. title: Program Supervisor
description:
The Program Supervisor - HS is the DFPS-approved Child Placement Management Staff (CPMS) responsible for day-to-day oversight of home studies and reports. The Program Supervisor assigns referrals, supervises Assessors (Service Providers), and reviews and approves every FAD Home Screening, KCHA, and HSEGH Report before it goes to DFPS. The Program Supervisor may also complete studies, but may never approve their own work; another CPMS must review and approve it. The Program Supervisor reports to the Program Director.


ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:

  • Assignment and Supervision:
    • Assign each referral within four hours of logging, based on coverage, caseload, availability, language needs, and conflicts of interest, with expedited referrals first.
    • Supervise Assessors through regular case consultation and staffing. For an Assessor qualifying through supervised experience, hold and document 10 monthly, face-to-face, individual, case-related conferences per year.
    • Review ExtendedReach alerts daily for contacts nearing or past 24 hours, cases with no activity for 48 hours, and missing documents, and act before deadlines are missed.
    • Make the decisions and send the notices for referral returns, withdrawals, and rescheduling within DFPS contract timeframes, including Form 2700 and the Withdrawal Report (Form 5520) within three business days of a withdrawal.
    • Direct the Intake Coordinator's daily work and resolve intake questions the same day.
  • Review and Approval:
    • Review and approve every home study and report before it is delivered to DFPS, signing and dating the approval. Confirm that it is complete, clear, concise, accurate, and free of errors; addresses every concern in the referral and any earlier study; shows with specific wording that each required standard is met; and identifies each person's relationship to everyone else named.
    • Confirm that each study follows the current DFPS form and instructions, including the rules on what must never be written: criminal history record information or its source, firearm details, Social Security numbers, and, in HSEGH Reports, identifying information about anyone other than the child.
    • Complete home studies and reports as needed, with another CPMS approving them.
  • Quality, Court, and Compliance:
    • Track reasons DFPS returns studies and coach Assessors to correct patterns; bring trends to the Program Director's monthly review.
    • Participate in court-related services, including testimony and depositions, when DFPS authorizes them on Form 2054, and complete Form 2057.
    • Confirm that supervised staff are DFPS-approved, background-cleared, and trained before they accept referrals.
    • Report suspected abuse, neglect, or exploitation to the Texas Abuse Hotline personally, and support staff who make reports.
  • Other tasks and responsibilities as assigned by supervisors.


SKILLS & ABILITIES:

  • Supervising staff and giving clear, constructive feedback on written work.
  • Working knowledge of the DFPS home study forms and instructions and 26 TAC Chapter 749.
  • Strong editing skills; able to spot gaps, unsupported conclusions, and prohibited content in a report.

title: Director, Administrative Operations Development
description:
HealthPartners is hiring a Director, Administrative Operations Development, to provide strategic and operational leadership for critical health plan administrative systems, with primary responsibility for our claims and prior authorization/referral platforms.

This is a highly collaborative and visible leadership opportunity for someone who enjoys connecting technology, business operations, and organizational strategy. The Director will lead a team responsible for supporting and advancing these applications from a business systems perspective, ensuring enhancements and modernization efforts are successfully implemented to meet evolving business priorities, regulatory requirements, and customer needs.

Collaborating closely with Claims Product Owners and leaders across IT, business operations, and data, the Director will maintain alignment around staffing, implementation status, and delivery of key initiatives. Near-term priorities include claims cost management implementations expected to generate significant savings over the next 18 months, making this position an important contributor to both operational performance and HealthPartners’ broader strategic goals.

The Director will oversee system development, software implementations, automation, analytics, operational process improvement, and ongoing maintenance associated with core administrative platforms and enabling technologies. Depending on assigned responsibilities, this work may span areas such as claims and prior authorizations/referrals, enrollment, billing, broker commissions, administrative documents and communications, and operational reporting.

Beyond day-to-day system leadership, the Director will contribute to long-range systems strategy and annual planning, department and project budget management, business continuity planning, and health plan data governance. The role will build and maintain strong partnerships across HealthPartners as well as with external technology and software vendors.

This position reports to the Senior Director, Administrative Operations Development and provides overall leadership and oversight for a department of 25+ staff, ranging from business systems analysts to leadership roles.

Required Qualifications:

  • Master’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Business Administration, Health Care Administration, or a related field.
  • Five (5) years of progressive experience in health plan operations, health care technology, software delivery, business systems analysis, program management, systems development, and/or agile product development. Experience within a health plan environment, particularly supporting claims administration, is strongly preferred.
  • Five (5) years of leadership experience, including responsibility for people leadership, cross-functional delivery, and operational and/or technology strategy.
  • Demonstrated success leading complex business, systems, or digital transformation initiatives from planning and implementation through operational adoption, including post-implementation performance measurement and monitoring.

  • Strong business, systems, and operational critical thinking skills, with the ability to navigate competing priorities, evaluate trade-offs, and make sound decisions within a complex, matrixed organization.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience leading large-scale administrative operations modernization, enterprise platform implementations, digital product delivery, or business transformation initiatives.
  • Experience applying advanced analytics, business intelligence, forecasting, process automation, artificial intelligence, data science, or pattern identification to improve operational performance and business outcomes.

  • Experience with tools and platforms supporting project management, issue tracking, release coordination, and operational analytics.
  • Experience with HealthPartners’ core claims administration system and key upstream and downstream systems that support claims operations.
  • Experience with vendor contracting and relationship management, including ongoing performance monitoring and evaluation of contract value against defined performance measures.
  • Relevant IT, project/program management, agile, or technology certifications.

  • M-F; core business hours
  • This position offers a hybrid work arrangement, with onsite work 4 days per week at our Bloomington corporate office. Additional onsite presence may be required based on meetings, workgroup sessions, or other business needs.

Pay within our ranges may also be determined by education, experience, knowledge, skills, location, and abilities as well as internal equity. Monitors delivery, removes barriers, manages risks, and holds self and others accountable for quality, timeliness, compliance, and financial stewardship.

Insider Threat Analysts triage data of anomalous events collected by User Activity Monitoring (UAM) Tools, and other data analytics tools and sources to decipher underlying trends or uncover anomalies and discern obscure patterns and attributes. title: Telecommunications Network Engineer
description:
Telecommunications Network Engineer

The Opportunity:

At Booz Allen, we power possibility for our clients facing their toughest challenges. Our cross-domain team of advisors, technologists, researchers, engineers, and cyber experts builds innovative solutions for the infrastructure and capabilities of tomorrow. We're trusted partners on our clients' most critical missions, and we bring expertise to the table, but it's our attitude, our courage, curiosity, and passion for tomorrow, that makes us unique.


We're seeking a Network Engineer to join a team that is building, integrating, and hardening next-generation telecommunications infrastructure that fuses carrier-grade networking with AI/ML acceleration. You'll work in a hands-on, fast-moving lab environment where systems need to be stood up, reconfigured, and troubleshot quickly, often on tight timelines ahead of demos, pilots, and government stakeholder reviews. You do not need prior cellular or open RAN experience to succeed here. We will teach the radio access side to a strong network engineer. What we need you to bring is deep Layer 2 and Layer 3 fundamentals, precision timing, Linux, and the discipline to document as you build. If you thrive when the pressure is on and enjoy tearing down and rebuilding systems until they work, we want to hear from you.


What You'll Work On:

  • Build, rack, cable, and configure the lab network stack including GPU-accelerated servers, enterprise switching, radio and antenna hardware, and supporting infrastructure.
  • Configure and validate precision timing distribution, including a PTP IEEE 1588 grandmaster with GPS or GNSS lock and SyncE, and verify the timing chain to downstream clients.
  • Design and implement VLAN segmentation for management, control, user, and timing traffic.
  • Configure QoS or CoS priority queuing for latency-sensitive, high-throughput flows.
  • Deploy and configure IP networking for all platform interfaces including transport and backhaul, device management, out-of-band server management, and Kubernetes cluster and pod networks.
  • Stand up and validate virtualized network functions on hypervisor VMs, including subscriber provisioning, routing, and policy configuration, and verify end-to-end connectivity.
  • Deploy and troubleshoot containerized network workloads on Kubernetes running on GPU-accelerated servers and validate interface connectivity between distributed components.
  • Provision and validate end-user devices and SIM or eSIM credentials and execute device connectivity, session establishment, and throughput validation such as iperf3.
  • Apply security hardening including CIS Level 1 baseline on Ubuntu, STIG checklists, NAC, and 802.1X configuration such as Aruba ClearPass, Cisco ISE, and TLS on management interfaces.
  • Write and maintain technical documentation, including Method of Procedure (MOP), Standard Operating Procedures (SOP), configuration guides, and troubleshooting guides, concurrently with lab work, not after the fact.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional engineering teams to translate mission requirements into working network configurations.

Join us. The world can't wait.


You Have:

  • 5+ years of experience with network engineering including telecommunications, defense systems, or enterprise networking
  • Experience configuring and troubleshooting Layer 2 and Layer 3 switching and routing including VLAN design, trunking, QoS policy configuration, and ACLs
  • Experience with Linux server administration including Ubuntu, RHEL, networking, SSH hardening, and log management
  • Experience with virtualization or containers such as VMware, Proxmox, KVM, Docker, or Kubernetes in a lab or production environment
  • Knowledge of IP networking fundamentals such as subnetting, routing, SCTP, UDP, TCP, DNS, and TLS
  • Ability to read and interpret packet captures such as Wireshark and tcpdump for protocol-level troubleshooting
  • Ability to work in a fast-paced lab environment with hard delivery deadlines and produce clear, accurate technical documentation under time pressure
  • Ability to triage and resolve issues independently without waiting for escalation
  • Ability to obtain a Secret clearance
  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or Telecommunications field and 4+ years of experience in network engineering, or 9+ years of experience in network engineering in lieu of a degree

Nice If You Have:

  • Experience with PTP/IEEE 1588 timing, including grandmaster, boundary clock, and client configuration, and with telecom timing profiles, such as ITU-T G.8275.1, and SyncE
  • Experience with 5G/O-RAN systems, including CU/DU/RU architecture, eCPRI fronthaul, O-RAN Split 7.2x, and the F1, E2, and O1 interfaces
  • Experience with O-RAN components such as O-RU, O-DU, O-CU, Near-RT RIC/Non-RT RIC, or xApp/rApp integration
  • Experience with SIM/eSIM provisioning tools and test UE validation such as iPhone and Android
  • Experience with NVIDIA GPU platforms, CUDA toolkit, or NVIDIA Container Toolkit in a server environment
  • Experience with network automation and infrastructure-as-code tools such as Ansible, Terraform, or NetBox
  • Experience with RF systems, including antenna installation, coax cabling, N-type/SMA connectors, spectrum analyzer use
  • Experience with DoD security frameworks, including DoD STIG, RMF, Nessus/ACAS scanning, CIS benchmarks
  • Knowledge of 5G core network functions, such as AMF, SMF, or UPF, including HPE Athonet, Ericsson, Nokia, open-source cores such as Open5GS, or equivalent, including PLMN, DNN, and network slicing S-NSSAI configuration
  • Cisco CCNP, Juniper JNCIP, or equivalent professional-level networking certification

title: Tradewell Fellowship - Healthcare Planning & Design
description:
Your Opportunity

At Stantec our Tradewell Fellowship is a one-year program in front-end Healthcare Planning and Design in one of our participating healthcare offices.

The Fellow will benefit from:

  • Accelerated immersive participation in the healthcare design practice
  • Exposure to the healthcare industry, our clients, consultants, and partners
  • Opportunities to explore healthcare design research questions in their area of interest
  • Attendance at a relevant conference of choice related to healthcare planning, design, and construction
  • Support and training offered by one year of employment at Stantec
  • Joining a dynamic, nurturing network of distinguished former Tradewell Fellows

As a Tradewell Fellow, you will have the unique opportunity to:

  • Work alongside senior healthcare planners and designers on a variety of healthcare projects, ranging from initial master planning efforts to design.
  • Create a body of work suitable for presentation and/or publication by the end of the year.
  • Build lasting connections in the field and enhance your career prospects.
  • Become a thought leader within the healthcare planning & design community.

Tradewell Fellows are full-time employees for the duration of the one-year fellowship. 85% of fellows have continued their career opportunities with the firm after the fellowship year

Your Responsibilities

We are currently seeking applications for our Tradewell Fellowship program beginning in Summer 2027. This is a one-year program in front-end Healthcare Planning and Design in one of our participating healthcare offices. The opportunity provides focused, fast-tracked exposure to collaborating with clients and thought leaders, positioning tomorrow’s healthcare planners and designers for rapid career advancement to design, build, and heal. The fellow is provided the opportunity to work with senior planners and designers on a variety of healthcare projects, ranging from initial master planning efforts to design, while gaining exclusive exposure to clients and consultants. Fellows also benefit from the unique experience and career guidance that comes from working with leaders in the healthcare industry and having access to in-house educational presentations and the network of past Tradewell Fellows. The ideal fellowship candidate is a dedicated professional who desires to be a lifelong learner and mentor to others in the healthcare architecture industry. To develop expertise in an area of their interest, the fellow will select a topic related to the design of healing spaces and create a body of work suitable for presentation and/or publication during their fellowship year. The fellowship includes employment with Stantec and attendance at a relevant conference of choice related to healthcare planning, design, and construction. The Tradewell Fellowship has produced many talented healthcare planners and designers, and this tradition is integral to Stantec's culture. Multiple Tradewell Fellowships may be awarded, based on merit, in separate participating healthcare office locations.

Education & Experience

At the commencement of the Tradewell Fellowship, the applicant must hold at least an NAAB, CACB, or NAAB substantially equivalent accredited first professional degree in Architecture.

Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the US for the contiguous 12-month period. The Tradewell Fellowship typically follows a June-to-June cycle. However, there is some flexibility for those who need to begin in May or July. Knowledge of Revit and 3D software is preferred. Effective communication, organization, and presentation skills and the ability to work in a fast-paced, challenging work environment are necessary. Prior internship experience is preferred.

Understanding LEED principles is a plus.

Application Timeline

Completed online application and all supporting materials must be received by midnight CST on Monday, January 11, 2027

Shortlisted candidates may be asked to participate in a brief video conference interview scheduled within 2 weeks. Applicants will be notified by mid-February.

Application Submission Requirements

Complete online application

Submit each file with your name and file name (Ex: YourName_DesignWork), maximum 10mb file size for each file.)

  • Resume (one page)
  • Statement of Intent/Purpose
    • In 35 words or less, describe how you see the Tradewell Fellowship impacting your journey in healthcare architecture.
  • Personal Essay
    • In one page or less, write about your general architecture and healthcare architecture accomplishments that have influenced your interest in healthcare design and explain why you would be a good fit for the Tradewell Fellowship.
  • Design Work
    • A compilation of images and text that represents your design work.
    • Showcase multiple projects.
    • Maximum of 10 pages of design content, no larger than 11”x17.”
    • Images may include (but are not limited to): models, presentation boards, freehand drawings, illustrations, computer drawings, photographs, renderings, etc. Design work must specify individual verses group projects and your role within the project.
  • Three (3) Reference Letters
    • Minimum of one (1) from an academic source is preferred.
    • One (1) professional reference is preferred.
    • Each letter should specify your qualifications for the Tradewell Fellowship.
    • These letters should be sent directly from your references, submitted via email to jennifer.kercull@stantec.com.

*Indicate your top 3 location preferences: Atlanta, Austin, California (Los Angeles, Sacramento, or San Francisco), Dallas, Denver, Houston, Los Angeles, Philadelphia, Washington D.C. Please only complete one application for the Tradewell Fellowship regardless of office location preferences*

Questions? Please get in touch with renee.fiala@stantec.com

This description is not a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities that may be required of the employee and other duties, responsibilities and activities may be assigned or may be changed at any time with or without notice.

About Stantec

Stantec is a global leader in sustainable engineering, architecture, and environmental consulting. The diverse perspectives of our partners and interested parties drive us to think beyond what’s previously been done on critical issues like climate change, digital transformation, and future-proofing our cities and infrastructure. We innovate at the intersection of community, creativity, and client relationships to advance communities everywhere, so that together we can redefine what’s possible.

title: Staff HIL Engineer
description:
At Relativity Space, we’re building rockets to serve today’s needs and tomorrow’s breakthroughs. Our Terran R vehicle will deliver customer payloads to orbit, meeting the growing demand for launch capacity. But that’s just the start. Achieving commercial success with Terran R will unlock new opportunities to advance science, exploration, and innovation, pioneering progress that reaches beyond the known.

Joining Relativity means becoming part of something where autonomy, ownership, and impact exist at every level. Here, you're not just executing tasks; you're solving problems that haven’t been solved before, helping develop a rocket, a factory, and a business from the ground up. Whether you’re in propulsion, manufacturing, software, avionics, or a corporate function, you’ll collaborate across teams, shape decisions, and see your work come to life in record time. Relativity is a place where creativity and technical rigor go hand in hand, and your voice will help define the stories we’re writing together. Now is a unique moment in time where it’s early enough to leave your mark on the product, the process, and the culture, but far enough along that Terran R is tangible and picking up momentum. The most meaningful work of your career is waiting. Join us.

About the Team:

The Interplanetary Sciences Program is building a philanthropically funded Mars science orbiter targeted to launch in 2028. You will build the integrated hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) test capability that allows the spacecraft team to test early, continuously, and with real hardware. Then carry that ownership into final spacecraft integration and test leading up to flight.

This is a hands-on integration and test role spanning hardware, software automation, and spacecraft-level validation. You will take the HITL environment from an empty rack to a running, automated, always-on validation system that proves our payloads, avionics, flight software, and interfaces work together as intended.

You will build the bench, the software fixturing that exercises flight software against real and representative hardware, and the CI and regression infrastructure that continuously checks the system as it evolves. You won't just execute test procedures—you'll understand what each test proves, why it matters, and whether the result is actually credible.

You will work shoulder to shoulder with engineers across the spacecraft. If you like owning a capability end to end, debugging across hardware and software boundaries, and being the reason the rest of the program can move quickly with confidence, this is that seat.


About the Role:

  • Design, build, and maintain the ISP HITL test environment end to end, including rack fabrication, avionics installation, breakout hardware, load emulation, harness fabrication and routing, and supporting test equipment.
  • Build the simulation, data-acquisition, and control infrastructure that drives stimulus into the system, captures results, and allows flight software to be exercised against real and representative spacecraft hardware.
  • Develop software fixturing, automated test frameworks, and CI/regression pipelines that validate every software change on hardware with automated pass/fail adjudication, regression detection, and clear failure reporting.
  • Debug integrated failures across flight software, avionics, interfaces, harnessing, timing, communications, and test infrastructure until root cause is understood and fed back to the responsible design teams.
  • Validate timing-sensitive behavior and interfaces across sensors, actuators, payloads, avionics, and communication buses, including longer-duration and soak testing where appropriate.
  • Establish dashboards, telemetry views, configuration control, and test procedures that make system health, test coverage, anomalies, and requirements traceability clear to the broader engineering team.
  • Drive final integration and test of flight hardware leading into launch, coordinating with subsystem responsible engineers to ensure hardware and software are designed for integration and test from the beginning.

About You:

  • Degree in computer, electrical, aerospace, or a related engineering field, or equivalent hands-on experience
  • 7+ years of experience in test engineering, including architecting automated test frameworks for integrated hardware, firmware, and software systems
  • Strong, current software skills for test automation, tooling, and validation pipelines
  • A track record of building test automation and CI/regression infrastructure from the ground up, including telemetry/logging, automated pass/fail, and continuous test execution
  • Hands-on hardware and embedded systems experience, including bench troubleshooting with standard electronics equipment and familiarity with interfaces such as Ethernet, UART, and SPI
  • Demonstrated ability to own a complex test capability end to end, drive integrated hardware/software failures to root cause, and coordinate effectively across engineering teams

Nice to haves but not required:

  • Experience standing up a test bench, HITL system, SIL/HIL environment, lab automation capability, or integrated test platform from scratch
  • Experience with spacecraft, launch vehicles, satellites, robotics, autonomous systems, aircraft, vehicles, medical devices, industrial equipment, or other high-reliability hardware
  • Hands-on experience with harnessing, cable fabrication, breakout boards, rack wiring, or test equipment setup
  • Experience helping establish test practices, tools, or team processes in a fast-moving engineering environment

Description

RSA SecurID Zero Trust & MFA

Leidos is seeking an experienced RSA SecurID-MFA Engineer to design, implement, and administer our enterprise Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) and Identity and Access Management (IAM) infrastructure. In this role, you will be responsible for managing both on-premises RSA Authentication Manager environments and expanding hybrid cloud components using RSA ID Plus. You will ensure high availability, secure user provisioning, seamless agent integration, and robust access governance across the organization.


Key Responsibilities

  • Administration & Operations: Administer, patch, and maintain RSA Authentication Manager (primary and replica instances), ensuring 99.99% availability for critical authentication services.
  • Identity Source Integration: Integrate and synchronize external identity sources (Active Directory, Azure AD/Entra ID, LDAP) with RSA Authentication Manager, managing user attribute mappings and group structures.
  • Authenticator & Token Lifecycle Management: Oversee the end-to-end lifecycle of hardware tokens, software tokens (SecurID Authenticator app), on-demand authentication (ODA), and modern risk-based or FIDO-based authentication methods.
  • Agent & RADIUS Configuration: Configure and support authentication agents, RADIUS clients, and REST APIs to secure VPNs, virtual desktop infrastructures (VDI), cloud applications, and network entry points.
  • Monitoring & Troubleshooting: Monitor system telemetry, audit logs, and security consoles. Troubleshoot authentication failures, replication lags, and agent connectivity issues promptly.
  • Compliance & Auditing: Generate regular administrative, user event, and agent inventory reports to support internal security audits and compliance frameworks (SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA).
  • Upgrade & Migration Support: Assist in planning and executing architecture upgrades, security hardening, and potential migration paths toward cloud-based ID Plus services.

Required Qualifications & Competencies

  • Bachelor’s degree in a related area with 8+ years of experience or a Master’s degree with 6+ years of experience. Additional experience may be considered in lieu of a degree.
  • Active TS/SCI security clearance.
  • 5+ years of hands-on experience in Information Security focusing on Enterprise Identity and Access Management (IAM) and Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA).
  • Core Technical Expertise:
    • Deep operational knowledge of RSA Authentication Manager (v8.x / v9.x) administration, maintenance, and backup/restore workflows.
    • Familiarity with RSA ID Plus and cloud/hybrid authentication models.
    • Strong understanding of directory services (Active Directory, LDAP) and network authentication protocols (RADIUS, TACACS+, SAML, OIDC).
  • Certifications (Preferred):
    • RSA SecurID Certified Administrator or RSA ID Plus Certified Administrator.
    • Active IAT or IAM Level II/III DoD approved 8570 baseline certifications, such as CISSP, CompTIA Security+, or relevant IAM vendor credentials are a plus.

Soft Skills: Strong analytical and troubleshooting mindset, excellent documentation capabilities, and the ability to collaborate across IT, Help Desk, and Security Operations teams.

title: Software Engineer II (Java) - Issuing
description:
This is Adyen

Adyen provides payments, data, and financial products in a single solution for customers like Meta, Uber, H&M, and Microsoft - making us the financial technology platform of choice. At Adyen, everything we do is engineered for ambition.

For our teams, we create an environment with opportunities for our people to succeed, backed by the culture and support to ensure they are enabled to truly own their careers. We are motivated individuals who tackle unique technical challenges at scale and solve them as a team. Together, we deliver innovative and ethical solutions that help businesses achieve their ambitions faster.

Senior Software Engineer, Issuing Team

The Adyen Issuing product is an API-driven product for generating physical and virtual payment cards for business use cases. This enables our customers to benefit from the features of Mastercard and Visa cards such as interchange kickbacks, chargebacks, intelligent transaction declines, etc. B2B card transactions can be a safer and much cheaper alternative to bank or wire transfers.

The Chicago Issuing team is currently building a best-in-class dispute case management api. This is particularly interesting to our online travel agency customers who are exposed to risks of airlines and hotels going bankrupt between booking time and services rendered. By using Adyen issued cards, the travel agency can reverse a transaction by raising a dispute via the API. Additionally, as Adyen explores more credit-driven products, the case management API will serve as the main gateway for initiating automated fraud procedures related to charge cards and other financial products.

We are building a deceptively simple api that is scheme agnostic, and that hides the huge complexity of getting money back into our customers account. The issuing product has entered a phase of hyper-growth, and many new backend systems are currently being built to accommodate the 100x growth expected over the near term.

What you’ll do:

  • Work on complex technical projects from requirements analysis through design, implementation, testing and launch into production.
  • Bring your own point of view on best engineering practices.
  • Be hands-on and contribute to the implementation. Identify and improve parts of the platform to make it more robust and scalable.
  • Your code will be used at scale and you are expected to think in that mindset when building features.
  • We launch fast and iterate often. Concretely, this means that within your first few weeks, you will bring live functionalities that impact many merchants and shoppers.
  • Build APIs and tooling according to quality principles such as performance and code quality.
  • Collaborate across teams and time zones to get projects over the finish line.

Who you are:

  • You enjoy seeing the big picture and understanding how your code impacts the business
  • You have experience with Java, Web Services, REST APIs, SQL/PostgreSql, and experience with Kafka and Elasticsearch is a plus
  • You have a good understanding of Software Engineering practices and interest in product knowledge
  • You are familiar with complex large scale distributed systems
  • You value involving other people to hear different perspectives
  • Added bonus: if you have worked in customer developer experience (e.g. tooling, observability) or payment related teams in the past

Minimum qualifications:

  • 5+ years of experience in the software development industry
  • Full professional proficiency in English
  • This role is based out of our Chicago office. We are an office-first company and value in-person collaboration; we do not offer remote-only roles.

Total rewards & compensation

The annual base salary range for this role is $154,000 - $200,000. Compensation is based on factors including qualifications, experience, and location. Total compensation package includes equity (RSUs), 401(k), health, dental, vision, and more.

In-office expectations

This role is based in our Chicago office. We're an office-first company and expect employees to work in-office at least 3 days a week on average. This approach helps strike a balance between bringing people together for in-person collaboration and learning from each other, while also supporting flexibility.

We actively seek different perspectives to sharpen our ideas. Our unique culture is a product of our diverse backgrounds and experiences. No matter who you are or where you’re from, you’re welcome to be your true self at Adyen.

title: Scientist L1 - Metabolic Engineering
description:
About CycloKinetics

CycloKinetics is advancing the next generation of high-performance propellants for aerospace and defense. Our highly innovative technology allows us to harness existing energy from biomass and convert it to superior performance fuels and propellants across aviation, aerospace, and defense applications.

We are a team of engineers, scientists, and operators driven by performance, innovation, and national security impact focused on building scalable, domestic energy solutions that power the future of propulsion. CycloKinetics is based in Salt Lake City, Utah.

Job Summary

CycloKinetics is seeking a Scientist L1 to independently design, build, and test engineered microbial strains with improved titer, rate, yield, and robustness. Working independently within strategic direction set by the project lead, the Scientist I will own strain engineering projects from hypothesis through data interpretation, and will translate results into the next round of designs. The Scientist L1 will work closely with the analytical chemistry and fermentation groups to move strains from the bench toward scale-up.

Essential Functions & Responsibilities

  • Independently plan and execute design-build-test-learn (DBTL) cycles to improve strain titer, rate, yield, robustness, and other performance metrics.
  • Identify genetic targets (gene overexpression, deletion, downregulation, enzyme variants, promoter tuning) using literature, pathway analysis, and prior strain data.
  • Design and build DNA constructs and genome edits in microbial strains using advanced gene editing techniques, homologous recombination, and modular cloning methods.
  • Construct, verify (colony PCR, sequencing), and bank engineered strains; maintain an accurate strain and plasmid inventory.
  • Apply sound experimental design and statistics to screen strains in small-scale cultivations (plates, tubes, shake flasks) and help translate these results to bench-scale bioreactors with the fermentation team.
  • Quantify products, byproducts, and substrates using HPLC, GC, or GC-MS, in collaboration with analytical chemistry.
  • Troubleshoot strain performance issues such as growth defects, genetic instability, and precursor or cofactor imbalance.
  • Present results, interpretations, and proposed next steps at project meetings; write technical reports and contribute to patent disclosures and grant reports.
  • Provide technical guidance to junior colleagues and develop and maintain SOPs.
  • Keep complete, timely laboratory notebook and data records according to company guidelines.
  • Accurately record work hours by project, as required for federally funded research.
  • Must be able to function within a team environment.
  • Support daily R&D processes involving the handling, preparation, and management of various chemical substances using the appropriate Personal Protective Equipment (PPE).
  • Safely handle, measure, mix, and transport chemical substances in accordance with established procedures using appropriate PPE.
  • Perform additional duties as assigned.

Education & Experience

  • A Ph.D. in Metabolic Engineering, Chemical/Biological Engineering, Microbiology, Molecular Biology, Biochemistry, or a related field, with 0–3 years of post-graduate experience (postdoctoral or industry).
    • A Master's degree in a closely related field with at least 4-8 years of post-graduate laboratory experience, preferably in industry, will also be considered.
    • A Bachelor's degree in a related field with at least 10 years of post-graduate laboratory experience, preferably in industry, will also be considered.

Requirements

  • Demonstrated hands-on experience engineering microbial strains, with yeast strongly preferred, including genome editing and plasmid or integration construct design.
  • Strong molecular biology skills: PCR, cloning and DNA assembly, transformation, sequence verification, and aseptic technique.
  • Ability to independently plan and execute hypothesis-driven experiments, analyze quantitative data, and translate results into strain improvement strategies.
  • Experience with shake-flask and bench-scale bioreactor (fed-batch) cultivation.
  • Demonstrated experience in improving flux through metabolic pathways is strongly preferred.
  • Familiarity with high-throughput screening, laboratory automation, or omics data (RNA-seq, proteomics, metabolomics).
  • Proficiency with DNA design software (e.g., SnapGene, Benchling) and data analysis tools (e.g., Excel, Python, R, or JMP).
  • Evidence of independent scientific contribution is strongly preferred via first-author publications, patents, or equivalent industry results.
  • Clear written and verbal communication skills, good record keeping, and a strong commitment to safety.

Physical Demands

Physical requirements may include lifting and/or moving items weighing up to fifty (50) pounds, bending, standing, reaching, climbing, walking, and prolonged sitting may be required. Must have safe work habits and perform all duties in accordance with company safety policies. Personal protective equipment is provided by the company, and its use is mandatory.

This position is based in Salt Lake City, Utah, with work performed on-site. CycloKinetics is an At-Will, VEVRAA, Equal Employment Opportunity Employer, E-Verify, and Drug Free Workplace. Employment is contingent upon successful completion of a background verification and drug screens.
