Competition Close Date: Sunday, January 31, 2027 at 11:59 pm PCT

Salary Range: $2,567.19 bi-weekly + 8% vacation pay

Job Description: JOB DESCRIPTION PDF


Job Summary

Employees of the Legislative Assembly of British Columbia (Assembly) provide professional non-partisan services to support the democratic institution of Parliament and its members through procedural advice, administrative support and information services. The Assembly is an autonomous employer, separate from the administrative framework of B.C. government ministries and agencies.


Established in 1976, the B.C. Legislative Internship Program (BCLIP) is a six-month program that gives post-secondary graduates exposure to public policy-making and legislative processes in British Columbia.


Reporting to the Parliamentary Education Officer (B.C. Legislative Internship Program Manager), the B.C. Legislative Intern provides research, analysis, and communications support during their placements in a provincial ministry or statutory office and in an officially recognized political party caucus. Interns are responsible for one or more educational projects during the program, including project management, research, and analysis, designing, and writing communication materials, and developing and implementing educational events. They represent the program with staff and executives within the B.C. public service and during both national and international exchanges. BCLIP is advised by an Academic Director and an Academic Steering Committee.


Program Components
The program begins in early-January each year and runs for approximately six months (25 weeks) until the end of June. A typical program year features the following training, educational and work opportunities. The timing and length of various program components can vary somewhat year-to-year.

  • Two weeks of intensive orientation and training – one in January and one in February.
  • A four-week placement in a ministry or statutory office under the direction of an assigned mentor. All placements are based in Victoria.
  • A placement in a political party caucus at the Legislative Assembly of British Columbia. This placement typically aligns with the Legislative Assembly’s spring session dates.
  • A one-week placement in an MLA’s constituency office.
  • Academic and topical seminars and bi-weekly debrief meetings.
  • In-person or virtual educational exchanges with other internships programs, including the Washington State Legislative Internship Program and the federal Parliamentary Internship Program.
  • A range of educational and leadership opportunities, including Model Parliament and Mock Trial exercises, K-12 student engagement projects, an optional research paper or Canadian Parliamentary Review submission, and the publication of the intern newsletter – the B.C. Legislative Internship Gazette.


Qualifications

Applicants must be/have:

  • Undergraduate degree in any discipline that was fully or partially completed at a Canadian post-secondary institution. (All degree requirements must have been completed within the immediate two-year period prior to the start of the program in January 2028)
  • Experience developing written and oral communication materials, conducting research and analysis, and contributing to and leading projects or project components within a team setting.


Please refer to the job description for a full list of duties and qualifications.


HOW TO APPLY

Follow this link to the 2028 B.C. Legislative Internship Program Application

  • Please reach out to BCLIP@leg.bc.ca for questions about the program or the application process.


Who We Are

Our values ground our work and reflect the beliefs and principles that are important to how we work with others.

  • Impartiality – We are non-partisan and objective in the performance of our duties.
  • Integrity – We build trust through responsible actions and respectful relationships.
  • Openness – We provide a welcoming and inclusive environment and promote public access and engagement.
  • Respect – We work together collaboratively with mutual respect, trust, and kindness.
  • Stewardship – We ensure institutional continuity and renewal.


Learn about the Legislative Assembly and what we do by watching this video!


What We Offer

  • Career development – We support continuing education by providing innovative, inclusive and diverse learning opportunities for growth, skill development and career advancement.
  • Community, engagement and recognition – We value teamwork, collaboration and connection. Employees have the opportunity to interact and engage through projects, committees, working groups and events. Together, we celebrate and acknowledge each other's outstanding achievements and contributions.
  • Extended health benefits – We provide eligible employees with a competitive benefits package, which includes extended health and dental, basic life insurance, an optional family funeral benefit plan, optional life insurance, optional accidental death and dismemberment, travel medical insurance, and short-term and long-term disability benefits. We also offer a Health Care Spending Account to help cover eligible additional medical expenses that are not covered by the extended health care package.
  • Work-life balance - We have a collaborative and team-oriented culture where onsite presence is required for all positions. We have 35-hour work weeks, and offer flexible work arrangements, including modified work weeks (flex days) and hybrid work schedules (onsite/remote) to eligible positions. Management employees are eligible for Time Off in Lieu, which is an additional 12 days off per year for time worked in excess of the regular hours required for their position.
  • Health and wellness – We promote employee health and wellness by providing access to an employee assistance program, an in-house fitness room, secure bike storage and a reduced-cost bus pass. We also offer an infant and family wellness room, a meditation room and a sustainable commuting and active living program that provides reimbursement for fitness and wellness activities.
  • Location, location, location — We provide employment in an architectural landmark, the Parliament Buildings, which overlooks Victoria's Inner Harbour on the edge of the downtown core, close to shops, restaurants, cafes and parks.
  • Retirement benefits – We offer a generous pension plan with the Public Service Pension Plan where contributions are made by both the employee and Legislative Assembly. This pension plan provides employees with a lifetime monthly pension when they retire.
  • Vacation benefits– We offer four weeks of annual vacation time to start, or 8 percent vacation pay.

For more information about our organization, go to:


Note

The Legislative Assembly of British Columbia is an equal opportunity employer committed to establishing an inclusive, equitable, and accessible environment for all. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, national origin, age, religion, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, marital status or any other basis protected by applicable law. We encourage applications from members of communities that are disadvantaged on any grounds under the B.C. Human Rights Code, including Indigenous Peoples, people of colour, people of all genders and sexualities and people with disabilities.


We are committed to ensuring that reasonable accommodations are made available to persons with disabilities during the recruitment, assessment, and selection processes. Applicants requiring reasonable accommodation at any point in the application or interview process, please contact human.resources@leg.bc.ca.


The Legislative Assembly Administration is a non-partisan workforce where political neutrality and impartiality is paramount. Employees must perform their duties in a non-partisan manner and manage their private affairs in a way that does not compromise or raise doubt about their ability to perform their job duties in a neutral and impartial way.


We would like to thank everyone in advance for applying as only those shortlisted will be contacted. An eligibility list may be established and/or auxiliary positions may be considered for future conversion to regular status. Lesser qualified applicants may be under-implemented or appointed at a lower classification. Reference checks and a Criminal Record Check (CRC) will be required as conditions of employment. An Education Verification Check may also be required.


All positions at the Legislative Assembly require applicants to be at least 16 years old and eligible to work in Canada.


The Legislative Assembly of British Columbia values diversity and is an equal opportunity employer.

title: [26-27] Reading Interventionist
description:
Summary

Midtown Community School (MCS) exists to foster a culture of belonging and academic excellence that supports the development of well-rounded individuals.


The Reading Interventionist provides targeted, structured literacy instruction for students who require additional support in reading development. Using evidence-based practices grounded in the Science of Reading, the interventionist delivers systematic and explicit instruction to accelerate student progress in foundational reading skills and comprehension. The role includes analyzing literacy data, implementing tiered interventions, and collaborating with teachers to strengthen literacy outcomes for all students.


For more information on Midtown Community School, please visit .


Responsibilities

Responsibilities will include, but are not limited to:

Instruction and Intervention

  • Deliver explicit, systematic reading instruction aligned with the Science of Reading and structured literacy practices.
  • Provide targeted Tier 2 and Tier 3 interventions to students identified through literacy screening and assessment data.
  • Teach and reinforce the essential components of reading, including:
    • Phonemic awareness
    • Phonics and decoding
    • Fluency
  • Vocabulary
  • Language comprehension
  • Use research-based instructional routines that include modeling, guided practice, and immediate feedback.
  • Differentiate instruction to meet the specific needs of struggling readers.

Assessment and Data Analysis

  • Administer universal screeners, diagnostic assessments, and progress monitoring tools.
  • Analyze literacy data to identify skill gaps and plan targeted interventions.
  • Monitor student progress frequently and adjust instruction based on data.
  • Maintain accurate documentation of interventions, progress monitoring, and student outcomes.

MTSS/RTI Collaboration

  • Work collaboratively with classroom teachers within the MTSS/RTI framework to support struggling readers.
  • Participate in problem-solving meetings and intervention planning.
  • Support teachers in implementing evidence-based literacy strategies in the classroom.

Instructional Support

  • Model effective literacy instruction and structured literacy strategies when appropriate.
  • Support the alignment of classroom instruction with intervention practices to ensure coherence for students.

Family Communication

  • Communicate student progress and provide families with strategies to support reading development at home when appropriate.

Professional Responsibilities

  • Stay current on research and best practices related to the Science of Reading and structured literacy.
  • Participate in professional learning focused on literacy instruction and intervention.
  • Contribute to school-wide literacy improvement efforts.


Qualifications & Traits

The ideal Reading Interventionist will have:

Required

  • Bachelor’s degree in Education, Literacy, or related field
  • Valid teaching certification
  • Demonstrated knowledge of the Science of Reading and evidence-based literacy instruction

Preferred

  • Master’s degree in Reading/Literacy or related field
  • Reading Specialist endorsement or certification
  • Training in structured literacy approaches (e.g., Orton-Gillingham, LETRS, or similar)
  • Experience providing reading interventions in an MTSS or RTI framework


Compensation & Benefits

This role is placed on the “A: Entry,” “B: Bachelor’s,” “M: Master’s,” or “D: Doctorate/Ed.S.” as appropriate.

MCS offers competitive salaries commensurate with experience and a comprehensive benefits package. MCS is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, or veteran status.

title: Zero Trust Enterprise Architect
description:
Zero Trust Enterprise Architect

The Opportunity:

A well-designed, secure network is critical to enabling the Department of Defense (DoD) to accomplish its mission. As a Zero Trust Enterprise Architect, you will play a key role in ensuring that enterprise and mission systems are resilient, scalable, and aligned with evolving operational and security needs. This role requires a blend of deep technical expertise, strategic planning, and hands-on implementation to design and maintain secure network architectures across complex environments.

You will collaborate with subject matter experts, customers, vendors, and end users to understand strategic objectives and operational requirements, translating them into robust network and security solutions. Leveraging your expertise, you will support the full lifecycle of network systems, including planning, acquisition, design, installation, configuration, testing, and maintenance of hardware and software components. As a Zero Trust Enterprise Architect, you will lead the design, integration, and operationalization of Zero Trust architectures aligned with DoD Zero Trust strategy and reference architecture.

This is an opportunity to work at the forefront of network engineering and cybersecurity, combining backbone networking, cloud technologies, and Zero Trust principles to support critical defense operations while continuously expanding your technical skill set.

Join us. The world can’t wait.


You Have:

  • 8+ years of experience in network engineering and cybersecurity within DoD or federal environments
  • 2+ years of experience designing, deploying, and supporting network and security architectures, including Zero Trust implementation
  • Experience architecting and implementing Zero Trust solutions aligned with DoD Zero Trust strategy and target-level frameworks
  • Experience documenting complex architectures, supporting defense programs, and delivering secure, scalable solutions
  • Experience in Identity and Access Management, micro-segmentation, endpoint security, and secure network or cloud architecture
  • Experience working within classified environments
  • Knowledge of DoD security standards, RMF or ATO processes, and compliance frameworks
  • Ability to travel up to 25% of the time
  • Top Secret clearance
  • HS diploma or GED

Nice If You Have:

  • Experience supporting and operating DoD networks in mission or tactical environments, including INDOPACOM or Pacific-based operations
  • Experience transitioning legacy perimeter-based architectures to Zero Trust models
  • Experience with multivendor network and security platforms such as Palo Alto, Cisco, Juniper, Dell, HPE, and VMware
  • Experience with commercial and DoD cloud environments and cloud security architecture
  • Experience applying STIGs and performing system hardening
  • Experience with Zero Trust Network Access (ZTNA)
  • Knowledge of automation, orchestration, and policy-as-code security enforcement
  • CISSP, CISM, CRISC, CCSP, or CCNA Certifications

Clearance:

Applicants selected will be subject to a security investigation and may need to meet eligibility requirements for access to classified information; Top Secret clearance is required.

title: O&M Shift Leader - Dublin
description:
Company Description

Welcome to Kanadevia Inova, a global innovation leader in the waste infrastructure space, where we believe in creating a sustainable future through technology and innovation.

Transforming Waste into Value

At Kanadevia Inova, we pride ourselves on being at the forefront of waste-to-X technology. We are not just waste managers; we are creators of value from what communities discard. Your role at Kanadevia Inova directly contributes to turning something once considered useless - waste - into something invaluable: energy, heat, hydrogen, fertilizer, and beyond..

Find out more about Kanadevia Inova at www.kanadevia-inova.com.

Job Description

Kanadevia Inova is hiring an O&M Shift Leader for our Dublin Waste to Energy Facility, located on the Poolbeg peninsula in Dublin, Ireland.

As an O&M Shift Leader, you will be responsible for the safe and efficient operation of the Energy-from-Waste facility during your assigned shift, ensuring the plant continues to operate in accordance with HSEQ requirements, Irish environmental regulations, production targets and contractual obligations.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead and manage the assigned operating shift, providing direct supervision and clear direction to Operators and other support personnel to ensure the continued safe, reliable and efficient operation of all plant processes, systems and equipment. Act as the senior management representative during nights, weekends and holidays when senior management is not on site, taking appropriate operational decisions and escalating issues where required.

Lead regular safety meetings, reinforce safe working practices, maintain high standards of housekeeping and ensure the plant remains a safe, clean and orderly working environment.
  • Ensure operational procedures, training and emergency arrangements are effectively maintained, ensuring Operators are appropriately trained and competent for their roles and follow established procedures during normal and emergency situations. Monitor plant performance, understand equipment interlocks, alarms, trips and control loops, and respond quickly and effectively to operational issues and emergencies using sound judgement.
  • Maintain effective operational control and reporting, ensuring daily shift logs, operator logs, system check sheets and other operational records are completed accurately and promptly. Prepare comprehensive event-based reports when required, raise maintenance work requests where plant or equipment requires attention, and ensure relevant operational issues are communicated effectively to the wider O&M and management teams.
  • Lead, develop and support the shift team, providing clear instructions, coaching and technical guidance while promoting teamwork, accountability and continuous improvement. Conduct performance reviews for Operators, provide regular feedback on development and performance, support HSE inspections, audits and assessments, and contribute to the ongoing improvement of plant operations and team capability.

This posting reflects the main responsibilities and requirements of the role and is not intended to be an exhaustive list. Additional responsibilities may be discussed during the recruitment process and may vary depending on the specific needs of the business.

Qualifications

  • Relevant engineering or technical qualification, with a Bachelor’s Degree in Engineering desirable but not essential where significant relevant operational experience is demonstrated.
  • Minimum five years’ experience in an Energy-from-Waste, power generation or similar industrial plant environment, with proven knowledge of power plant equipment, systems and processes. Experience in mass-burn, waste-fired or fossil-fuel plant environments would be advantageous.
  • Previous experience in a Shift Leader, Shift Team Leader or senior operational position, ideally with two to three years' experience at Shift Leader level, with responsibility for leading operators and maintaining safe and reliable plant operation.
  • Strong practical understanding of plant operations, equipment interlocks, alarms, trips and control loops, together with the ability to diagnose operational problems, identify root causes and make sound, timely decisions during both routine operations and emergency situations.
  • Demonstrable leadership, communication and people-management skills, with the ability to motivate and develop a team, provide clear instruction, manage conflict, work effectively under pressure and build constructive relationships. Fluent English and a strong understanding of HSEQ standards, procedures and requirements are essential.

Additional Information

  • Competitive benefits package, including a company pension life assurance, private medical to support your health and wellbeing.
  • A collaborative, team-oriented working environment within a global Green Tech organisation.
  • The opportunity to contribute to innovative and sustainable energy solutions while developing your career with an international industry leader.

title: Senior Systems Engineer – Mission Engineering, Modeling & Simulation
description:
Description

Leidos's Digital is seeking a Senior Systems Engineer – Mission Engineering, Modeling & Simulation.

The Senior Systems Engineer will support the U.S. Coast Guard CG-TECH-DME organization in executing enterprise digital transformation, digital engineering, and mission engineering (ME) initiatives supporting Force Design 2028 objectives. The role provides technical leadership in mission engineering, model-based systems engineering (MBSE), and mission-level modeling and simulation (M&S), applying the methodology of the DoW Mission Engineering Guide (MEG) v2.0 and the digital engineering practices established in DoW Instruction 5000.97 to Coast Guard missions. The Unified Architecture Framework (UAF) and its modeling language, UAFML, together with SysML, are the primary languages for this position: the Senior Systems Engineer will characterize missions, develop digital mission architectures composed of mission threads and mission engineering threads in UAF, and execute threat-informed, quantitative analyses to evaluate operational concepts, assess capability gaps and candidate solutions, inform acquisition, modernization, and resourcing decisions, and quantify mission effectiveness across Coast Guard mission systems, platforms, and systems of systems. This individual will work closely with Coast Guard leadership, requirements owners, operational planners, program managers, enterprise architects, operations analysts, developers, cybersecurity teams, and mission stakeholders.


Primary Responsibilities

  • Lead and support mission engineering studies following the MEG v2.0 methodology: define the mission problem statement, characterize the mission (scenario, vignettes, threats, environment, assumptions, and constraints), and scope each analysis to the acquisition, modernization, or resourcing decision it is intended to inform.
  • Develop and maintain digital mission architectures in UAF/UAFML, including mission threads (MTs) that capture the end-to-end sequence of operational activities and mission engineering threads (METs) that allocate systems, platforms, organizations, and information exchanges to those activities, as baseline and alternative mission architectures.
  • Apply the UAF grid across the Strategic, Operational, Services, Resources, Personnel, Security, Projects, and Standards domains to produce coherent, traceable views from capability and mission objectives through operational activities to resource and system realization, and generate DoDAF-conformant views from the UAF model where required by DHS, DoW, or Joint stakeholders.
  • Define mission metrics, including measures of effectiveness (MOEs), measures of performance (MOPs), and measures of suitability (MOSs), and maintain traceability from desired mission outcomes through UAF capabilities and operational activities to SysML system requirements and design parameters.
  • Build and maintain enterprise, mission, and system architecture models in CATIA Magic / Cameo (Enterprise Architecture and Systems Modeler) using UAFML and SysML, including model organization, profiles and customizations, validation suites, model queries and reports, and trade studies, and support transition planning toward SysML v2.
  • Develop and execute mission-level modeling and simulation using tools such as AFSIM, MATLAB/Simulink, or Ansys STK to assess baseline and alternative mission architectures, quantify capability gaps, and compare candidate materiel and non-materiel solutions against mission metrics.
  • Connect UAF/SysML architecture models, engineering analyses, and operational simulations into an authoritative, integrated analytical environment (digital thread) supporting decision-making across the lifecycle, and verify, validate, and document models and simulations (VV&A) in accordance with DoW M&S policy so results can be relied upon for decisions of record.
  • Develop mission engineering and systems engineering products, including mission problem statements, mission characterization, UAF mission architecture views, analysis plans, study reports, findings and recommendations briefs, CONOPS, requirements documentation, and interface definitions.
  • Support structured, iterative experimentation, prototyping, and wargaming activities that use mission engineering analysis to refine capability requirements and evaluate Coast Guard, partner, and industry solutions against priority operational problems, consistent with the DoW Mission Engineering and Integration Activity (MEIA) model.
  • Support alignment and interoperability of Coast Guard mission architectures with DHS, DoW, Joint, and partner architectures, including joint kill-chain and kill-web constructs and maritime domain awareness, where Coast Guard missions intersect with joint operations.
  • Establish and maintain UAF modeling standards, style guides, model governance, and configuration management practices for the Coast Guard digital engineering ecosystem, and coordinate with cloud, cybersecurity, and data teams on secure, scalable model and simulation environments.
  • Present model- and simulation-derived findings to technical and non-technical audiences in governance boards, mission reviews, technical reviews, and program briefings.
  • Support technical roadmaps, mission engineering and digital engineering ecosystem strategies, and implementation plans; monitor risks, dependencies, and integration impacts; and contribute to continuous improvement and workforce competency development.

Basic Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Systems Engineering, Engineering, Computer Science, Operations Research, or related discipline and 8–10 years of related experience, or 6–10 years with a Master’s degree. Additional experience may be considered in lieu of a degree.
  • Demonstrated experience developing enterprise and mission architectures in UAF/UAFML (UAF 1.2 or later) in Cameo Enterprise Architecture or CATIA Magic, including multi-domain traceability across the UAF grid and integration with SysML system models.
  • Demonstrated experience conducting or directly supporting mission engineering studies, including mission characterization, mission thread and mission engineering thread development, mission metric definition, and analysis of alternative mission architectures.
  • Working knowledge of the DoW Mission Engineering Guide v2.0, DoWI 5000.88 (Engineering of Defense Systems), and DoWI 5000.97 (Digital Engineering), and their application to acquisition and capability development decisions.
  • Modeling and simulation experience using tools such as AFSIM, MATLAB/Simulink, or Ansys STK, including scenario development, execution, and analysis of results.
  • OMG Certified Systems Modeling Professional (OCSMP) Model Builder.
  • Experience supporting complex federal IT, systems engineering, or modernization programs, and familiarity with systems engineering lifecycle and requirements management practices.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • U.S. Citizenship required; ability to obtain and maintain a DHS Public Trust.

Preferred Qualifications

  • OMG Certified UAF Professional (OCUP or UAF certification) and experience with DoWAF-to-UAF migration or DoWAF view generation from UAF models.
  • Experience integrating UAF/SysML mission architectures with AFSIM or Ansys STK scenarios to trace mission outcomes back to system requirements and design decisions.
  • Experience supporting OUSD(R&E) mission engineering activities, Service mission engineering organizations, or experimentation campaigns tied to Key Operational Problems or equivalent Service-level priority operational problems.
  • Familiarity with SysML v2, its API and services, and model interoperability approaches for integrating architecture models with analysis and simulation tools.
  • Proficiency in Python or MATLAB for simulation automation, model queries, and data analysis; familiarity with operations research methods (design of experiments, sensitivity analysis) and HLA/DIS or cloud-based simulation environments.
  • Experience supporting U.S. Coast Guard, DHS, or DoW mission engineering, wargaming, or analytical modeling and simulation programs.
  • INCOSE CSEP/ESEP, DAU or Service mission engineering coursework, or Ansys STK / AFSIM training.

Please be advised that during the interview, you will be required to keep your camera on, and your interviewer will be taking your picture for identification purposes if an offer letter is extended to you.

title: Tech Transfer Lead (Drug Substance)
description:
Candidates must currently reside in the Republic of Ireland and have a valid Stamp 4 VISA or European citizenship.


A biopharmaceutical company in Dublin is seeking a Tech Transfer Lead to lead the transfer of biologics drug substance manufacturing processes from process development or sending sites into GMP manufacturing, including internal sites and external manufacturing partners. The successful candidate will ensure robust technical transfer, process understanding and operational readiness for clinical and commercial production, working closely with Process Development, Manufacturing, Quality, Analytical, Supply Chain, Manufacturing Science and Technology, Regulatory and external manufacturing teams.


Responsibilities:

  • Lead end-to-end technology transfer activities for drug substance biologics processes, including cell culture, upstream, downstream operations and analytical methods.
  • Develop and execute transfer strategies, project plans, timelines, risk assessments, and readiness assessments.
  • Partner with process development teams to transfer process knowledge, critical process parameters, control strategy, and material attributes into manufacturing.
  • Coordinate creation, review, and approval of transfer documentation, including process descriptions, sample plans, bills of materials, protocols, reports, and technical summaries.
  • Lead cross-functional transfer teams and facilitate regular governance meetings to ensure alignment on scope, milestones, and risks.
  • Support process scale-up, characterisation, comparability, and process validation activities as required.
  • Ensure analytical methods, sampling plans, raw materials, equipment, and facility requirements are aligned to support successful transfer.
  • Identify technical and operational risks and drive mitigation plans to resolution.
  • Partner with Quality and Regulatory functions to ensure compliance with cGMP, internal procedures, and applicable regulatory expectations.
  • Support deviation investigations, change controls, and CAPA activities related to transfer execution.
  • Provide technical oversight during engineering batches, Process Performance Qualification (PPQ) or process verification campaigns.
  • Support training and knowledge transfer to manufacturing and quality teams at the receiving site.
  • Monitor post-transfer performance and lead continuous improvement initiatives to improve process robustness and transfer effectiveness.
  • Manage communication with internal, global and sending-site stakeholders to ensure accountability and timely issue resolution.


Qualifications & Experience:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Biology, Biochemistry, Chemical Engineering, Biotechnology, or related scientific/engineering discipline.
  • Typically 5–8+ years of experience in biologics process development, manufacturing science and technology, manufacturing, or technology transfer.
  • Strong understanding of drug substance manufacturing for biologics, including upstream and downstream processing.
  • Knowledge of cGMP regulations, process validation, and quality systems in a regulated biotech environment.
  • Ability to travel as needed to support site-to-site or partner transfers.
  • Experience with monoclonal antibodies, recombinant proteins, or other biologic modalities is desirable.
  • Experience with external manufacturing partners, contract manufacturing organisations (CMOs) or contract development and manufacturing organisations (CDMOs) is desirable.
  • Familiarity with process characterisation, scale-down models, and comparability assessments is desirable.
  • Experience supporting clinical and/or commercial tech transfers is desirable.
  • Project management experience or certification is desirable.

title: Electrical Team Leader
description:
Your Opportunity

At Stantec, we are on a mission to become the world's leading integrated design practice. Our architects, engineers, interior designers, consultants, sustainability specialists, and technologists are passionate about the power of design. Our collaborative culture and multidisciplinary approach enable us to deliver innovative solutions for projects of all sizes and complexities.

Stantec's Houston, TX office is seeking an experienced Electrical Team Leader to join our growing Buildings Engineering practice. This is an exciting opportunity for a highly motivated engineering professional to lead and develop a talented electrical team while contributing to the design and delivery of complex building projects.

As the Electrical Team Leader, you will oversee the electrical engineering team in Houston, providing technical leadership, managing workloads and resources, and supporting the professional development of engineers and designers. You will also serve as a senior technical resource on projects of varying scales and complexities, collaborating with multidisciplinary teams to deliver innovative, high-quality engineering solutions.

The ideal candidate is a collaborative leader, effective communicator, and skilled problem-solver with extensive experience in building electrical systems design. Experience supporting advanced manufacturing, healthcare, and data center projects is highly desirable.

Your Key Responsibilities

  • Serve as the Electrical Engineering Team Leader for the Houston office, overseeing team performance, workload planning, staffing assignments, and resource allocation.
  • Lead, mentor, and develop electrical engineers, designers, and production support staff, including conducting performance reviews and supporting professional growth.
  • Delegate work effectively to team members while maintaining project quality, efficiency, and accountability.
  • Provide technical leadership and engineering expertise on projects of varying size, scope, and complexity.
  • Develop project scopes, budgets, schedules, and design approaches in collaboration with project managers and multidisciplinary teams.
  • Manage engineering resources and project deliverables to support financial performance and schedule objectives.
  • Lead and oversee the design of electrical systems for commercial, institutional, industrial, and other complex building projects.
  • Perform field investigations, engineering analyses, and technical evaluations to develop solutions to complex design challenges.
  • Prepare and review basis-of-design narratives, engineering calculations, cost estimates, construction drawings, technical specifications, and related documentation.
  • Collaborate with architects, engineers, clients, building officials, contractors, and other project stakeholders throughout design and construction.
  • Coordinate with manufacturers and contractors to address technical challenges and develop practical, constructible solutions.
  • Support construction administration activities, including site observations, review of shop drawings and submittals, and responses to requests for information (RFIs).
  • Ensure engineering documents comply with applicable codes, client requirements, and Stantec quality standards.
  • Identify and resolve design conflicts, provide technical recommendations, and support continuous improvement in project delivery.
  • Perform quality control reviews and participate in multidisciplinary project peer reviews.
  • Support client relationships, technical presentations, and project pursuits as needed.
  • Occasional travel may be required, approximately 10%.

Your Capabilities and Credentials

  • Professional Engineer (PE) license in the State of Texas is required. Additional state licenses are considered an asset.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead, manage, and mentor electrical engineering teams in a consulting engineering environment.
  • Strong technical knowledge of building electrical systems, including power distribution, lighting, emergency power, and related infrastructure.
  • Advanced understanding and application of the National Electrical Code (NEC), applicable building and energy codes, and industry standards.
  • Proven ability to manage multiple projects, prioritize assignments, and coordinate technical resources to meet project schedules and budgets.
  • Thorough understanding of engineering design processes, construction documentation, specifications, and quality assurance procedures.
  • Ability to review and verify the accuracy, completeness, and technical quality of engineering work produced by others.
  • Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to develop practical solutions to complex engineering challenges.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to collaborate effectively with multidisciplinary teams, clients, and project stakeholders.
  • Ability to work independently while fostering a collaborative, team-oriented environment.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite, Autodesk Revit, and SKM PowerTools or comparable electrical engineering analysis software.
  • Experience with technical presentations, client interviews, and project pursuits is preferred.

Education and Experience

  • Bachelor's degree in electrical engineering; ABET-accredited degree preferred.
  • Minimum of 15 years of professional electrical engineering experience in building systems design, including experience with large-scale and technically complex projects.
  • Demonstrated experience leading engineering teams, mentoring technical staff, and overseeing multidisciplinary project delivery.
  • Experience in advanced manufacturing, healthcare, data centers, and/or mission-critical facilities is preferred.

This description is not a comprehensive listing of activities, duties, or responsibilities that may be required of the employee. Other duties, responsibilities, and activities may be assigned or changed at any time with or without notice.

title: Client Relationship Director
description:

We give you a world of potential

We are looking for a Client Relationship Director to lead our Edinburgh-based client management team within Issuer Services UK, a key area of Computershare responsible for supporting corporate clients through a broad portfolio of registry products and services. The team plays an important role in addressing clients’ stakeholder engagement, risk management and corporate governance needs.

A key focus of the role will be driving business growth, understanding market developments and positioning Computershare’s solutions to meet clients’ evolving needs. You will also play a pivotal role in developing strategic partnerships with larger clients through initiatives such as the Existing Client Programme.

The role offers an opportunity to work collaboratively with teams across Issuer Services and the wider business, contributing to regional and group strategies, enhancing client satisfaction and supporting business growth. You will help drive service excellence, respond to industry changes and develop long-term client relationships that support Computershare’s continued success.

A role you will love

In this role, you will be responsible for leading the Edinburgh-based Client Management teams within the UK Registry business, part of UCIA Issuer Services. You will drive market share growth and the adoption of Computershare’s products and services, while ensuring the delivery of excellent client service, maintaining high-quality standards and effectively managing risk through appropriate controls. You will also provide inspirational leadership and strategic direction to the business, ensuring that client, people, financial and risk objectives are consistently achieved and exceeded.

You will play a key role in developing and strengthening client relationships through effective account management practices, ensuring that you and your team have a thorough understanding of the Computershare proposition and can identify and respond to clients’ needs and challenges with appropriate solutions. Client retention will be a fundamental priority, alongside identifying opportunities to enhance existing relationships and drive long-term business growth.

Working closely with key client stakeholders, including primary contacts, procurement and legal teams, you will also lead and support successful RFP processes and contract negotiations. Through strong relationship management, commercial awareness and a focus on service excellence, you will contribute to securing client partnerships and supporting the continued success of the business.

Key responsibilities:

  • Responsible for increasing market share, driving uptake of Computershare products and services, ensuring excellence in client service (and quality assurances) whilst effectively managing risk using appropriate controls.
  • Providing inspirational leadership and direction for the Computershare business, to ensure client, people, financial and risk targets in line with Group and Regional goals are met / exceeded through leadership and coaching.
  • Responsible for the strategic direction and developing high-performing teams, the recruitment, ongoing development and staff management of all CIS staff in your allocated client facing teams. Developing and maximising the potential of the CIS staff and ensuring robust succession planning is in place and that staff have adequate client management experience.
  • Ensuring your team have a comprehensive understanding of the Computershare proposition, business/industry insight and experience together an excellent understanding of compliance and regulatory requirements.
  • Responsible for ensuring your team effectively engage with clients and deliver market leading service quality to build client trust and develop effective relationships to aid business growth (i.e. support the Existing Client Programme).
  • Acting as senior-level point of contact for major clients, gaining trust and respect, taking a key role in major client relationships including the management of fee and contract negotiations and strategic account planning. For those non-direct client relationships provide advice, support and direction to your team.
  • Responsible for continual improvements in the level of client satisfaction, as measured through internal and external surveys, and enhancing Computershare’s reputation in the marketplace.
  • Represent the Business Unit internally, Computershare in the business community and actively promote the brand and reputation, whilst seeking opportunities for business development.
  • Support the Business Development team with new business opportunities and proactively seek out opportunities for new business from within your external network.
  • Demonstrate advanced commercial expertise in relation to your business unit P&L, and participate in the budget and forecast process, in line with CIS policy
  • Develop and maintain advanced Industry and Market awareness.

title: Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) Technical Integration and Migration SME
location: Washington, District of Columbia, United States
description:
The Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) Technical Integration and Migration SME IV will provide senior-level cryptographic engineering, technical integration, and advisory expertise in support of Department of War post-quantum cryptography initiatives.

The position requires deep technical understanding of cryptographic algorithms, protocols, public key infrastructure (PKI), key management, and their integration across enterprise and mission systems, combined with the ability to translate that expertise into cryptographic inventory implementation, PQC policy, migration planning, technical assessments, and enterprise adoption strategies. The ideal candidate will advise senior Government leadership and DoW stakeholders on cryptographic dependencies, technical integration challenges, migration risks, solution viability, and practical implementation pathways across devices, applications, networks, cloud environments, embedded systems, and enterprise infrastructure.


Responsibilities:

  • Provide senior-level cryptographic engineering and technical integration expertise across cryptographic algorithms, protocols, cipher suites, PKI, key management, encryption, authentication, and crypto-agile architectures.
  • Assess the integration and migration of cryptographic capabilities across applications, devices, networks, cloud environments, embedded systems, and other mission and enterprise platforms, including compatibility, interoperability, performance, lifecycle, and operational constraints.
  • Identify cryptographic migration challenges, system dependencies, interoperability concerns, technical gaps, and potential mission or functionality impacts.
  • Develop migration scenarios, implementation-plan mappings, technical reports, and practical recommendations for transitioning cryptographic algorithms, protocols, PKI, authentication mechanisms, key-management capabilities, and encryption services.
  • Conduct technical briefings, use-case reviews, solution assessments, architecture reviews, and implementation-plan evaluations to support DoW PQC planning and decision-making.
  • Provide cryptographic technical consultation supporting research, engineering, architecture, policy, and enterprise transition activities.
  • Develop a synchronized DoW-wide methodology for implementing and maintaining cryptographic inventories across devices, applications, networks, cloud environments, and embedded systems.
  • Support cryptographic inventory timelines, milestones, tasking, reporting requirements, and deliverables in accordance with OMB guidance and Government direction.
  • Collaborate with Combatant Commands, Services, Agencies, DISA, and other stakeholders to establish consistent inventory processes, technical requirements, data requirements, and outputs.
  • Research, develop, and draft DoW PQC policies, governance frameworks, implementation guidance, and migration roadmaps aligned with NSM-10, NIST standards, and DoW mission requirements.
  • Assess Government and commercial PQC solutions for security, technical maturity, scalability, interoperability, performance, operational suitability, and alignment with DoW use cases.
  • Evaluate vendor claims and proposed cryptographic solutions to identify implementation limitations, integration requirements, technical tradeoffs, and viable migration approaches.
  • Maintain visibility of industry capabilities, vendor solutions, implementation risks, emerging cryptographic technologies, and developments relevant to DoW PQC adoption.
  • Advise Government leadership on enterprise cryptographic deployment, modernization, update, sequencing, and risk-management considerations.
  • Develop executive briefings, technical reports, decision papers, roadmaps, and other documentation for technical and nontechnical audiences.
  • Facilitate technical meetings and collaborate with organizations such as DIU, DISA, NSA, NIST, USCYBERCOM, DoW Components, cloud providers, and industry partners.

This position is designed to be flexible, with responsibilities evolving to meet business needs and enable individual growth.


Requirements:

  • Active Top Secret/Sensitive Compartmented Information clearance required.
  • Ph.D. in mathematics, computer science, cryptography, cybersecurity, electrical engineering, or a related field, with at least 20 years of related professional experience in cryptography, including significant experience in cryptographic engineering, technical integration, architecture, or
  • implementation; OR Master’s degree in a related field, with at least 20 years of related professional experience in cryptography, including significant experience in cryptographic engineering, technical integration, architecture, or implementation.
  • Extensive experience engineering, integrating, architecting, implementing, or modernizing cryptographic capabilities within complex production, enterprise, or mission environments.
  • Expert knowledge of classical and post-quantum cryptography, cryptographic algorithms, protocols, cipher suites, key management, PKI, encryption, authentication, digital signatures, and cryptographic agility.
  • Demonstrated experience integrating or migrating cryptographic algorithms, protocols, PKI, key-management capabilities, authentication mechanisms, encryption services, or related cryptographic technologies within operational systems.
  • Experience assessing cryptographic integration and migration risks, including compatibility, interoperability, performance impacts, lifecycle dependencies, operational constraints, and mission impacts.
  • Demonstrated experience providing senior-level technical leadership for enterprise cryptographic programs, cybersecurity initiatives, or large-scale technology modernization efforts.
  • Experience identifying, documenting, and managing cryptographic dependencies across applications, devices, networks, cloud environments, and embedded systems.
  • Ability to evaluate commercial, cloud-based, open-source, and Government cryptographic solutions and assess the technical validity of vendor claims, implementation approaches, and migration options.
  • Experience developing technical policy, implementation frameworks, migration strategies, roadmaps, or governance documentation for federal or DoW organizations.
  • Knowledge of NSM-10, OMB Memorandum M-23-02, NIST PQC standards, CNSS issuances, and related federal cryptographic guidance.
  • Ability to translate deep cryptographic technical knowledge into clear policy, technical guidance, implementation plans, migration strategies, and executive recommendations.
  • Strong technical writing, briefing, facilitation, analytical, and stakeholder-engagement skills.

Explore the Area:
Grand Junction, Colorado, is the key access point to the mountains and canyonlands of western Colorado and eastern Utah. Centrally located between Denver, CO (250 miles east) and Salt Lake City, UT (270 miles west), Grand Junction was named for the convergence of the Gunnison River and Colorado River. Over 1.5 million acres of public lands connect the area’s alpine terrain with the dramatic high desert, nourished by powerful rivers that sustain the vibrant agriculture industry. Opportunities for outdoor adventures are abundant in every season due to the year-round temperate climate. Home to “Nature’s Trifecta,” Grand Junction is surrounded by the Colorado National Monument – a mini-Grand Canyon, Rattlesnake Arches – the second-largest concentration of natural arches in the world, and the Grand Mesa – the largest flat-top mountain in the world. title: Infrastructure Engineer
description:
Job Summary

The Junior Cloud/Infrastructure Engineer will support the design, implementation, and maintenance of our organization's cloud and on-premise infrastructure. This role is an excellent opportunity for an early-career engineer to gain hands-on experience with system monitoring, performance optimization, and cloud technologies under the mentorship of senior engineers.

YOUR IMPACT

At Redwood, we strive to automate and optimize our operations to support the scale of our business. As a junior observability engineer, you will support systems that collect, analyze, and visualize data from software applications and infrastructure. You will gain deep exposure to system health monitoring, alerting strategies, and proactive problem identification.

Responsibilities:

  • Support Infrastructure Strategy: Assist in implementing infrastructure initiatives including data collection pipelines, dashboards, metrics, logging, tracing, and alerting under senior engineer guidance.
  • System Monitoring: Help monitor system performance, identify potential bottlenecks, and support solutions to optimize efficiency and reliability.
  • Incident Response: Assist in incident response efforts and troubleshooting of system issues, learning root cause analysis practices.
  • Tooling and Infrastructure: Learn and work with observability tools such as Prometheus, Datadog, New Relic, and VictoriaMetrics to capture metrics, logs, and traces.
  • Alerting: Help configure and maintain alerts based on defined thresholds, ensuring timely notification of potential issues.
  • Data Analysis: Support analysis of collected data to identify performance trends, collaborating with engineering teams on resolutions.
  • Automation: Assist in developing automation scripts for repetitive monitoring and alerting tasks to reduce manual effort.
  • Cross-functional Collaboration: Learn from and collaborate with development and operations teams, gaining exposure to cloud and infrastructure best practices across the software development lifecycle.
  • Capacity Planning: Assist with capacity planning tasks under senior engineer guidance using observability data.
  • Dashboard Support: Help create and maintain dashboards that provide real-time insights into system health and operational metrics.

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, a related field, in progress or completed — or equivalent bootcamp/self-taught experience
  • 0-2 years of systems administration/engineering experience (internship or co-op experience counts)
  • Basic understanding of monitoring principles and best practices
  • Familiarity with one or more observability tools (Prometheus, Grafana, Datadog, New Relic, etc.)
  • Basic exposure to cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, GCP) and containerization concepts (Docker, Kubernetes)
  • Some scripting experience in Python, Bash, or PowerShell
  • Basic understanding of layer 2/3 networking concepts (VLANs, routing, ACLs)

  • Strong communication and collaboration skills

Preferred Qualifications:

title: Technical Services Manager – Estates and Facilities
description:
Our client is a leading nationwide healthcare organisation providing specialist residential and community based services across Ireland. With an estate of approximately 180 residential properties, they are now seeking an experienced Technical Services Manager to lead the facilities and maintenance function across the organisation.


This is a significant leadership role. You will oversee three Facilities Managers, each responsible for approximately 60 properties and supported by a five person maintenance team. These properties are not simply buildings. They are people’s homes. The role requires someone who can maintain them with the same care and attention they would give their own home, while operating within the standards and scrutiny of a highly regulated environment.


Reporting to the General Manager, you will:

→ Lead the facilities and maintenance function across approximately 180 residential properties

→ Manage and develop three Facilities Managers and their maintenance teams

→ Maintain high standards across maintenance, fire safety and regulatory compliance

→ Oversee reactive maintenance, ensuring issues are prioritised, completed and recorded through the AZOLA maintenance management system

→ Manage planned maintenance programmes delivered through external service providers

→ Manage contractors and specialist suppliers, ensuring performance, quality and value for money

→ Lead estate improvement projects including insulation programmes, wastewater treatment upgrades, property adaptations and other capital works

→ Manage budgets, procurement and expenditure across the estate

→ Ensure properties remain ready for regulatory inspections and compliance checks

→ Use maintenance and asset data to identify recurring issues, manage risk and improve performance across the portfolio


What We Are Looking For

We are looking for an experienced facilities, estates or construction management professional with the technical capability and leadership experience to manage a large, geographically dispersed property portfolio.


You will bring:

→ A Level 8 qualification in facilities management, construction management, engineering or another relevant technical discipline

→ At least five years’ management experience within facilities, estates, construction, engineering or technical services

→ Experience leading facilities, maintenance or technical teams

→ Strong knowledge of planned and reactive maintenance, fire safety, building compliance and contractor management

→ Strong budget management, procurement and commercial judgement

→ The ability to manage multiple priorities while maintaining consistently high standards

→ A full clean driving licence and flexibility to travel across the estate


Experience within healthcare, disability services or another regulated environment would be highly desirable, but is not essential.


We are equally interested in candidates who have developed their careers through facilities management or construction management and can demonstrate the leadership, technical judgement and compliance mindset required to succeed in this environment.


The Opportunity

You will inherit an established operation with strong existing compliance performance, experienced Facilities Managers and maintenance teams already in place.


With the current incumbent planning to retire, there is also an opportunity for a structured handover. For the right person, this is an opportunity to take responsibility for a substantial nationwide estate, lead an established team and shape how the organisation manages its properties, maintenance, compliance and investment for the future.


Apply through LinkedIn or contact Donal O'Donoghue, Managing Director at Sanderson for a confidential discussion.

title: FPGA Design Engineer
description:
Description

​Looking for an opportunity to make an impact?


​At Leidos, we deliver innovative solutions through the efforts of our diverse and talented people who are dedicated to our customers’ success. We empower our teams, contribute to our communities, and operate sustainable. Everything we do is built on a commitment to do the right thing for our customers, our people, and our community. Our Mission, Vision, and Values guide the way we do business.

​

​Your greatest work is ahead!

​

​Leidos’ Defense Systems Electrical Systems department is seeking a talented Embedded Firmware Developer to join our team. The Electrical Systems Department is a design-focused group of engineers specializing in advanced hardware-based products. The individual selected for this position will be an embedded design engineer with varied technical interests and demonstrated engineering and leadership skills. The individual must be a self- starter with experience working with inter-disciplinary teams to solve challenging technical problems. The engineer will lead efforts on and develop architectures for embedded systems integrated into a diverse range of aerospace and military systems including manned/unmanned ground/air vehicles, missiles, defensive radars, and space systems.


​​The selected candidate will be a key technical leader in a fast-paced, environment through all phases of the product life cycle from concept development and detailed design through manufacturing, qualification testing, and post-delivery support. The candidate will be responsible for architecting, implementing, and testing embedded firmware and software on a variety of platforms, including FPGAs, microcontrollers, microprocessors, and mixed signal designs. Additional skills such as communications data-link design, digital-signal processing (DSP) design, system design, experience with technical trade studies, and evaluation of technology improvements are a plus.


​With a product focus, the individual is also expected to actively partner with other engineers, project managers, technicians, and the customer to develop solutions that adhere to a diverse set of requirements. This includes architecture decisions from requirements that help inform and drive hardware implementations and working closely with hardware engineers. Additionally, the engineer will support resolution of technical issues that are discovered during the manufacture and test of deliverable products. This will include troubleshooting board-level issues, assessing failures for root cause, and identifying corrective actions. The ideal candidate will thrive in a learning environment that encourages leadership and technical growth.

​

​If this sounds like the kind of environment where you can thrive, keep reading!

​

​Leidos Defense Systems Sector provides a diverse portfolio of systems, solutions, and services covering land, sea, air, space, and cyberspace for customers worldwide. Solutions for Defense include enterprise and mission IT, large-scale intelligence systems, command and control, geospatial and data analytics, cybersecurity, logistics, training, and intelligence analysis and operations support. Our team is solving the world’s toughest security challenges for customers with “can’t fail” missions. To explore and learn more, click here!

​

​Are you ready to make an impact? Share your resume with us today!

​

​Primary Responsibilities

  • ​Key technical leader in a fast-paced, environment.
  • ​Responsible for all phases of the product life cycle from concept development and detailed design through manufacturing, qualification testing, and post-delivery support.
  • ​Responsible for architecting, implementing, and testing embedded firmware and software on a variety of platforms, including FPGAs, microcontrollers, microprocessors, and mixed signal designs.
  • ​Additional skills such as communications data-link design, digital-signal processing (DSP) design, system design, experience with technical trade studies, and evaluation of technology improvements are a plus.
  • ​Support resolution of technical issues that are discovered during the manufacture and test of deliverable products.
  • ​Troubleshooting board-level issues, assessing failures for root cause, and identifying corrective actions.

​Basic Qualifications

  • ​Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering or equivalent degree from an ABET-accredited institution.
  • ​Candidate must have at least 4+ years of experience in embedded system design and test or 2+ years with MS degree.
  • ​Understand trade-offs of embedded system targets (such as FPGA, SoC, microcontroller, RTOS, bare-metal) for developing best cost/option architectures
  • ​Proven experience with FPGA design and hardware description languages such as VHDL, Verilog, or SystemVerilog
  • ​Experience with common communication protocols such as: UART, Ethernet, SPI, I2C, CAN bus, etc.
  • ​Hands-on laboratory experience with instrumentation, test equipment, and debug/test methods
  • ​Position requires candidates to be capable of performing in a collaborative engineering environment working closely with multi-disciplinary teams
  • ​Candidate must be a resident of the North Alabama area or willing to relocate to the Huntsville - North Alabama, AL area
  • ​Candidate must be a US Citizen and possess (and be able to maintain) a Final Secret Clearance or meet the eligibility to obtain (and maintain) a Secret Clearance.

​Preferred Qualifications

  • ​Developing overall firmware/software architecture for embedded systems
  • ​Experience with embedded software/firmware programming in languages such as C, C++, or assembly languages
  • ​Embedded operating systems (Linux, VxWorks, Integrity, FreeRTOS, uC/OS-II)
  • ​GNU/Linux and development of kernel drivers
  • ​Utilizing modern Xilinx FPGA and SoC families and design tools (Xilinx IP Cores, AXI4, AXI-Stream)
  • ​Software or FPGA test and verification experience (unit testing, FPGA simulation testbenching, HWIL)
  • ​RISC microprocessors architectures (ARM Cortex, Microblaze, PowerPC, RISC-V)

title: Medical Data Scientist
description:
Medical Data Scientist Responsibilities

The Medical Data Scientist will be responsible for the analysis of clinical trial data in partnership with the medical monitor to identify and to support the identification, assessment, management and interpretation of clinical trial subject safety and identification of safety signals, trends, and patterns.

In addition, the role will provide internal project management and coordination support for standalone projects across Chief Medical Office (CMO) functional groups, contributing to efficient project delivery and operational consistency.

Responsibilities

  • Collaborate with medical monitors to establish clinical/safety data workflows to meet the clinical/safety data review needs of individual clinical studies in accordance with medical monitoring plans and data management plans.
  • Assist the medical monitors with pre study activities and the preparation and drafting of relevant study documentation and clinical study plans such as medical data review plans, medical monitoring plans, safety plans, Safety Review Committee (SRC) / Data and Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) charters etc.
  • Extract and convert clinical data into formats that assists the medical monitor to perform ongoing clinical assessment of safety and efficacy as per individual study needs.
  • Perform periodic aggregate data analyses of individual subjects and defined sub-populations to identify potential safety signals, trends, and individual and collective data outliers in collaboration with the medical monitor.
  • Undertake pre-processing of clinical data and presenting this information in useable formats (tables, listings, and data visualization techniques) in collaboration with the medical monitors to support activities such as data provision for SRC/ DSMB meetings, Interim and Clinical Study Report requirements.

Standalone Project Management and Operational Support

  • Provide internal project management and coordination support for standalone projects across CMO functional groups, working collaboratively with designated project leads and subject matter experts.
  • Support project initiation, planning, milestone tracking, deliverable monitoring and project close-out activities.
  • Assist with project financial administration, including budget and end of month project finance activities.
  • Contribute to the development and implementation of standardised project management tools, templates and processes to improve operational efficiency, consistency and quality of project delivery.

Minimum Qualifications & Experience

  • Bachelor's Degree in medical, biostatistics, pharmaceutical sciences or equivalent qualifications with experience in clinical data analysis, clinical practice or clinical research.
  • Expertise in clinical data management, medical data reviews and conducting data trend analysis.
  • Demonstrated ability to analyse complex clinical data and convert data into useable information that is easy to interpret.
  • Excellent computer literacy, knowledge of data management applications with expertise in using data software (Microsoft Excel, Microsoft Office, Rave EDC etc).
  • Analytical mindset with good problem-solving skills.
  • Strong organisational, time management and communication skills, with the ability to coordinate multiple activities and work collaboratively across functional teams.

  • Experience in project coordination, project administration or supporting clinical research projects would be advantageous.

We offer hybrid working arrangements and full flexibility in working hours to ensure our staff achieve the work-life balance often missing in this role.

The Defense Sector at Leidos is looking for a Senior DevSecOps Engineer to support a fast-paced program with the Air Force Life Cycle Management Center. description:

This role focuses on operating, maintaining, troubleshooting, and supporting 3D printing equipment and post-processing systems to ensure high quality production output. The technician works closely with engineering and production teams to maintain print schedules, meet production deadlines, and ensure all printed components meet required specifications.

title: Manager, Demand Planning
description:
HOURGLASS COSMETICS — Manager, Demand Planning (Hybrid Role)

Connected by creativity and driven by purpose. Hourglass Cosmetics is a vegan and cruelty-free beauty brand, redefining luxury cosmetics with high-performance products, innovative formulas, and award-winning franchises. Recognized by Forbes, Fast Company and Time Magazine as one of the most inventive beauty companies, Hourglass leads the industry with its breakthrough products and its commitment to animal welfare. Founded in 2004, Hourglass is globally available in 32 markets and over 4,600 doors including Sephora, Ulta, Neiman Marcus, Selfridges, Space NK and more. Hourglass became part of the Unilever Prestige division in 2017. Discover more about the Hourglass brand story and mission on our website hourglasscosmetics.com.

The Manager, Demand Planning leads demand planning for the North America and DTC regions, owning the consensus demand plan for both. This person serves as a link between the sales, finance, and supply chain functions to ensure alignment between plans and will work to create and achieve consensus for forecasts through collaborative cross-functional planning processes.

WHAT YOU’LL DO:

  • Lead demand planning for the North America and DTC regions including:
    • Owning top-down and bottom-up finished goods wholesale and retail forecasts for North America and DTC
    • Building forecasts that combine statistical baselines with commercial inputs such as promotions, pricing, new launches, and retailer plans
    • Leading North America and DTC forecast reviews and forecast alignment with senior commercial, finance, and operations leadership
    • Leading the new product development, sampling, and gratis forecast process for North America and DTC
    • Developing demand planning standards, processes, and documentation
    • Leading the North America and DTC demand review in the monthly S&OP process and presenting the consensus forecast, risks, and opportunities to leadership
    • Accountable for forecast accuracy and bias for North America and DTC, analyzing variances and driving improvement plans
  • Own monthly SKU-level forecasts by retailer for North America and DTC including:
    • Synthesizing retail sales, wholesale, DTC, and operational data to build and challenge forecast assumptions
    • Anticipating supply and demand imbalances, inventory gaps, and overstock exposure, and leading mitigation plans with operations and supply chain leadership
  • Technology including:
    • Business expert for Oracle Planning Cloud Demand Planning Tool at Hourglass, responsible for forecast data integrity in the tool
    • Managing the relationship with Unilever Prestige IT and external partners for upgrades, enhancements, and maintenance to Planning Tool
    • Evaluating and creating processes and tools in support of continuous improvement efforts to support demand planning at Hourglass
    • Using analytics and AI-enabled tools to improve planning, reporting, and efficiency
  • Lead analysis and reporting including:
    • Presenting performance, trend, and forecast learnings to leadership
    • Delivering accurate, timely reporting on sales results, and translating those results into forecast and business recommendations for stakeholders
    • Leading ad-hoc analysis in support of leadership and commercial decisions
    • Managing allocations and gratis requests to support inventory merchandise strategy for newness, events, and promotions

YOU’LL LOVE THIS JOB IF:

  • You are CREATIVE: You are innovative and forward-thinking in your approach and mindset.
  • You are highly STRATEGIC: You are able to develop creative concepts and vision that support brand and business goals.
  • You are extremely ORGANIZED: You are not overwhelmed by the thought of tackling multiple tasks at a time.
  • You are DETAIL ORIENTED: You appreciate the importance of having detailed and precise information.
  • You are a strong COMMUNICATOR: You are a people person, natural leader and collaborate well with others.
  • You are AGILE: You adapt well to changing needs and priorities and are able to pivot easily to achieve goals and deadlines.
  • You are PASSIONATE about beauty: You are eager to learn and absorb all things related to beauty, brand and creative strategy.

QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Business, Economics, Finance, or related field
  • 6+ years of experience in demand planning, supply chain, or analytical role, beauty/retail experience preferred
  • Strong track record of cross-functional influence and presenting to senior leadership
  • Strong Excel and analytical skills required; PowerBI and Oracle Planning Cloud experience preferred
  • Must be highly organized and have strong attention to detail
  • Passion for product, specifically cosmetics and skincare
  • Proven success creating and leading processes
  • Analytical, with experience tracking and reporting
  • Adaptable, resourceful and forward thinking
  • Thrive on solving problems and looking at implementing creative solutions
  • Creative, positive and high-energy individual with an ability to execute
  • Must be able to work from Corporate Office at least 60% of the time

The expected base salary range for this position is $95,000 to $105,000 per year. The exact base salary is determined by various factors including experience, skills, education, geographic location, and budget.
