title: Energy Policy Director
description:
About the role

The Director Energy Policy EMEA owns EdgeConneX's view of the European energy policy and regulatory landscape as it affects data centers' access to power — grid access and connection, capacity allocation, grid codes and connection standards, energy market rules, and energy procurement. The role monitors and shapes the company's engagement with energy regulation, grid connection reform and policy developments across EMEA, translates regulatory change into actionable internal strategy, and represents EdgeConneX in the industry forums where data center energy policy is debated and formed. This is a senior individual-contributor role within the global Public Policy and Affairs function, working closely with the Site & Energy Development EMEA team across markets, alongside Country VPs and energy development, site selection and legal colleagues. The position carries real influence over where EdgeConneX invests: a regulatory shift in connection queueing, capacity allocation, grid code requirements or flexibility obligations can change the viability of a site or an entire market, and this role is accountable for seeing those shifts early and turning them into decisions.

What you'll do

Policy and regulatory monitoring

  • Track EU-level energy legislation and regulation affecting data centers' access to and procurement of power, including electricity market design, grid codes including emerging requirements for large loads, connection and capacity allocation rules, obligations and market rules that shape energy procurement.
  • Monitor national-level developments in EdgeConneX's EMEA markets: grid connection reform, capacity allocation frameworks, connection queue management, tariff changes, renewable energy and sustainability obligations, together with developments in energy supply regulations and data-center-specific regulation (energy efficiency, reporting rules).
  • Maintain a structured regulatory watch across regulators, TSOs and national authorities, and flag changes with project or market impact as they emerge.

Translation into internal strategy

  • Convert regulatory developments into clear internal guidance: what changed, which projects and markets are affected directly or indirectly, and what EdgeConneX should do about it.
  • Advise site selection, energy development and investment decisions on regulatory risk and opportunity, including market entry and exit considerations.
  • Advise on the regulation shaping access to grid capacity and energy procurement, including market rules and support schemes.
  • Produce concise briefings and position papers for EMEA leadership and support due diligence on acquisitions and new sites with regulatory assessments.
  • Maintain a forward view of grid code and market reform trajectories, assess their business impact on existing sites and the future pipeline, and feed that view into EdgeConneX's long-term EMEA strategy for power, site design and market selection.

External representation and engagement

  • Represent EdgeConneX in relevant industry forums and trade associations, and in regulatory consultations and stakeholder processes at EU and national level.
  • Join the working groups and technical committees where grid codes and connection requirements are designed so EdgeConneX helps shape requirements for large loads before they are finalized.
  • Build and maintain working relationships with regulators, TSOs, ministries and peer companies' policy teams.
  • Shape industry positions on grid access, capacity allocation, energy market reform and renewables policy for data centers, ensuring EdgeConneX's commercial interests are reflected in collective responses and advocacy.

Qualifications

  • 10+ years in energy policy, energy regulation or regulatory affairs, with substantial exposure to European electricity markets, grid regulation and energy policy; experience on the regulator, TSO, utility or large energy consumer side all considered.
  • Demonstrated understanding of grid connection processes and reform debates in at least two major European markets, of the EU legislative process as it applies to energy, and of grid codes development process.
  • Track record of representing an organization in industry associations, regulatory consultations or public stakeholder processes.
  • Established relationships with energy policy decision makers across EU institutions, national ministries, regulators and TSOs, and a demonstrated ability to use that network to influence policy outcomes.
  • Experience translating regulatory analysis into business or investment decisions, ideally for energy-intensive infrastructure (data centers, industrial loads, generation or storage).
  • Degree in law, economics, engineering, public policy or a related field
  • Fluent English required; a further major European language (German, Spanish, Italian, French or a Nordic language) is a strong advantage.

title: Environmental Remediation Engineer
description:
Description

Leidos is seeking a Remediation Engineer to support environmental investigation, remediation, and restoration projects under the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act (CERCLA/Superfund) and Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (RCRA) corrective action programs.


The Remediation Engineer will support technical design, regulatory documentation, field implementation, and coordination with clients, regulatory agencies, and multidisciplinary project teams throughout the remedial lifecycle—from site characterization and remedy evaluation through remedial design, implementation, and long-term monitoring.


The successful candidate will independently execute defined project tasks while collaborating with engineers, scientists, geologists, project managers, and other technical specialists. Strong organizational, technical writing, and communication skills are essential.


This position may be performed remotely within the United States, subject to Leidos remote-work eligibility requirements, or based onsite in Reston, VA, or Twinsburg, OH.


Primary Responsibilities

  • Support development of project plans and technical deliverables, including Project Management Plans (PMPs), Quality Assurance Project Plans (QAPPs), Accident Prevention Plans (APPs), Health and Safety Plans (HASPs), Remedial Investigation/Feasibility Study (RI/FS) reports and cost estimates, Proposed Plans (PPs), Records of Decision (RODs), remedial design packages (30%, 60%, 90%, and 100%), Remedial Design/Remedial Action Work Plans (RD/RAWPs), and equivalent RCRA documents.
  • Support the design, field implementation, evaluation, and reporting of pilot and treatability studies for remedial technologies.
  • Evaluate and design remediation approaches, including groundwater extraction and treatment, in-situ chemical oxidation/reduction, enhanced bioremediation, soil vapor extraction, air sparging, dual-phase extraction, thermal treatment, permeable reactive barriers, excavation, capping, stabilization, and monitored natural attenuation.
  • Prepare engineering drawings, design specifications, calculations, technical evaluations, and cost estimates in support of remedial design and implementation.
  • Support preparation of technical and cost proposals, subcontractor scopes of work, and bases of estimate.
  • Coordinate with project teams, clients, subcontractors, regulatory agencies, and other stakeholders as required to support project execution.
  • Perform work in accordance with Leidos and client environmental, quality, and health and safety requirements.
  • Travel to project locations as needed to support field activities, site visits, and client and stakeholder meetings.

Required Education and Experience

  • Bachelor's degree in Civil, Environmental, Chemical Engineering, or a related engineering discipline and at least 4 years of relevant environmental engineering experience, or Master's degree with at least 2 years of relevant experience.
  • Professional Engineer (PE) license or Engineer-in-Training (EIT) certification with demonstrated progress toward PE licensure.
  • Experience supporting projects under federal and state environmental regulatory frameworks, including CERCLA and RCRA.
  • Experience evaluating, designing, or implementing remedial technologies such as in-situ soil and groundwater treatment, groundwater extraction and treatment, thermal treatment, soil vapor extraction, air sparging, dual-phase extraction, permeable reactive barriers, excavation, capping, stabilization, dredging/sediment remediation, and monitored natural attenuation.
  • Experience with the investigation or remediation of contaminants such as PFAS, volatile organic compounds (VOCs), semi-volatile organic compounds (SVOCs), explosives, metals, PCBs, and pesticides/herbicides in soil, groundwater, surface water, and/or sediment.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to prepare clear and technically sound project documentation.
  • Ability to work independently on assigned tasks while contributing effectively within multidisciplinary project teams.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, including Word, Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint, and Project, and experience with environmental data or geospatial tools such as EQuIS, ArcGIS, or similar applications.
  • Valid driver's license.

Must be able to pass a Public Trust background investigation; due to contract requirements, U.S. Citizenship or U.S. Permanent residency is required.

title: Electronics Technologist
description:

Leidos is seeking an Electronics Technologist to execute on cutting-edge engineering efforts within the Maritime System Solutions (MSS) Portfolio of our Maritime Systems Division (MSD). This role is a unique opportunity to drive innovation in underwater vehicle systems, maritime sensors, subsea telemetry, and ISR solutions that support critical defense and national security missions.


You'll work with a multidisciplinary team advancing maritime technologies, from prototype design to full-scale system deployment for ongoing Navy missions.


Leidos’ Maritime Systems Division is a recognized leader in C4ISR technologies, delivering innovative, mission-critical solutions across sensor networks, unmanned systems, and tactical platforms. We’re known for achieving “industry firsts” in the most challenging maritime domains.


Join us and be part of a world-class team delivering unmatched solutions for today's most pressing maritime missions.

This position requires US citizenship and an active Secret security clearance.

Why Join Us?

  • Make an Impact: Your work will directly support U.S. maritime dominance and national security.
  • Lead Innovation: Be at the forefront of applying innovative technology and autonomy to real-world maritime systems.

Preferred Experience:

  • Experience with UUVs, deployed subsea systems, and underwater payloads
  • Proven track record in product manufacturing and transitioning designs to production

title: Part-Time Faculty: Architecture 350
description:
The University of Maine at Augusta is seeking qualified applications for part-time faculty in the Bachelor of Architecture (B. Arch) Program to teach ARC 350: Mechanical Systems in Architecture. Topics to be covered include mechanical, electrical, plumbing (MEP), fire protection, lighting, communication, security, acoustics, and vertical transportation systems. Students will learn how to design buildings with consideration to the needs of the systems and how those needs impact design program and process.

  • ARC 350: Mechanical Systems in Architecture

In-person (live) teaching on the Augusta campus is preferred, but a distance synchronous class (currently taught via Zoom) or hybrid course may be considered. This appointment is for the Spring 2027 semester and may continue into future semesters as needed.

UMA's Bachelor of Architecture program is Maine's only professional architecture program and the only public B.Arch in northern New England. The program is built upon our thirty-five-year history of providing architectural education in Maine. This is an exciting opportunity to be part of this new chapter of architectural education in Maine.

UMA's Architectural Mission: Architecture through Engagement

Our mission expresses who we are: SMALL . . . INTEGRATED . . . HANDS-ON. This fundamentally means we are about people: our students, our faculty, and our community partners. We teach architecture through engagement, educating, and empowering students to explore, investigate, and analyze the built environment. Engagement brings students into active contact with each other, their coursework, and our community partners.

The University of Maine at Augusta's Architecture program is rooted in three essential elements. The first is the mission to engage community; this is where our work takes place. The second is the desire to work in collaboration, within the department, the university, and with community partners; this is what allows us to affect positive change. And third is seen in our curriculum, based on the idea of being "grounded in real.” These are the tools we use to affect our collective build environment. title: Software Engineer III - Salesforce
description:
We have an exciting and rewarding opportunity for you to take your software engineering career to the next level.

As a Software Engineer III at JPMorgan Chase within the Consumer & Community Banking, JPM Wealth Management Technology team, you will be part of a team that owns end-to-end technical execution (design through production support), supports architectural evaluations with internal and external partners, and helps modernize platforms through automation, optimization, and capabilities including AI/LLM and Agentforce. You will also support and build Java microservices and React-based UI applications for use cases outside the Salesforce ecosystem as business needs arise.

  • Executes software solutions, design, development, and technical troubleshooting with ability to think beyond routine or conventional approaches to build solutions or breakdown technical problems
  • Leverages enterprise-authorized AI coding assist tools within the work environment to improve code quality, delivery speed, and productivity across complex deliverables (e.g., code generation/refactoring, unit test creation, documentation), while validating outputs through peer review, automated testing, and secure coding standards; contributes learnings and reusable patterns to improve broader team effectiveness.

  • Produces architecture and design artifacts for complex applications while being accountable for ensuring design constraints are met by software code development
  • Designs, develops, and troubleshoots software solutions on the Salesforce platform (including Apex, LWC, and Lightning Connect) and breaks down complex technical problems using practical, effective approaches
  • Builds secure, production-grade code; reviews, debugs, and improves code written by others
  • Designs and builds Java-based microservices (e.g., Spring Boot) and React-based UI components for applications outside the Salesforce ecosystem

  • Contributes to a team culture rooted in diversity, opportunity, inclusion, and respect

Required qualifications, capabilities, and skills

  • Formal training or certification in software engineering concepts, with 3+ years of applied experience.
  • Hands-on experience in system design, application development, testing, and operational stability for Salesforce-based applications.
  • Experience developing, debugging, and maintaining code in a large corporate environment using modern programming languages and database querying languages.
  • Hands-on experience with enterprise-authorized AI-assisted software development tools for coding, test creation, troubleshooting, or documentation, with the ability to critically evaluate, validate, and refine AI-generated outputs for correctness, performance, and security.
  • Understanding of responsible AI practices in engineering workflows, including data sensitivity, secure handling of inputs and outputs, resiliency, and security requirements, with the ability to guide peers on safe and effective AI usage.

  • Working proficiency in full-stack Java development, including building microservices using Spring Boot and Spring Cloud, as well as experience with modern UI frameworks such as React, to support applications beyond the Salesforce ecosystem.
  • Strong communication skills and executive presence, with the ability to clearly explain technical concepts, end-to-end system functionality, and the rationale behind architectural and design decisions.
  • Proven experience working with large data volumes, performance tuning, and platform/application optimization.

Preferred qualifications, capabilities, and skills

  • Financial services industry experience.
  • Experience building or integrating cloud-native applications, including AWS.
  • Familiarity with Jira, Bitbucket, and source/version control systems.
  • Salesforce certifications and/or Java/Spring or equivalent full-stack credentials.
  • Experience with API gateways, service mesh, or event-driven architecture patterns.
  • Experience designing or integrating AI-driven features within Salesforce or full-stack applications.
  • Strong understanding of modern cloud, integration, and application architecture patterns

title: Privacy Manager
description:
Join the transformative team at City of Hope, where we're changing lives and making a real difference in the fight against cancer, diabetes, and other life-threatening illnesses. City of Hope’s growing national system includes its Los Angeles campus, a network of clinical care locations across Southern California, a new cancer center in Orange County, California, and treatment facilities in Atlanta, Chicago and Phoenix. Our dedicated and compassionate employees are driven by a common mission\: To deliver the cures of tomorrow to the people who need them today.

Position Summary

The Manager, Privacy is an opportunity to play a key leadership role within City of Hope’s enterprise Privacy Program. Reporting to the System Director, Privacy, you will help translate privacy strategy and regulatory requirements into effective day-to-day operations across a growing national healthcare organization.

In this role, you will lead privacy investigations, auditing and monitoring, patient rights matters, Business Associate Agreement reviews, policy implementation, education, corrective actions, and regulatory response activities. You will evaluate privacy risk, provide practical guidance to business and clinical partners, and help ensure City of Hope continues to protect highly sensitive information while meeting evolving federal and state privacy requirements.

You will also supervise Privacy Program staff and collaborate across Legal, Human Resources, Health Information Management, Information Technology and Security, Research, clinical operations, and other key areas of the organization.

As a successful candidate, you will\:

  • Manage day-to-day activities supporting City of Hope’s Privacy Program and enterprise privacy priorities.
  • Lead privacy investigations from intake through closure, including fact-finding, risk assessments, documentation, breach-response coordination, mitigation, and corrective actions.
  • Manage privacy auditing and monitoring activities, including electronic access monitoring, control testing, trend analysis, reporting, and remediation.
  • Provide expert guidance regarding patient privacy and rights, including access, amendments, restrictions, confidential communications, and accounting of disclosures.
  • Manage Business Associate Agreement reviews and privacy-related contract provisions while partnering with Legal, Supply Chain, Information Security, and business leaders.
  • Draft, review, implement, and maintain privacy policies, procedures, standards, guidance, and operational tools.
  • Monitor federal and state privacy requirements, including HIPAA, and help assess emerging regulatory requirements affecting healthcare, research, consumer, employee, and digital information.
  • Collaborate with clinical and operational leaders and subject matter experts to identify privacy risks and incorporate privacy requirements into business processes.
  • Develop Privacy Program metrics, dashboards, analyses, and presentations to identify trends, measure effectiveness, and support executive and board-level reporting.
  • Supervise Privacy Program staff through work assignments, coaching, performance management, and professional development.

title: Sr District Manager, Enterprise (Majors)
description:
Everpure (NYSE: P) has evolved from storage pioneer to data platform, closing fiscal 2026 with $3.7 billion in revenue, its first billion-dollar quarter, and accelerating growth into FY27. Our strategic agenda spans the companies defining the next era of technology - hyperscalers, AI labs, the AI hardware supply chain, data platform providers, and the broader AI ecosystem.

This type of work—work that changes the world—is what the tech industry was founded on. So, if you're ready to seize the endless opportunities and leave your mark, come join us.

Should you accept this challenge?

Everpure is looking for a strategic, operationally strong Senior District Manager to lead and grow a group of our largest Enterprise West field-sales business. This leader will translate regional and company priorities into a clear district strategy, set operating direction for a high-performing team of Enterprise Account Executives, and align the extended sales organization and channel ecosystem to deliver durable results.

The Senior District Manager is accountable for district sales performance, including bookings, new-logo production, pipeline health, forecast accuracy, and team development. Success requires sound judgment across complex sales situations, strong executive relationships, and the ability to direct coordinated action across Account Executives, PreSales Engineering, Channel, and Inside Sales. The ideal candidate lives and sells in the Bay Area; significant field travel is expected.

What you’ll be doing

  • Set district strategy and deliver results: Translate regional and company objectives into district priorities, territory plans, and execution plans. Own district performance against annual bookings and new-logo goals, and adjust plans as market conditions and business needs evolve.
  • Lead and develop the sales organization: Lead, coach, and performance-manage Enterprise Account Executives. Recruit and develop talent, set clear expectations, build succession and team capability, and ensure Everpure’s culture and values are embedded in how the team operates.
  • Direct cross-functional execution: Align PreSales Engineers, Channel Managers, Inside Sales, and other partners around district priorities, account strategies, and resource needs. Coordinate complex, multi-resource sales motions through to close.
  • Establish operating rigor: Set and maintain standards for pipeline coverage, forecast accuracy, proof-of-concept management, partner alignment, and CRM discipline. Maintain a 4X pipeline to goal, review activity and pipeline weekly, and take timely action when coverage or performance is off plan.
  • Build strategic channel partnerships: Develop and sustain productive relationships with channel partner principals, account executives, and leadership teams. Establish alignment between partner plans and district objectives, and mobilize partners to improve customer outcomes and business results.

title: Staff Software Engineer
description:
StackAdapt is the leading technology company that empowers marketers to reach, engage, and convert audiences with precision. With 465 billion automated optimizations per second, the AI-powered StackAdapt Marketing Platform seamlessly connects brand and performance marketing to drive measurable results across the entire customer journey. The most forward-thinking marketers choose StackAdapt to orchestrate high-impact campaigns across programmatic advertising and marketing channels.

About the Team

Activations is part of StackAdapt's Data Hub product, our customer data platform. Advertisers bring their first-party data into Data Hub: CRM lists, website and app events, product catalogs and store locations. Activations turn that data into something they can use. We build audiences, keep them in sync with the channels advertisers buy on, and feed products and locations into dynamic creative.

We are a small team of senior and mid-level engineers. We work mostly in Go, on event-driven services that run at large scale, using Kafka, gRPC and TiDB on AWS. Advertisers spend against the audiences we build, and privacy law shapes how we handle their data, so correctness matters as much as speed.

The team runs flat. Senior engineers lead projects from design to launch. You will set the technical standard those project leads work to: how we design, review and ship. You will help every engineer on the team get better at it, mostly by building alongside them.

You will work closely with our Data Hub architect, who sets technical direction across the whole domain and decides designs that cross Data Hub teams. You decide designs inside Activations, and the two of you work together on the ones that cross the line. You also own the technical calls the team makes day to day, and the case for changing direction when what we learn in production says we should.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Owning the technical health of the team's systems. You will own audience evaluation, CRM and programmatic audience syncs, and the product and location feeds behind dynamic creative. You will decide where reliability, cost and tech debt work goes, and make the case for it on the roadmap.
  • Building. You will write production code every week and take on the hardest work yourself: how we evaluate audiences at scale, how we keep long-running syncs reliable, and how activation grows beyond email to new identifiers.
  • Setting the review bar. A growing share of our code is written with AI coding agents. You will define what a good review looks like when an agent wrote the first draft, review the risky changes yourself, and teach the team to catch what agents miss: concurrency, data correctness, idempotency, privacy.
  • Coaching engineers. You will help senior engineers lead their own projects, and help mid-level engineers grow into senior ones. Expect to do this through design reviews, pairing and code reviews that teach.
  • Making the team faster with AI, carefully. You will find where AI tools save real time for us, such as review assistants, test generation, runbooks and on-call triage. You will build or adopt those tools, measure whether they work, and drop the ones that don't.
  • Turning product needs into technical plans. You will work with Product and the engineering teams around us to shape multi-month plans. You will find unknowns and cross-team dependencies early, and explain trade-offs in plain language.
  • Leading on reliability. You will take part in the on-call rotation, lead root cause analysis for team incidents, and make sure the fixes hold. You will set the team's standards for testing, observability and alerting.

What You'll Bring to the Table

  • 8+ years building backend systems, with several years as the engineer others turned to for design decisions on a team that owns production services.
  • Strong Go, or deep experience in another backend language and a willingness to work in Go every day.
  • Experience designing and running distributed, data-heavy systems: event streaming (Kafka or similar), workflow orchestration, high-volume batch or streaming pipelines, and SQL/NewSQL stores at scale.
  • Has led a multi-month project across teams, from design to production.
  • Has led incident response and root cause analysis for production services.
  • A track record of raising a team's engineering standards beyond code review, through artifacts others adopted: design docs, review guidelines, shared libraries, CI checks, runbooks.
  • Real experience with AI coding tools: you use them to build, you know where they fail, and you have helped others use them well.
  • Evidence that engineers grew because of you, through mentoring, sponsorship, or by stepping back so someone else could lead.
  • Clear writing. Most of our decisions are made in design docs and pull requests.
  • Good judgment about trade-offs: when to ship the simple thing, when to pay down debt, and when to push back.
  • Bonus: Ad tech, marketing technology or customer data platforms (identity resolution, audience segmentation, CRM integrations).
  • Bonus: Privacy and data deletion compliance (CCPA/CPRA, data broker deletion requests, GDPR).
  • Bonus: Temporal, gRPC/protobuf, TiDB or Vitess.

title: Associate Director
description:
A leading international architecture and design practice is looking to appoint an experienced Aviation Studio Lead to join its Dublin office, taking a senior leadership role within its growing aviation team. This is an exciting opportunity to lead the design and delivery of large-scale international airport and aviation projects, while playing a key role in developing the practice's aviation offering across Ireland and the wider European market. The practice is seeking an accomplished architectural leader with a strong background in aviation, excellent client-facing capabilities and experience managing multidisciplinary design teams. The successful candidate will combine design leadership, project delivery and commercial awareness, helping to shape the strategic direction and continued growth of the studio. Working closely with senior leadership across the wider international business, the Aviation Studio Lead will oversee major aviation projects, develop client relationships, mentor architectural teams and contribute to new business opportunities.


Job Description


  • Lead and develop the aviation studio in Dublin, overseeing the design, coordination and delivery of major airport and aviation projects.
  • Provide strategic and architectural leadership across international aviation developments, including airport terminals, terminal expansions, refurbishments and associated infrastructure.
  • Take responsibility for the overall quality of architectural design, ensuring projects meet client expectations, operational requirements and commercial objectives.
  • Lead multidisciplinary project teams, coordinating architects, designers, engineers, specialist consultants and external stakeholders.
  • Oversee projects from early feasibility and concept design through design development, technical delivery and construction.
  • Act as a senior point of contact for key aviation clients, airport operators, consultants and project stakeholders.
  • Build and maintain strong client relationships, identifying opportunities for repeat business and long-term partnerships.
  • Support business development activities, including identifying new opportunities, preparing proposals, participating in interviews and contributing to competitive bids.
  • Work closely with international studio leaders to develop the practice's aviation portfolio and strengthen its presence across the European market.
  • Oversee project programmes, resources, budgets and deliverables, ensuring projects are delivered efficiently and to a consistently high standard.
  • Provide design direction and technical oversight, ensuring architectural solutions respond to complex airport operations, passenger requirements and regulatory constraints.
  • Lead internal design reviews, client presentations and project coordination meetings.
  • Support recruitment, team development and resource planning as the aviation studio continues to grow.
  • Mentor and develop architects, designers and project leaders, encouraging collaboration, professional development and design excellence.
  • Promote effective collaboration between the Dublin studio and the practice's wider international aviation teams.
  • Contribute to the strategic direction of the studio, supporting operational improvements, commercial performance and long-term growth.


Key Skills


  • Qualified Architect with substantial experience working within a recognised international architecture or multidisciplinary design practice.
  • Extensive experience within the aviation sector, ideally involving major international airports, terminal developments, expansions or refurbishment programmes.
  • Proven experience operating at Studio Lead, Director, Associate Director, Principal or equivalent senior leadership level.
  • Strong understanding of airport planning, terminal design, passenger experience and the operational requirements of aviation environments.
  • Experience leading large-scale, technically complex architectural projects across multiple design and delivery stages.
  • Demonstrable experience managing multidisciplinary architectural and engineering teams.
  • Strong client-facing capabilities, with experience developing and maintaining relationships with airport operators, developers and other major stakeholders.
  • Commercial awareness, including experience managing project budgets, fees, resources and delivery programmes.
  • Experience contributing to business development, project pursuits, fee proposals and client presentations.
  • Ability to balance architectural design quality with operational, technical and commercial project requirements.
  • Strong understanding of multidisciplinary coordination, project delivery processes and construction documentation.
  • Experience overseeing BIM-led project delivery, with knowledge of Revit and other digital design platforms advantageous.
  • Excellent communication, presentation and negotiation skills.
  • Strong leadership and mentoring capabilities, with experience developing teams and supporting career progression.
  • Experience working on international aviation projects and collaborating with geographically distributed design teams.
  • A proactive, commercially minded approach with the ability to contribute to the strategic growth of an architectural studio.


This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced Aviation Director, Studio Lead or senior architectural leader looking to take on a significant leadership position within a highly regarded international architecture and design practice. The role offers the chance to lead a growing aviation team in Dublin, working on major international airport and terminal developments while contributing to the strategic direction and expansion of the practice's aviation business. The successful candidate will have the opportunity to combine hands-on architectural leadership with broader responsibilities across client relationships, business development, team management and studio growth. Working closely with established international aviation specialists, they will play an important role in strengthening the Dublin studio's capabilities, developing its project portfolio and building long-term relationships with key clients. The practice offers a collaborative international working environment, exposure to high-profile aviation projects and the opportunity to make a meaningful contribution to the continued growth of its aviation division.

title: Cloud Engineer
description:
Description

The Defense Sector at Leidos is looking for a Cloud Engineer to support multiple fast-paced programs across the Air Force. The Cloud Engineer will deploy, maintain, and scale hybrid cloud digital infrastructure for multiple Air Force customers. This position requires a fast-learning, high-performing candidate with a proven history of delivering cloud solutions to customers. The ideal candidate will have experience in deploying and maintaining cloud infrastructure in Microsoft Azure cloud using DevSecOps practices and an Everything-as-Code approach. This position offers a valuable opportunity to further develop your career in cloud engineering within an Air Force program, contributing to the secure and efficient delivery of service in a challenging and innovative environment. You will be a member of a team providing 24x7 monitoring and management of customer networks and will be on-call in the event of off-hours emergencies.

This position does require on-site work, and the primary location is in Omaha, NE. Candidates located near Lorton, VA and also Oklahoma City, OK will also be considered.

Primary Responsibilities:

  • Design, deploy, and manage virtual cloud infrastructures across hybrid environments in Microsoft Azure Cloud (IaaS & PaaS).
  • Automate deployments and configurations using Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) and Configuration-as-Code tools such as Terraform, Ansible, and ARM/BICEP templates.
  • Provision, maintain, and scale cloud resources in Microsoft Azure in collaboration with cross-functional teams.
  • Monitor cloud resource utilization to ensure cost efficiency and scalability.
  • Troubleshoot and resolve system, application, and infrastructure issues, performing root cause analysis as needed.
  • Ensure infrastructure meets security, compliance, and operational standards within a DevSecOps framework.
  • Support CI/CD pipelines and integrate infrastructure automation into the development lifecycle.
  • Implement and manage containerization and orchestration technologies, such as Docker and Kubernetes, for microservices architectures.
  • Configure and maintain monitoring tools to ensure system and application availability and performance.
  • Identify and implement optimizations to improve efficiency, reduce latency, and enhance system uptime.
  • Apply security best practices, including identity and access management (IAM), network segmentation, and encryption, to protect hybrid cloud infrastructures.
  • Assist in audits and compliance initiatives (e.g., RMF, NIST, ISO 27001).
  • Provide Tier-2/3 support for escalated issues, working closely with internal teams and external vendors.
  • Document procedures, configurations, and troubleshooting steps to enhance knowledge sharing.

Basic Qualifications:

  • US Citizen with at least an active Top Secret security clearance and the ability to obtain a SCI prior to your start date.
  • Bachelor’s degree with 4+ years of experience or a Master’s degree with 2+ years of experience. Additional years of experience will be accepted in lieu of a degree.
  • Must have a DoD 8140 Intermediate certification (Security+ CE or equivalent) (formerly DoD-8570 IAT Level 2 baseline certification).
  • Intermediate Azure Certifications such as AZ-104: Azure Administrator Associate or similar certifications from other Cloud Service Providers.
  • Proficiency in virtualization technologies, including VMware, Hyper-V, and OpenStack.
  • Proficiency in public cloud platforms such as AWS, Azure, Google Cloud (GCP), and Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI).
  • Hands-on experience with Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) tools like Terraform, Ansible, and CloudFormation.
  • Solid understanding of containerization (Docker) and orchestration platforms (Kubernetes).
  • Familiarity with monitoring tools (Prometheus, Grafana, etc.) and incident management.
  • Solid Understanding of networking concepts, including VPCs, subnets, VPNs, and firewalls.
  • Practical knowledge of DevSecOps principles, methodologies, and best practices.
  • Interest in continuous learning and professional development in cybersecurity and DevOps practices.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience with Air Force programs.
  • Experience with security tools and practices related to DevSecOps (e.g., SAST, DAST, IAST).
  • Experience with compliance standards (e.g., OWASP, NIST) and DoD regulations.
  • Expert cloud certifications such as Microsoft Certified: Azure Solutions Architect Expert or similar certification from another cloud provider.
  • Experience with Azure Stack Edge family of devices.
  • Experience with DoD networks, especially classified and operational networks.
  • Understanding of enterprise networking concepts, especially Virtual Private Networks (VPNs), tunneling, QoS, and cloud connectivity solutions (e.g. Azure Express Route).
  • Experience with Infrastructure as Code (IaC) and security automation.

post coverage, verifying officer readiness, and responding to incidents in real time. They serve as a direct supervisory presence for Protective Service Officers, ensuring adherence to post orders,
appearance standards, and operational procedures. As part of our layered supervisory model, PSO Supervisors provide essential oversight that reinforces continuity, compliance, and contract performance

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Conduct shift briefings, communicate operational updates, and reinforce site-specific protocols and safety priorities.

title: Material Program Manager
description:
Job Overview

The Material Program Manager is responsible for overseeing the procurement and supply of materials needed for a project or program, ensuring that materials are available on time, within budget, and according to quality standards.

Essential Functions

  • Develop and implement material strategies for specific projects or programs.
  • Collaborate with project teams to understand material requirements and timelines.
  • Create and maintain material delivery schedules, ensuring alignment with project milestones.
  • Identify, evaluate, and select suppliers based on quality, cost, and delivery performance.
  • Work closely with procurement teams to negotiate contracts and secure materials in a timely manner.
  • Establish strong relationships with suppliers and address any supply chain disruptions or issues.
  • Manage the material budget for the program, ensuring material costs stay within approved limits.
  • Identify cost-saving opportunities, including supplier negotiations and process improvements.
  • Track and report on material expenditures, variances, and forecasts.
  • Proactively identify risks related to material shortages, supplier disruptions, or market fluctuations.
  • Develop and implement risk mitigation strategies, including alternative sourcing and buffer stock planning.
  • Monitor supply chain performance to anticipate potential delays and adjust plans accordingly.
  • Collaborate with engineering, manufacturing, and project management teams to ensure material availability aligns with production schedules.
  • Facilitate communication between internal teams and suppliers to address material issues and drive resolutions.
  • Work with quality assurance teams to ensure materials meet the required specifications and standards.
  • Implement and track key performance indicators (KPIs) related to supplier on-time delivery, and supplier performance.
  • Maintain accurate records of material orders, deliveries, and costs.
  • Provide regular status updates to program leadership on material availability, risks, and costs.
  • Ensure compliance with regulatory and contractual obligations for material management
  • Perform other duties as required.

Standard Essential Functions

  • Regular and reliable attendance on a full time basis [or in accordance with posted schedule].
  • Responsible for exhibiting professional behavior with both internal and external business associates that reflects positively on the company and is consistent with the company's policies and practices.
  • Embodies AEVEX’s cultural values and aligns daily actions with department goals and company culture.

Qualifications and Competencies

  • Strong knowledge of procurement processes, supplier management, and material logistics.
  • Excellent negotiation, communication, and interpersonal skills.
  • Proficiency in supply chain management software (e.g., Infor LN, SAP, Oracle, or similar ERP systems).
  • Ability to manage budgets, timelines, and competing priorities.
  • Strong problem-solving and risk management skills.
  • Skilled at analyzing data to inform decision-making and optimize material flow.
  • Ability to track complex material schedules and manage multiple suppliers simultaneously.
  • Able to quickly respond to changes in material requirements, production schedules, or supplier issues.

Education / Certifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain Management, Business, Engineering, or a related field.

Experience

  • 10+ Experience in Aerospace manufacturing operations; defense contract manufacturing experience preferred
  • Global supply chain experience preferred.
  • Proven experience in developing, negotiating, and closing subcontracts with large spend (greater than $500,000 USD) suppliers.
  • Experience with sourcing and managing the following commodity suppliers.
  • Composites (mid to high volume)
  • Aerospace wing, fuselage, and flight surface composite manufacturing experience a plus
  • Small gasoline engine propulsion - Aerospace
  • Electric, Electronic and Electro-mechanical components; established relationships with key franchised distributors including Arrow, Avnet, TTI, etc.

AEVEX, headquartered in Solana Beach, California, supports the U.S. national security mission and partner nation needs around the world by providing full-spectrum aviation, remote sensing, and analysis solutions. title: Global Material Planning Manager
description:
About us

AB InBev is the leading global brewer and one of the world’s top 5 consumer product companies. With over 500 beer brands, we’re number one or two in many of the world’s top beer markets, including North America, Latin America, Europe, Asia, and Africa.

Purpose of the job

The Global Material Planning Manager is a critical role within the Global Supply Chain Planning organization. The role owns the global Material Planning framework and 1YP Budgeting and Tactical Planning process. The position connects long-term supply chain strategy with monthly tactical decisions and operational execution, ensuring material requirements, supplier capacity, inventory, allocation and financial trade-offs are integrated into one feasible plan.

The role will partner with Zone and BU Planning teams, Global and Regional Procurement, Supply Network Planning, Supply Chain Design, Finance, Vertical Operations, Technology and Product teams. It will define global standards, drive digital adoption and lead the performance agenda across packaging, raw materials and vertically supplied materials.

Key Responsibilities:

Global Material Planning ownership

  • Act as the global process owner for end-to-end Material Planning, defining the vision, operating model, standards, governance, roles and roadmap across all Zones and BUs.
  • Lead the global Material Planning community, coach Zone and BU leaders, share best practices and improve capability through LCP and other benchmarking mechanisms.

1YP Budgeting and Tactical Planning

  • Own the global 1YP Budgeting and Tactical Material Planning process, Planning in the o9 Planning system, translating approved demand and network assumptions into a 12-18 month material 1YP.
  • Define the annual planning calendar, inputs, scenarios, review gates and handshakes connecting Budget, Latest Estimate, Tactical SNP and Zone material plans.

Supplier collaboration and risk management

  • Define the global Supplier S&OP standard for critical suppliers, including capacity validation, commitment tracking, risk escalation and mitigation follow-up.
  • Partner with Procurement to improve supplier segmentation and allocation, balancing unit cost with flexibility, inventory, freight, service and total end-to-end value.

Performance, value and continuous improvement

  • Own the global KPI framework for Material Planning and Tactical MRP, including planning accuracy, supplier demand attainment, allocation efficiency, inventory, service and process adherence.
  • Create transparent global performance views, benchmark Zones and convert insights into prioritized improvement actions.

Technology, data and transformation

  • Act as global business process owner for Material Planning capabilities in o9 and connected planning solutions.
  • Drive adoption of standardized, exception-based and increasingly touchless planning

Skills, Experiences and Capabilities

  • A university degree or advanced qualification in Supply Chain, Engineering, Operations Research, Business, Finance or a related discipline.
  • Approximately 7-10 years of professional experience in supply chain planning, material planning, supply network planning, procurement planning or integrated business planning.
  • Strong knowledge of MRP, tactical planning, S&OP/IBP, supplier capacity planning, inventory and allocation processes in a complex manufacturing or FMCG environment.
  • Experience leading annual budgeting or 1YP planning cycles and translating volume plans into operational and financial implications.
  • Hands-on experience with advanced planning technology such as o9, SAP IBP, SAP APO or similar platforms; strong curiosity about planning logic and data.
  • Ability to build scenarios, quantify trade-offs and convert complex operational issues into clear management decisions.
  • Proven leadership of cross-functional transformation programs across multiple markets, cultures and organizational levels.
  • Strong stakeholder management and communication skills, with the ability to influence senior leaders, local teams, Procurement, Technology and external partners.
  • Professional fluency in English.
  • An ownership mindset: you take results personally, act with accountability and transparency, and maintain a strong bias for action.

What success looks like:

  • One global Material Planning operating model with clear ownership, governance and standard handshakes across planning horizons.
  • A credible 1YP and rolling tactical material plan that is supply-feasible, financially transparent and used for decision-making.
  • Earlier visibility of material constraints and stronger supplier commitments, with risks resolved before they reach execution.
  • Improved material availability, allocation efficiency, inventory and working-capital performance.
  • Higher adoption of o9 and standardized planning processes, with less manual work and stronger scenario-based decisions.

What you can expect from us:

We're about more than just credentials. At AB InBev and in our Global Supply Chain team, we want people who believe in our culture, our values and Dreaming Big. Brewing the world's most loved beers and creating meaningful experiences is what inspires us. We are owners, empowered to lead real change, deliver on tough challenges and take accountability for the results.

We are looking for talent that shares these values: ambitious, bold and resilient. We want talent looking for fast career growth, cross-functional experiences, global exposure and robust training and development.

Title: Software Engineer - Monterrey

John Deere is a foremost leader in the ag equipment business, and we continue to put a solid stamp on other industries. For over 185 years, the company's portfolio of groundbreaking products has grown to include industries related to and outside of agriculture, including Turf, Construction and Forestry and Wind Technologies. The image of John Deere is no longer that of a signature green tractor meandering across a field; it's been replaced with an image of acceleration, swift progress, and innovative leaping toward the company's 200th year. The product line alone serves as proof with advances in machine performance, equipment automation, fleet management, and John Deere's ongoing investment in emerging markets.

_Note: All candidates should have their tax situation certificate (Constancia de Siituación Fiscal) up to date with the salary regime to be eligible for the hiring process_.

Main Resposibilites
  • Embedded software engineers in this space contribute high-quality, secure, and innovative solutions for enabling global telematics on an embedded development scrum team.
  • Develop and test high-quality software features in C++ on embedded controllers in a Linux environment
  • Investigate embedded software issues and implement sustainable solutions
  • Collaborate with system engineers, architects, and cross-functional teams to define requirements, analyze potential impacts, and drive for results
  • Operate on an Agile scrum team on a variety of features with direction from technical leads.
What Skills You Need
  • Expertise in embedded software development.
  • Expertise in C++ or similar language.
  • Ability to analyze complex systems, identify issues, and implement sustainable solutions.
  • Communication and collaboration skills on a diverse, distributed team.
What Makes You Stand Out
  • Knowledge of scripting languages (Python, Bash, CMake, etc.) .
  • Experience in a Linux environment.
  • Experience with real-time, embedded, multithreaded systems.
  • Understanding of wireless communications (Cellular, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth).
  • Experience in Agile software development processes.
  • Exposure to Internet of Things (IoT) and telematics.
  • Ability to learn quickly, adapt, and communicate cross-functionally.
Education
  • Mechatronics, Computer Science, Information Systems or similar Engineering Degree.

This position will be posted for a minimum of 10 business days and unposted when a qualified pool of candidates is achieved.

Candidates must have the necessary work permits to work in the country.

About Carrier

Carrier Global Corporation, global leader in intelligent climate and energy solutions, is committed to creating innovations that bring comfort, safety and sustainability to life. Through cutting-edge advancements in climate solutions such as temperature control, air quality and transportation, we improve lives, empower critical industries and ensure the safe transport of food, life-saving medicines and more. Since inventing modern air conditioning in 1902, we lead with purpose: enhancing the lives we live and the world we share. We continue to lead because of our world-class, inclusive workforce that puts the customer at the center of everything we do.

About the role

An Embedded Java Software Developer is responsible for designing, developing, and maintaining Java-based firmware solutions for embedded systems. This individual will work on all aspects of Java-centric embedded firmware, focusing on the interaction between the software and hardware components of the system.

In this role, you will be involved in key phases of development, from project planning and implementation to testing and deployment, ensuring that the embedded firmware meets the performance and functional requirements of our products. You will also contribute to advancing our product offerings and supporting legacy firmware systems by providing expert-level product knowledge.

Key Responsibilities
  • Develop and maintain Java-based embedded firmware solutions using Agile methodologies.
  • Write and maintain Java firmware that interacts with low-level hardware components (e.g., sensors, actuators, communication protocols).
  • Participate in project planning by investigating solutions to embedded system challenges and providing accurate estimates.
  • Collaborate with hardware and systems engineering teams to ensure smooth integration of firmware with embedded hardware components.
  • Ensure that the embedded firmware meets timing and performance requirements.
  • Use test-driven development (TDD) methodologies to write unit and functional tests, ensuring firmware quality and reliability.
  • Debug and resolve hardware/firmware interaction issues using diagnostic tools and methodologies.
  • Assist in sustaining and upgrading legacy embedded firmware products, offering consultation and product expertise.
  • Explore and implement new technologies and methodologies for embedded systems, including power management, memory optimization, and low-level driver interaction.
  • Maintain documentation related to embedded firmware development, processes, and troubleshooting guides.
Requirements
  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering or Electrical Engineering
  • 3-5 years of hands-on experience in embedded systems and Java
Other skills needed
  • Certifications or coursework related to embedded systems development is a plus.
  • Experience with deployment of Java-based applications on embedded systems.
  • Familiarity with Java platforms designed for constrained devices.
  • Experience maintaining embedded firmware across distributed devices.
  • Knowledge of safety-critical or mission-critical embedded software development
  • Strong Java programming skills. Experience in embedded Java applications preferred.
  • Experience with embedded Linux or RTOS environments.
  • Experience with Test-Driven Development (TDD) and unit/functional testing for embedded systems.
  • Familiarity with Java-based memory management, garbage collection tuning, and optimization in resource-constrained environments.
  • Familiarity with ensuring that firmware meets timing and performance requirements.
  • Experience with Gradle, Maven, or other Java build systems.
  • Understanding of embedded system design
  • Familiarity with debugging tools (e.g., JTAG, oscilloscopes) and Linux-based diagnostic tools (e.g., dmesg, strace).
  • Experience working in an Agile/Scrum development process.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • Analytical and logical reasoning skills.
  • Problem-solving skills and attention to detail.
  • Ability to multi-task and stay organized in a dynamic environment.
Preferred Qualifications
  • Experience with design and development of large-scale distributed applications.
  • Experience with Kubernetes and containerized applications.
  • Experience with Grafana/Plutono, Solr, OpenSearch.
  • Exposure to Telecom / Cable

title: Sanctions Technology Application Lead
description:
JOB DESCRIPTION

At Citizens, we invest in the people who design and deliver innovative technology solutions that protect our customers and the financial system. As Sanctions Technology Application Lead, you will be responsible for the strategic direction, engineering oversight, and operational stability of the bank’s Sanctions screening systems.

This role covers Sanctions screening capabilities leveraging platforms such as FircoSoft, LexisNexis Bridger and other related technologies. You will lead modernization initiatives, AI automation and integration of advanced technologies such as microservices, event-driven architectures and screening optimization and intelligent alert prioritization.

Key Responsibilities:

Platform Strategy & Engineering

· Lead design, configuration, and delivery of Sanctions platforms across AWS cloud and SaaS

· Hands-on experience implementing technical solutions for sanctions screening systems.

· Ability to diagnose and resolve product and environment issues, apply hotfixes and product patches, and manage production incident resolution to ensure system stability.

· Drive modernization, automation, and optimization of Sanctions processes using containerization (Docker/Kubernetes), CI/CD pipelines, and DevOps practices.

· Experience in automating functional testing.

· Own the technical roadmap and lifecycle management for Firco and LexisNexis Bridger, including upgrades, rule and list configuration, integrations, performance, resilience, and end-of-life planning.

· Design and maintain real-time and batch screening services for payments, customers, counterparties, and messages, with traceable decisioning and reliable downstream alert handling.

Cloud & SaaS Integration

· Manage application deployment, hosting, and integration within AWS cloud, including real and batch data ingestion, controls and monitoring.

· Oversee integration with SaaS vendor environments ensuring compliance with internal security and cloud policies.

· Implement API-first architecture, Kafka-based event streaming, and microservices for real-time alerting and data ingestion.

Regulatory Alignment & Risk Management

· Ensure systems comply with Sanctions requirements.

· Implement audit, logging, and control frameworks aligned with regulatory expectations, and internal risk policies.

· Lead remediation initiatives for regulatory exams, audits, and compliance testing.

· Translate sanctions policy and regulatory requirements into screening rules, list-management controls, testing evidence, and auditable technology procedures.

Data, Screening & Operational Excellence

· Oversee inbound/outbound data flows for customer profiles, transactions, sanctions screening requests, match results, alerts, and dispositions.

· Partner with Sanctions Operations to reduce false positives and improve detection accuracy.

· Leverage AI/ML models for alert prioritization, and sanctions screening optimization.

· Establish data-quality controls, reconciliation, lineage, and alert completeness checks across source systems, screening engines, and case-management handoffs.

Stakeholder & Vendor Engagement

· Act as primary technology liaison for Sanctions vendors (Firco, LexisNexis, etc.).

· Manage cross-functional relationships with Compliance, Operations, InfoSec, Enterprise Architecture, and Cloud Engineering.

· Influence strategic discussions for future sanctions capabilities, product upgrades, and roadmap alignment.

Governance, Controls & Performance

· Establish SLAs, KPIs, and monitoring dashboards for screening uptime, throughput, and processing timeliness.

· Oversee change management, release management, and production stability.

· Manage issue resolution, incident response, and root cause analysis.

· Define and test high-availability, disaster-recovery, capacity, and failover requirements for sanctions screening services supporting time-critical payment flows.

Team Leadership

· Lead a team of application engineers, analysts, and integration specialists supporting sanctions platforms.

· Mentor, coach, and grow talent in financial crimes technology discipline.

· Foster a culture of accountability, innovation, and operational excellence.

Required Qualifications:

· 7 plus years of experience in Sanctions or Financial Crimes technology

· Hands-on experience with FircoSoft, LexisNexis Bridger or equivalent sanctions screening tools.

· Strong technical experience with:

· AWS cloud environment (EC2, S3, Lambda, RDS)

· SaaS integrations and vendor-hosted models

· APIs, microservices, ETL, batch pipelines

· Good understanding of sanctions regulations, lists, alerts, screening logic, and tuning.

· Working knowledge of OFAC and other major sanctions regimes, screening-control evidence, model or rule validation, and regulatory-exam support.

· Experience working with Compliance, Regulatory, Risk, InfoSec, and Audit stakeholders.

· Background in large banking or financial institutions strongly preferred.

Preferred Skills:

· Knowledge of Payments (ACH, Wire, SWIFT), Customer/Transaction screening.

· Familiarity with monitoring tools.

· Experience managing large vendor relationships and multi-year product roadmaps.

· Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced environment.

· Experience with AI/ML-based screening enhancements and automation.

Hours & Work Schedule

  • Hours per Week: 40
  • Work Schedule: Monday - Friday

Pay Transparency

The salary range for this position is $133,000 - $174,000 per year, plus an opportunity to earn an annual discretionary bonus. Actual pay is based on various factors including but not limited to the budget, work location, relevant skills, and experience.

We offer competitive pay, comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage, retirement benefits, maternity and paternity leave, flexible work arrangements, education reimbursement, wellness programs, and more. Citizens’ paid time off policy exceeds the mandatory paid sick or paid time away policies of local and state jurisdictions in the United States. For an overview of our benefits, visit our Careers site - https://jobs.citizensbank.com/benefits

title: Quantum Information Research Scientist
description:
Description

Leidos has a new and exciting opportunity for a Quantum Information Research Scientist in our INTEL Sector's Cyber & Analytics Business Area (CABA). Our talented team is at the forefront in Security Engineering, Computer Network Operations (CNO), Mission Software, Analytical Methods and Modeling, Signals Intelligence (SIGINT), and Cryptographic Key Management. At Leidos, we offer competitive benefits, including Paid Time Off, 11 paid Holidays, 401K with a 6% company match and immediate vesting, Flexible Schedules, Discounted Stock Purchase Plans, Technical Upskilling, Education and Training Support, Parental Paid Leave, and much more. Join us and make a difference in National Security!


The technical team will be developing a variety of sensing and communications demonstration systems for the customer. In addition to team supervision, the Scientist will also be tasked with participating in R&D along with various program development tasks.


Responsibilities will include supervising and participation in the building and testing of quantum-based communications and sensing systems along with collaborating with sub-contractor partners.

  • Expertise in optical systems is not required but basic familiarity with optics is preferred.
  • The position may require short periods of travel within the US., primarily to other Leidos facilities in DC and Huntsville, AL.
  • Potential employee should be comfortable communicating technical work, both orally and written to subject matter experts and non-technical audiences.
  • Familiarity with proposal processes and white paper writing is a plus.
  • Good communications skills are vital as the employee will be regularly presenting complex material to non-technical governmental and military audiences.
  • Provide regular updates to the group lead in Huntsville, AL.

Required Qualifications:

  • Must hold a BS, MS or PhD in physics, optics, quantum information science (QIS), or some related engineering field with 2+ years of experience.
  • Candidate must be proficient with physical quantum mechanical systems used in sensing or communications applications.
  • Must be able to obtain a TS/SCI security clearance.
  • Work location is in Lawton, OK
  • Must be a US Citizen and be able to obtain and maintain a TS/SCI security clearance

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Expertise in an applicable field of quantum physics/QIS, either theoretical or experimental.
  • Familiarity with Python, Matlab, Mathematica, LabVIEW, C#, or any optical modeling program.
  • Experience in the theory and design of experimental quantum systems for sensing/communications applications.
  • Experience in setting up lab equipment for optical and quantum experiments.
