title: Medi-Cal Navigation Specialist
description:
Title: Medi-Cal Navigation Specialist

Reports to: CalAIM Director

FLSA Status: Non-Exempt

Position Status: Regular, Part Time, Hourly

Wage Range: $30 per hour

Effective Date: November 2026 ending on or before November 1, 2028

Location: Hybrid; The person in this position works primarily from an approved home office with occasional work in the field at different worksites in Orange County.

Schedule: 30 hours per week.

Position Summary

Under the direct supervision of the CalAIM Director, the Administrative Coordinator provides high-level administrative, operational, logistical, and program support to maintain smooth workflows. This position supports leadership by managing schedules, travel, and communications; and facilitates program-related logistics, data & compliance tracking, and contract support. The role demands initiative, discretion in maintaining confidentiality, and excellent communication and organizational skills, particularly in supporting a variety of teams and external relationships.


Essential Functions, Duties, and Responsibilities

Healthcare Enrollment and Navigation

  • Provide information and assistance regarding healthcare coverage programs, including Medi-Cal, Covered California, Medi-Cal Access Program (MCAP), county health programs, and other public benefit programs.
    Assist members with applications, renewals, redeterminations, and enrollment processes.
  • Troubleshoot eligibility and enrollment issues and provide follow-up support to ensure successful enrollment and retention of benefits.
  • Support OC Team with troubleshooting and strategies
  • Support in creating tools and enhancing Medi-Cal Enrollment process
  • Conduct member calls.
  • Assist members with reporting changes related to income, employment, household composition, address, and contact information.
  • Support members with annual Medi-Cal renewals and required documentation submissions.
  • Assist members in creating and navigating online benefits accounts and healthcare service portals.
  • Educate members about healthcare coverage options, benefits, provider networks, and available services.
  • Assist members with selecting or changing primary care providers, medical groups, and health plans.

Case Management and Member Advocacy

  • Conduct intake assessments to identify healthcare, behavioral health, and social service needs.
  • Provide ongoing case management services, including care coordination, service planning, referrals, and follow-up support.
  • Conduct case reviews to monitor member progress, identify barriers, and evaluate outcomes.
  • Advocate for members to address barriers related to healthcare access, transportation, housing, food security, and other social determinants of health.
  • Coordinate services with healthcare providers, community organizations, managed care plans, and government agencies.
  • Support members in accessing preventive care, specialty care, behavioral health services, and community resources.

Health Education and Community Outreach

  • Conduct outreach activities to engage underserved, uninsured, and underinsured populations.
  • Provide culturally and linguistically appropriate health education and healthcare navigation services.
  • Facilitate health education workshops, presentations, enrollment events, and community-based outreach programs.
  • Promote awareness of healthcare coverage programs, preventive services, and available community resources.
  • Attend community events, health fairs, and resource fairs to educate and enroll community members.
  • Build and maintain collaborative partnerships with healthcare providers, schools, community-based organizations, faith-based organizations, and local agencies.

Community Health Program Coordination

  • Coordinate and support community health initiatives to improve access to care and health outcomes.
  • Ensure efficient delivery of services and timely follow-up with program participants.
  • Manage scheduling, outreach activities, member follow-up, and community engagement efforts.
  • Monitor program participation and assist with implementation of outreach and enrollment strategies.
  • Support quality improvement activities and recommend process enhancements to improve member outcomes.

Financial Assistance and Resource Navigation

  • Assist members with hospital financial assistance applications and programs designed to reduce medical debt.
  • Help members understand healthcare costs and available financial assistance resources.
  • Connect members to food assistance, housing resources, transportation services, utility assistance programs, and other community supports.
  • Maintain knowledge of local community resources and referral networks.

Documentation and Compliance

  • Maintain accurate and timely documentation of all member interactions, assessments, referrals, and services provided.
  • Enter and update member information in electronic health record systems, case management platforms, and reporting databases.
  • Collect demographic, household, employment, and income information necessary for eligibility determinations.
  • Track enrollment outcomes, referrals, case activity, and program performance metrics.
  • Ensure compliance with HIPAA, confidentiality requirements, and program regulations.

Compliance and Goal-Meeting

  • Consistently meet all assigned productivity and outcome goals
  • Prepare reports and assist with program data collection and evaluation activities.
  • In all activities, comply with all contracts, funder requirements, and VyC procedures and policies.
  • Meet or exceed all goals and requirements established by the CalAIM Director for this position.

Addtional Duties

  • Respond to member inquiries and provide customer service in person, by phone, and electronically.
    Schedule, confirm, and reschedule appointments.
    Complete data entry, filing, record maintenance, and other administrative tasks.
  • Participate in staff meetings, trainings, professional development activities, and organizational initiatives.
  • Work with vendors, contractors, and consultants to achieve departmental goals, as required and available
  • Provide administrative support related to assigned enrollment, navigation, and outreach activities as requested.
  • Other duties as assigned.

The duties listed here are typical examples of the work performed; not all duties assigned are included, nor is it expected that all similar positions will be assigned every duty.


Required Competencies

Education/Experience

  • High School Diploma or equivalent required.
  • A minimum of two (2) years of experience in Medi-Cal enrollment, healthcare navigation, public benefits programs, case management, community outreach, or related healthcare services.
  • A minimum of two (2) years of progressively responsible administrative experience.
  • Experience working with diverse and underserved populations.

Demonstrated experience maintaining accurate records, using databases or case management systems, and organizing member follow-up.

Skills

  • Ability to collaborate closely and across all VyC departments with a wide range of staff, community members, partner agencies, and funders.
  • Strong interpersonal, communication, and customer service skills.
  • Strong attention to detail, organizational abilities, and effective establishment of priorities.
  • Ability to handle sensitive matters with discretion, maintain a high level of confidentiality, and comply with HIPAA regulations.
  • Strong problem-solving and critical-thinking abilities.
  • Demonstrated initiative and a proactive approach to tasks.
  • Ability to organize and maintain member records, track pending actions and deadlines, and use office and case management systems effectively.
  • Ability to accurately review household and income information, perform basic calculations needed for applications, and identify missing or inconsistent information.
  • Ability to independently manage an assigned caseload with minimal supervision, exercise judgment within established procedures, work as part of a team, and recognize when to seek guidance.
  • Proficiency in the principles and methods of office management and modern office procedures, systems, and equipment.
  • Adaptable and reliable in the face of conflict, crisis, or changing priorities.
  • Ability to calculate figures and amounts, including discounts, interest, commissions, proportions, percentages, area, circumference, and volume.
  • Ability to work independently with minimal direct instruction, both individually and as part of a team.
  • Knowledge of Medi-Cal, Covered California, BenefitsCal, and other health and human services programs.
  • Skilled in recognizing the impact of trauma and delivering compassionate, person-centered services that promote safety, trust, empowerment, and resilience.

Language Skills

  • Demonstrated exceptional verbal and written communication skills, both virtual and in-person.
  • Ability to speak effectively to various audiences, including grantors, grantees, members of the public, or employees of the organization.
  • Strong proofreading skills.
  • Ability to read, analyze, interpret, and summarize documents such as safety rules, operating and maintenance instructions, general reports, procedures, or regulations.
  • Ability to complete reports and write business correspondence.
  • Ability to effectively present information and respond to questions from individuals, groups, and the general public.

Computer Skills

  • Proficiency in utilizing technology to navigate community members through the health system as needed.
  • Computer skills for the purpose of data entry during enrollment events, sending and receiving email, and calendar scheduling.
  • Comfort using and learning new technology.
  • Proficiency in Google Suite, Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, PowerPoint), Google Chrome or other widely used and supported Internet browsers, and Zoom or telecommunication software.
  • Proficiency with social media platforms like Facebook, Facebook Messenger, Instagram, and WhatsApp.

Certificates, Licenses, and Registrations

  • Valid Driver’s License or the ability to utilize a reliable alternative method of transportation when needed to carry out job-related essential functions.
  • Valid automobile liability insurance is required if driving.
  • CHW certificate (within 18mo of start date). CHWs must complete a minimum of six hours of additional relevant training annually
  • CPR certification (must be complete within 2 months of hire)
  • Mandated Reporter Training certification (must be completed within 2 weeks of hire)


Preferred Competencies - Nice to Have

    • Bi-lingual in English and Spanish.
    • Experience facilitating workshops, community presentations, and health education activities.
    • Knowledge of managed care plans, healthcare systems, and community resource networks


    Physical and Mental Demands

    • Must be able to
      • remain in a stationary position up to 75% of the time.
      • move about in multiple work environments up to 25% of the time.
      • detect incoming visitors, recognize stakeholders, and inspect printed paperwork.
      • reason logically and make sound decisions, to consider alternative and diverse perspectives, to communicate effectively both orally and in writing, to remain poised under all circumstances, and to interact effectively with people in a positive manner that engenders confidence and trust.
      • multitask without loss of efficiency or accuracy, including the ability to perform multiple duties from multiple sources.
      • work and sustain attention with distractions and/or interruptions.
      • maintain regular attendance and be punctual.
      • understand, remember and follow verbal and written instructions.
      • complete assigned tasks without direct supervision.
      • exercise independent judgment and make decisions.
      • perform under stress and/or in times of urgency.
      • perform in situations requiring speed, deadlines, or productivity quotas.
    • Constantly operates a computer, smartphone, and other office productivity machinery, such as a calculator, copy machine, and computer printer.
    • Frequently communicates with community members, colleagues, community partners, and other stakeholders. Must be able to exchange accurate information in these situations.
    • Occasionally moves about inside the office to access file cabinets, office machinery, etc.
    • Occasionally works in outdoor weather conditions.

    The physical demands described here are representative of those that an employee must meet to perform the essential functions of this job successfully. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of the job.

      • This job operates primarily in a professional home office environment, with occasional work “in the field” travelling to local offices, community centers, or similar environments.
      • The noise level in these various work environments is typically quiet to moderate.

title: ITP Senior Network Engineer
description:
Description

The Digital Sector at Leidos currently has an opening for a ITP Senior Network Engineer supporting the HEITS Contract as part of the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) Insider Threat Program (ITP). This is an exciting opportunity to use your experience to support, sustain, design and evolve the network enterprise of the ITP. The ITP mission is to identify insider threats to the department by utilizing advanced analytics, monitoring, and data correlation which in turn help address and eliminate potential threat actors from compromising the DHS mission in safeguarding the homeland.


The selected candidate will be responsible for the following:


  • Support the ITP network infrastructure, perform all routine maintenance activities, provide guidance on upgrades and system recapitalization, perform availability/capacity management.
  • Oversee High Speed Guard Cross Domain solution that supports the transfer of data between multiple classification domains.
  • Support all documentation to effectively capture the configuration baseline.
  • Design and support system recapitalization plans to account for capacity growth and changes as directed by the customer.
  • Serve as the subject matter expert on all ITP network infrastructure.

Basic Qualifications:

  • Bachelors degree 12-15 years of prior relevant experience. Additional education and experience may be considered in lieu of a degree
  • Cisco Certified Network Professional (CCNP)
  • Engineering, Deployment and operations of LAN and WAN Switches, and Firewalls ensuring seamless integration into existing network infrastructure
  • Working knowledge of defense-in-depth principles, network/HW/SW security architecture, network topology, IT device integrity, and common security elements

description:
National Security Government Relations Leader

The Opportunity:

Booz Allen is seeking a National Security Government Relations Leader to join our government relations team in a registered lobbyist role, supporting our national security business and defense technology portfolio.

This is a leadership role on our government relations team. The individual will be the external spokesperson and internal proponent of a multi-year government relations strategy to help grow our national security business by achieving legislative, engagement, and thought leadership outcomes and through building relationships with key stakeholders. The successful candidate will possess a strong understanding of Congress, the defense authorization process, military services, the intelligence community, and national security policy. An exceptional candidate will further understand the evolving landscape in defense acquisition policy and have experience with the evolving defense technology landscape and related policy issues.

We need a collaborative leader committed to excellence in government relations who values their role in fostering a high-performing government relations function. The successful candidate will embrace teamwork and thrive in a collaborative environment. They must possess the executive presence to collaborate with senior business leaders in the development of lobbying, eminence, and thought leadership strategies. The role will require intellectual curiosity, strong business acumen, continuous learning, sound judgment, and a willingness to engage differing perspectives.

What You'll Work On:

  • Own and evolve the company's government relations strategy for national security policy, defense technology, space, and military modernization.
  • Lead our annual strategy to ensure the company is shaping key issues in the defense authorization cycle and defense appropriations process.
  • Build and sustain a strong network of relationships with national security policymakers in Congress and the executive branch, involving senior executives to advance goals.
  • Serve as the principal government relations advisor to our national security business leadership, providing sound political counsel on the reputational, business, and policy risks arising from the evolving defense policy and budget landscape.
  • Partner closely with legal and our national security business to navigate shifts in acquisition policy and advocate for outcomes favorable to the company.
  • Prepare and support business leaders at external defense policy forums, conferences, and meetings with senior elected officials and administration policymakers.
  • Deliver timely analysis of legislative, budgetary, and policy developments affecting the defense and national security market, translating implications for business leadership.
  • Collaborate with colleagues in media, strategic communications, and engagement teams to raise the company's profile at major events and identify moments where the company can shape the policy debate.
  • Participate in the planning and execution of our Political Action Committee strategy.

Join us. The world can’t wait.

description:
Overview

Job Summary

Galapagos Federal Systems LLC is seeking an Information Technology Specialist Level 2 to support mission-critical IT systems and infrastructure within a secure Department of Defense (DoD) environment. This role supports secure enterprise technologies, network infrastructure, and operational IT systems essential to mission success.

The selected candidate will assist with the installation, configuration, maintenance, and sustainment of enterprise hardware, software, servers, and network infrastructure across physical and virtual environments. The ideal candidate is a proactive technical professional capable of troubleshooting complex issues, supporting end users, and maintaining secure and reliable IT operations in fast-paced environments.

Responsibilities include supporting Windows and Linux operating systems, VMware and Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization platforms, and enterprise Microsoft services including Active Directory, Group Policy, DNS, DHCP, DFS, SQL Server, and Azure. Additional duties include system monitoring, cybersecurity compliance support, backup and recovery operations, CAC authentication support, and troubleshooting hardware, software, network, and peripheral systems.

The position also supports LAN connectivity, network cabling, switches, routers, printers, telephones, UPS systems, and Video Teleconference (VTC) systems, as well as IT equipment installation, relocation, accountability, sanitization, and disposal activities in accordance with DoD security policies and procedures.

Key Responsibilities

The Information Technology Specialist will:

  • Support IT systems, technical programs, projects, and operational tasks requiring advanced technical oversight and coordination
  • Perform day-to-day IT operations to ensure system availability, performance, reliability, and compliance
  • Coordinate with internal teams, customers, and stakeholders to ensure system requirements and project milestones are achieved
  • Maintain and administer networked and standalone servers, workstations, user accounts, network access, security monitoring systems, and system documentation
  • Analyze, troubleshoot, and resolve hardware, software, network, and system anomalies to maintain operational effectiveness
  • Research, evaluate, and recommend system enhancements, emerging technologies, and IT solutions to improve mission performance
  • Administer and support virtualized environments and enterprise services supporting mission operations
  • Provide end-user and client technical support, including account provisioning, modification, and deactivation activities
  • Identify Automated Information System (AIS) vulnerabilities and implement appropriate security countermeasures and remediation actions
  • Ensure AIS and network infrastructure are operated, maintained, sanitized, and disposed of in accordance with applicable security policies and procedures
  • Support Video Teleconference (VTC) systems, including scheduling, configuration, troubleshooting, and administration as required

Requirements

Skills and Experience

The Information Technology Specialist must have:

  • Active Top-Secret clearance with eligibility for Sensitive Compartmented Information (TS/SCI) access
  • Minimum of 6 years of relevant Department of Defense (DoD) IT systems and operations experience
  • Minimum of 2 years of experience supporting SAP and/or SCI environments within the past five (5) years
  • Demonstrated experience supporting enterprise IT systems within secure, mission-critical environments
  • Strong analytical, troubleshooting, and problem-solving capabilities across complex IT environments
  • Experience supporting servers, workstations, virtualization platforms, network infrastructure, and enterprise services
  • Ability to communicate technical concepts effectively to leadership, customers, and non-technical stakeholders
  • Proven ability to prioritize workloads, manage competing tasks, and operate independently with minimal supervision

Education and Certifications

The Information Technology Specialist must meet the following:

Required

  • Bachelor's degree in computer science, Information Technology (IT), or related discipline

Must be a U.S. Citizen. A high-level Department of Defense active security clearance is/may be required. Applicants selected will be subject to a security investigation and may need to meet eligibility requirements for access to government information.

Physical Requirements

Work may involve sitting or standing for extended periods of time and typing and reading from a computer screen. The candidate must have enough mobility, including bending, reaching, and kneeling, to complete daily duties in a prompt and efficient manner, and that may include lifting up to thirty pounds, as necessary.

title: Technical Environment Manager
description:
Job#: 3054935

Job Description:

Apex Systems is a world-class technology services business that incorporates industry insights and experience to deliver solutions that fulfill our clients’ digital visions.


Apex has an opportunity for a Technical Environment Manager. For applicants who are interested in this opportunity, send your updated resume to Gabriel Ortega, Account Manager, at [email protected].


Here are the details:

Position: BEST Technical Environment Manager

Location: 1 Ashburton Place, Boston, MA 02108 (Hybrid)

Duration: Thru 6/30/27 (with possibility of extension)

Pay Rate: $90-$96/hour


Detailed Description of Services:


About the Office of the Comptroller

The Office of the Comptroller of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts (CTR) is an independent and apolitical agency charged with overseeing the Commonwealth’s financial systems, preparing the annual financial reporting, and managing the external single audit process. In fiscal year 2021 CTR oversaw approximately $95 billion in spending. In addition, CTR oversees the Commonwealth’s General Ledger, payroll and vendor management, trains state employees on risk mitigation and operates the Commonwealth’s financial system.


As stewards of the public trust, CTR aspires to inspire confidence by maintaining our core principles: clarity, integrity, and accountability. The powers and obligations of the Office of the Comptroller are generally dictated by M.G.L. c. 7A.


About Business Enterprise Systems Transformation (BEST) Program

The Commonwealth of Massachusetts is undertaking a multi-year project known as the Business Enterprise Systems Transformation (BEST) Program to implement a comprehensive Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) software solution that will support a wide range of business functions used by all state agencies. The initial scope of the project replaced the Commonwealth’s core financial and accounting system.


Phase 2 will replace the Commonwealth’s HR and Payroll solution (HR/CMS). This phase is projected to span a 2-year period. A software solution and Systems Implementation (SI) vendor have been selected. The solution is a SaaS cloud-based system, replacing the existing heavily customized software currently hosted on-premises, whether on virtual or physical servers, and supports more than 95,000 employees.


The BEST Program is jointly sponsored by the Secretary for Administration and Finance, the Comptroller of the Commonwealth, the Secretary of Technology Services and Security, and the Chief Human Resources Officer of the Human Resources Division. This job posting is being issued through the Office of the Comptroller.


Learn more at: https://best.macomptroller.org/


Position Summary

The BEST Technical Environment Manager will work for the BEST Deputy Program Manager and Solution Technical Lead to support the adoption of the future state Human Resource and Payroll system. Together with the BEST PMO, and BEST Program Operations Lead, and BEST Phase 2 Technical Lead, BEST Phase 2 Risk and Compliance Lead, Product Vendor, Systems Integrator (SI), Office of the Comptroller, and Executive Office of Technology Services and Security (EOTSS) staff to deploy technical configurations and manage the status of data to meet the evolving needs of BEST project throughout the project duration. Each environment will have specific data, end-user security, integration, and configuration needs.


The BEST Technical Environment Manager will be a part of the BEST Technical Implementation team and work closely with the other members of the BEST functional and Comptroller’s Risk and Compliance teams to develop and implement a comprehensive environment management solution. This includes:

  • Support security policies, processes and standards related to end user roles and data access for application users.
  • Provide operational support for the BEST team, product vendors, and CMW users, during the project.
  • Provide necessary reporting and information about each environment.
  • Support and oversee proper access to each non-production and production environment that will be needed to implement the new Human Resource Management and Payroll solution.

The BEST Technical Environment Manager is responsible for defining the standards, protocols, procedures, tools, and resources required to manage program’s technical environments during the project and prepare the environments for the on-going operations of the new Human Resource and Payroll solution. This role involves collaboration with a diverse team, including the System Integrator (SI) and product vendor, BEST Phase 2 Technical Lead, BEST Risk and Compliance Lead, and BEST Program Technical Operations Lead, EOTSS Operations, and others. The focus will be particularly on the SaaS software procured for this engagement. The BEST Technical Environment Manager will make recommendations based on the SI and product vendor’s maintenance and support standards and procedures, best practices, and Commonwealth business needs to maintain the new solution.


Specific Duties

The specific duties for the BEST Technical Environment Manager role, includes:

The roles and responsibilities of the SI, product vendor, and other Commonwealth staff regarding systems operation will be clearly identified in coordination with the Environment Manager, including such as:

  • Manage and support the overall configuration of each environment in coordination with SI and Vendor, including but not limited to:
    • User access status
    • Data status
    • Solution functional configuration – high level
    • Integration solution status
    • Monitoring SI and product vendor operational protocols and mitigation of identified issues.
    • Manage timing and procedures for software upgrades and configuration updates
    • Monitor performance of the infrastructure hosting solution
    • Oversee Service Level Agreement (SLA) metrics for SaaS operations and support/maintenance services.
  • Manage and support the detail configuration of each environment aligned with program business, testing, and technical needs
    • Functions specific configuration and version
    • Batch jobs supporting daily and other timing requirements
    • Assisting in management of end user security.
    • Support on-going and new configuration tasks.
  • Designing and implementing a cross-system monitoring solution, including Cloud SaaS vendor, legacy on-premises vendor solutions, EOTSS responsible services, and other tasks that support the management of the end state business solution.
  • Work with Commonwealth and BEST teams to implement, monitor status, and operational performance of connected Commonwealth integrated “touch points” appropriate for each environment, including but not limited to:
    • CIW (data warehouse)
    • Single Sign on (SSO)
    • Mobius (reporting)
    • Time Reporting System(s)
    • PrintShop
    • MOVEit (file sharing tool)
    • Oversee and align typical operational support tasks such as data backups, application and network performance monitoring, and data, etc.
  • Provide regular written communications on
    • Reporting Environment status
    • Coordination issues with CMW touchpoints, SI, Product vendor, Agencies, or other
    • Provide regular status updates and status reports on the condition of each environment and it’s future plans.
  • Ensure quality and effectiveness of operational documentation.
  • Assist all phases and cycles of testing, including end-to-end testing, user acceptance testing, payroll parallel testing, and pre go live operational solution testing.
  • Assist execution of “tabletop” operational reviews of end-to-end go live operational processes.
  • Oversee on-going systems training for system administrators and operational support staff.
  • Define protocols and tools to troubleshoot the system to maintain operational integrity and security.
  • Coordination of efforts with SI and product vendor for upgrades and routine maintenance.
  • Manage, oversee, and communicate the data refreshes into the various environments
  • Participate in the BEST Program Maintenance and Operations Workstream to enable the future state operational solution, transitioning existing roles and responsibilities to agreed future business solution delivery model. This includes but not limited to:
    • Provide advise on operational processes for business and IT
    • Identify gaps in future state on-going operations
    • Define regular / monthly maintenance functions
    • Alignment of CMW managed components with Workday solution
    • Identify best practices and recommend procedures and organizational structures for overseeing the day-to-day running of the new Human Resource and Payroll solution.
    • Align with SI and product vendor and Commonwealth on roles and responsibilities for on-going systems maintenance tasks such as upgrades and defect fixes by the product vendor, and SLA reporting.
    • Recommend procedures and tools for ensuring that the system delivers consistently on the Service Level Agreement (SLA).
    • Recommend additional operational “unofficial” metrics, that simplify business and IT operational support functions.
    • Recommend procedures and tools for troubleshooting software issues, applying patches, dealing with exceptions, and escalating problems in meeting SLAs.
    • Recommend procedures for managing future upgrades.
    • Support program technical workstreams, including: data conversion, integration, security, data oversight, and other as defined by BEST technical leadership.
    • Work with the BEST Risk and Compliance Lead to recommend procedures for monitoring vendor data security protocols.
    • Align with CTR, BEST, and EOTSS on disaster recovery testing and documentation approach by the product SaaS vendor and risk mitigation steps that the Commonwealth and the SI and product vendor could undertake to ensure business continuity and data security.
    • Work with the BEST Risk and Compliance Lead to
      • recommend procedures for provisioning end user security.
      • ensure that compliance requirements are implemented as necessary
    • Participate in the generation of detailed operational procedures and processes that will operate across multiple delivery partner environments and teams.

Required Skills

  • Experience in technical configurations, technologies, and processing environments in one or more projects of similar size and complexity to BEST.
  • Experience with system administration and monitoring for various application platforms particularly SaaS delivery models.
  • Demonstrated experience at leading root-cause analysis (RCA) document creation and work with other administrators or integration developers to drive resolution.
  • Experience with all phases of large program system implementation, including requirements definition, Testing: unit, system, integration, parallel, user acceptance, Go live conversion, and post go live on going operations.
  • Experienced with LAN/WAN/VPN and remote network technologies and protocols (such as, but not limited to, TCP/IP, HTTP, FTP, Ethernet, token ring, ARCNET, HTML CGI, ATM, CDPD) routers, hubs, and servers.
  • Experience at learning new technologies and vendor solutions and applying past experience to understand complexity and potential risks quickly.
  • Excellent customer service attitude.
  • Demonstrated written and verbal communication and interpersonal skills.
  • Experience with Agile based operations.
  • Demonstrated ability to work across multiple operational delivery partners and ensure quality and compliance to enable a business solution.
  • Demonstrated experience in working in a 24 X 7 operational environment and business solution.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in designing and implementing Human Resource and Payroll based applications.
  • Exposure to implementing end user security protocols in a large public or private sector entity comparable in size to the Commonwealth.
  • Exposure with WorkDay Human Resource and Payroll solution, with an additional preference of implementation within a government agency.
  • Exposure with WorkDay Prism data and reporting solution.
  • Exposure with WorkDay user security management as a member of a business (non-IT) team.

title: CHW Program Manager
description:
Job Title: CHW Program Manager

Department: Community Wellness

Reports To: Senior Director of Community Wellness

FLSA Status: Non-Exempt

Work Schedule: Monday – Friday 9:00 am to 5:00 pm

Pay Range: $28.00 - 39.00 hourly

Overview:

Share provides a wide range of services including street outreach, hunger response, emergency shelter, housing, and asset building to help people experiencing poverty, hunger, and homelessness move toward stability, housing, and self-sufficiency.

Our employees are at the heart of this work. Every role contributes essential skills, knowledge, and expertise to our mission and makes a meaningful difference in the lives of the people we serve. At Share, we value the unique strengths and potential each person brings, and we are committed to a workplace grounded in collaboration, inclusivity, growth, and opportunity.

If you are looking for meaningful work where your skills can make a real difference, we invite you to join our mission-driven team. Share offers a generous benefits package, including four weeks of PTO, a wellness program, a 401(k) with employer match, and health, dental, and life insurance.

DEI Statement:

Share wants to be part of a community that brings about change. We are committed to actively working to dismantle racist systems, focusing on sustainable solutions to structural racism, police violence, and inequitable economic, health care, and education systems. It requires all institutions, including ours, to ask what more we can and should do to live our commitments to diversity, equity, and inclusion – and we must be brave enough to make changes.

EEO Statement :

We value and are actively seeking to create a diverse work environment because teams are stronger with different perspectives and experiences. We encourage women, people of color, LGBTQIA+ individuals, people with disabilities, members of ethnic minorities, foreign-born residents, older members of society, and others from minority groups and diverse backgrounds to apply.

We do not discriminate on the basis of race, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sex, religion, color, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status. All employees and contractors of Share are responsible for maintaining a work culture free from discrimination and harassment by treating others with kindness and respect.

Job Summary:

Community Health Workers (CHWs) serve as frontline public health workers who have a close understanding of the communities they serve. Their role is to facilitate access to health and social services, improve service delivery quality and cultural competence, and build individual and community capacity through education, support, and advocacy.

The CHW Program Manager will provide leadership, supervision, and direct service within Share’s Community Health Worker programs. The position will oversee two distinct contracts, including the SWACH program and the PeaceHealth program, each with unique program expectations, service settings, referral processes, documentation requirements, and deliverables. The Program Manager will ensure that services are delivered consistently and effectively across both contracts while maintaining flexibility to meet the needs of each program and the communities they serve.

Essential Functions:

Supervision and Staff Engagement – 50%

  • Provide direct supervision of CHW staff across the SWACH and PeaceHealth contracts, including task assignments, case consultation, meeting facilitation, coaching, performance feedback, and documentation as required.
  • Conduct regular individual and team supervision and provide guidance related to complex client needs, case management, care coordination, professional boundaries, and program expectations.
  • Review, approve, and sign off on staff case notes and other required documentation to ensure accuracy, completeness, timeliness, and compliance with program standards.
  • Monitor staff caseloads and assignments and distribute referrals and workload appropriately based on program requirements, staff capacity, client needs, and contract expectations.
  • Maintain an individual caseload and provide direct CHW services, including client engagement, assessment, resource navigation, care coordination, follow-up, and documentation.
  • Support staff in managing complex cases and provide consultation when additional intervention, coordination, or problem-solving is needed.
  • Complete employee performance evaluations and participate in goal setting and professional development planning.
  • Address performance concerns, workplace conflicts, attendance issues, and other staff-related concerns in coordination with the Senior Director of Community Wellness and Director of People and Culture as appropriate.
  • Support recruitment, onboarding, orientation, training, and ongoing development of CHW staff.
  • Ensure staff understand and consistently follow Share’s internal policies, professional standards, and confidentiality requirements.
  • Provide leadership and decision-making support for the Community Wellness Department in the absence of the Senior Director of Community Wellness, as assigned.
  • Facilitate communication and coordination between community-based CHW staff, PeaceHealth hospital-based staff, Share program leadership, and external partners.
  • Model trauma-informed, culturally responsive, and person-centered engagement with clients, staff, healthcare providers, and community partners.

Contract and Program Oversight – 25%

  • Use Share’s equity lens as new policies are developed and implemented.
  • Oversee the day-to-day implementation of the SWACH and PeaceHealth contracts and ensure services are delivered in accordance with each contract’s scope of work, performance expectations, and reporting requirements.
  • Monitor contract deliverables, performance measures, and program outcomes and identify gaps or barriers to meeting contractual expectations in collaboration with the Senior Director of Community Wellness.
  • Ensure required documentation, referrals, client contacts, and service activities are completed accurately and in accordance with contractual requirements.
  • Review program data to identify trends, service gaps, quality concerns, and opportunities for improvement in collaboration with the Senior Director of Community Wellness.
  • Prepare and provide regular program updates and performance reports to the Senior Director of Community Wellness.
  • Participate in meetings with SWACH, PeaceHealth, funders, healthcare partners, community organizations, and other stakeholders as needed.
  • Maintain effective working relationships with PeaceHealth staff and support CHWs in navigating hospital-based workflows, communication processes, and program expectations.
  • Ensure program operations and staff activities remain aligned with applicable healthcare, privacy, confidentiality, and contractual requirements.
  • Assist with development and implementation of program goals, work plans, policies, procedures, workflows, and quality improvement initiatives.
  • Keep current with laws, regulations and best practices that impact people experiencing homelessness and that are related to supported housing programs.

Administrative Support – 25%

  • Coordinate daily CHW program operations across community-based and hospital-based settings and ensure teams are equipped and supported to meet program expectations.
  • Serve as a liaison between CHW staff and program leadership, communicating operational needs, client concerns, staffing issues, and program updates.
  • Monitor program capacity and make recommendations to program leadership as needed.
  • Support the development and maintenance of systems for tracking referrals, client engagement, caseloads, outcomes, and contract deliverables.
  • Ensure accurate and timely completion of required program reports to funders.
  • Assist with monitoring program spending and ensure expenditures are consistent with approved budgets and contract requirements, as assigned.
  • Identify operational barriers and develop or recommend changes to improve program efficiency, service delivery, communication, and participant outcomes.
  • Support coordination of required training, meetings, and program activities across both contracts.
  • Promote collaboration and problem-solving with healthcare providers, social service agencies, community organizations, and other external partners.
  • Perform related duties as assigned.

Required Knowledge/Skills/Abilities:

  • Bachelor’s degree in public health, social work, healthcare, human services, behavioral health, or a related field, with at least three (3) years of relevant professional experience; OR five (5) years of relevant professional experience in a related field.
  • Previous experience supervising, leading, or managing staff.
  • Experience working within healthcare, clinics, or community-based organizations.
  • Ability to manage programs with multiple contracts, grants, or funding sources.
  • Knowledge of Housing First philosophy, injury prevention, trauma-informed care, and the challenges faced by individuals experiencing homelessness and complex health and social needs.
  • Strong relationship-building skills and the ability to engage diverse populations, individuals with persistent mental illness, substance use disorders, homelessness, and complex health and social needs.
  • Ability to provide crisis intervention, clear direction, constructive feedback, and appropriate accountability while maintaining supportive relationships with staff and clients.
  • Ability to supervise staff, review documentation for accuracy, quality, and compliance.
  • Awareness of and respect for cultural differences and health disparities.
  • Basic computer skills, including proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite or Google Workspace.
  • Ability to maintain confidentiality and comply with applicable privacy requirements, organizational policies, and hospital standards.
  • Valid driver’s license when necessary to fulfill community-based program responsibilities.
  • Ability to complete and maintain applicable PeaceHealth hospital requirements, including badging, background checks, drug screening, vaccinations, and other requirements for hospital-based staff.

Preferred Knowledge/Skills/Abilities:

  • Master’s degree in public health, social work, healthcare, human services, behavioral health, or related field preferred.
  • Experience working with hospital systems, clinics, and community-based partnerships.
  • Experience with electronic health record (EHR) systems, data entry, and clinical documentation.
  • Experience with hospital-based care coordination and interdisciplinary healthcare teams.
  • Experience with program development, quality improvement, contract compliance, grant reporting, and developing or implementing program policies, procedures, and workflows.
  • Knowledge of HIPAA requirements and healthcare confidentiality practices.
  • Certification as a Community Health Worker (CHW).
  • Bilingual proficiency

What we offer:

  • Mission driven work, focused on success for those we serve as well as the success of our staff.
  • Kaiser Medical & Vision plans, Guardian Dental, Life Insurance and Employee Assistance Program, WEX FSA and HRA, Wellness Plan worth up to $900 per year, and a 401 K plan with a 4% match.
  • Opportunities for personal advancement, robust trainings, and a People & Culture Newsletter to keep you informed.
  • We also support several employee-led committees focused on building connections, fostering inclusion, and strengthening our workplace culture in support of Share’s mission.

Special Requirements:

Potential new hires will require a background check, which will include:

  • Valid Driver’s License/ Motor Vehicle record
  • Criminal Background History
  • Sex Offender Registry
  • OFCCP Registry
  • Drug Screening
  • Health Screening (proof of vaccinations)
  • PeaceHealth Orientation and Quiz
  • Confidentiality Agreement
  • Badge Agreement

title: Senior Data Scientist
description:
Teamwork makes the stream work.

Roku is changing how the world watches TV

Roku is the #1 TV streaming platform in the U.S., Canada, and Mexico, and we've set our sights on powering every television in the world. Roku pioneered streaming to the TV. Our mission is to be the TV streaming platform that connects the entire TV ecosystem. We connect consumers to the content they love, enable content publishers to build and monetize large audiences, and provide advertisers unique capabilities to engage consumers.

From your first day at Roku, you'll make a valuable - and valued - contribution. We're a fast-growing public company where no one is a bystander. We offer you the opportunity to delight millions of TV streamers around the world while gaining meaningful experience across a variety of disciplines.

What you'll be doing

  • Develop data visualizations and self-serve dashboards that illustrate complex platform phenomena using Looker and Tableau.
  • Build dashboards and ensure their performance through maintaining data pipelines, translate answers to strategic questions into data visualizations.
  • Develop and maintain data processing and reporting pipelines using Airflow, SQL, and Python.
  • Build data processing pipelines to process upstream data to facilitate business facing reporting needs.
  • Write SQL queries to process data catalogue and develop Python code to manage Airflow DAGs.
  • Conduct statistical analyses to understand the results and provide recommendations from A/B tests.
  • Conduct rigorous analyses using tools SQL, R, Python, and Excel to identify areas of opportunity for the business and understand user behavior.
  • Develop A/B test designs, factoring statistical power, testing capabilities/limitations, and decisioning needs.
  • Conduct analysis in spreadsheet tools and document test results.
  • Translate business needs into actionable analytics questions and datasets of key metrics.
  • Conduct statistical analysis of user behaviors to drive marketing efforts.
  • Explore the immense data catalogue at Roku to generate appropriate and actionable proxies for difficult to measure concepts/behaviors.
  • Develop log, fact, dim and agg tables. Work cross-functionally, including with Data Engineers to identify database gaps.

You are required to have

  • Master’s degree or foreign equivalent in Data Science, Analytics or related field.
  • Will also accept a Bachelor’s degree or foreign equivalent in Data Science, Analytics or related field plus 3 years experience in position or related occupation.
  • Must have prior experience, internship, coursework or project background in the following:
    1. SQL and Big Data Processing and Analysis
    2. Coding in R or Python
    3. A/B Test Design and Analysis
    4. Hypothesis testing and Statistical Analysis
    5. Data visualization and data storytelling including Tableau and Looker

Up to one day per week telecommuting may be permitted.

For California Only - The annual salary for this position is between $148,750 - $208,250.

Compensation packages are based on factors unique to each candidate, including but not limited to skill set, certifications, and specific geographical location.

This role is eligible for health insurance, equity awards, life insurance, disability benefits, parental leave, wellness benefits, and paid time off.

#LI-DNI

What's Roku's approach to hybrid working?

Roku fosters an inclusive and collaborative environment where teams generally work in the office Monday through Thursday. Fridays are generally flexible for remote work, except for employees whose specific roles or assigned office location require five days' a week attendance.

What are some of the benefits?

Roku is committed to offering a diverse range of benefits as part of our compensation package to support our employees and their families. Our comprehensive benefits include global access to mental health and financial wellness support and resources. Local benefits include statutory and voluntary benefits which may include healthcare (medical, dental, and vision), life, accident, disability, commuter, and retirement options (401(k)/pension). Employees are supported in taking time off, in accordance with local leave policies and other personal needs to support their evolving work and life needs. It's important to note that not every benefit is available in all locations or for every role. For details specific to your location, please consult with your recruiter.

Accommodations

Roku welcomes applicants of all backgrounds and provides reasonable accommodations and adjustments in accordance with applicable law. If you require reasonable accommodation at any point in the hiring process, please direct your inquiries to EmployeeRelations@Roku.com.

What should I know about Roku's culture?

Roku is a great place for people who want to work in a fast-paced environment where everyone is focused on the company's success rather than their own. We try to surround ourselves with people who are great at their jobs, who are easy to work with, and who keep their egos in check. We appreciate a sense of humor. We believe a fewer number of very talented folks can do more for less cost than a larger number of less talented teams. We're independent thinkers with big ideas who act boldly, move fast and accomplish extraordinary things through collaboration and trust. In short, at Roku you'll be part of a company that's changing how the world watches TV.

We have a unique culture that we are proud of. We think of ourselves primarily as problem-solvers, which itself is a two-part idea. We come up with the solution, but the solution isn't real until it is built and delivered to the customer. That penchant for action gives us a pragmatic approach to innovation, one that has served us well since 2002.

title: Senior Software Engineer
description:
Job brief

Our client, a well-funded, early-stage startup revolutionizing B2B payments, is looking for a Software Development Engineer to join their Platform team as a key technical contributor. The successful candidate will design, build, and maintain the core systems — including Spring Boot microservices, a Spring Boot BFF, and Kubernetes-based cloud infrastructure — that power secure, scalable payment processing for enterprise customers worldwide. They will own backend services and APIs, drive integrations with banking partners, and mentor other engineers while helping shape the platform architecture.

Responsibilities

  • Own and evolve the platform's core architecture, including service boundaries, data models, and the shared libraries and infrastructure other teams build on.
  • Design and implement secure, well-documented backend services and REST APIs, shaping API contracts and OpenAPI specifications.
  • Design database schemas, caching strategies, and event-driven, message-based workflows that keep high-volume transaction processing consistent, performant, and resilient.
  • Champion system reliability and security across the platform, including monitoring, alerting, error handling, data encryption, and secure API design that meets the standards of a regulated financial environment.
  • Build and maintain secure, scalable integrations with major financial institutions and payment networks, translating complex banking protocols into robust, reusable platform capabilities.
  • Implement high-volume transaction processing systems with the accuracy, idempotency, and auditability that financial operations require.
  • Partner with Product, Architecture, and Engineering teams to translate business requirements into platform solutions, drive technical decisions, and advocate for reliability and security in architectural discussions.
  • Mentor mid-level and junior engineers on backend best practices, code quality, system design, and platform engineering principles.
  • Lead code reviews, establish coding standards, and help shape engineering culture as the team grows.

Requirements

  • 7+ years of software engineering experience with a strong focus on backend and distributed systems.
  • Expert proficiency in Java and the Spring framework (Spring Boot), with a track record of building complex, high-scale backend systems.
  • Deep experience designing and building microservices and REST APIs, including OpenAPI-driven contracts and generated clients.
  • Hands-on experience with containerization and orchestration (Docker, Kubernetes) and cloud platforms (AWS, GCP, or Azure).
  • Strong system design skills across distributed systems, including database design, caching strategies, and message queues or event-driven architectures.
  • Solid understanding of authentication and security best practices (OAuth2/OIDC, data encryption, secure API design) in a financial services context.
  • Proven ability to debug complex issues, optimize performance, and architect solutions for high-scale, high-availability systems.
  • Strong proficiency with modern AI coding assistants (e.g., Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, or similar), with a track record of using them to boost engineering speed, quality, and impact.
  • Excellent communication skills and experience collaborating in cross-functional agile teams.
  • Professional fluency in English (written and verbal); all engineering collaboration, documentation, code reviews, and stakeholder communication are conducted in English.

Nice to have

  • Experience with real-time payment systems or high-frequency transaction processing.
  • Knowledge of banking APIs, SWIFT messaging, or ACH processing.
  • Experience with event-driven architectures and stream processing.
  • Background in fintech, payment processing, or B2B financial platforms.
  • Familiarity with enterprise DevOps practices and infrastructure as code.
  • Experience building multi-tenant SaaS applications with organization-scoped data access.
  • A track record of leading backend architecture decisions and establishing engineering standards.

What's on offer

  • Foundational technology ownership — they'll own core platform services that process millions in B2B payments, directly powering how enterprise customers manage counterparties, execute payments, and maintain compliance.
  • A real technical voice — their opinions on service architecture, API contracts, and data design will directly shape how the stack is built; this is a role that defines systems, not just maintains them.
  • A modern stack — a thoughtfully chosen technology stack that values simplicity and pragmatism over hype, with new tools adopted where they add real value.
  • Early-stage impact — a well-funded startup where their contributions will shape both the product and the engineering culture from the ground up.
  • An AI-forward culture — AI is embraced as a tool for innovation and efficiency, with curious, adaptable engineers welcome to bring it into their work.
  • A strong, growing team — a diverse team, including engineers from SAP and fintech innovators, who value technical excellence, continuous learning, and work-life balance.

Recurrent Training Instructors (RTIs) are responsible for training Federal Flight Deck Officers in the use of weapons and self-defense tactics to defend the cockpits of commercial aircraft.

HOW Recurrent Training Instructors (RTIs) WILL MAKE AN IMPACT:

RTIs must be current or former federal, state, or local law enforcement agents/officers. RTIs must have the ability to provide subject matter expertise in each of the areas of instruction that comprise the Recurrent Training Program. EDUCATION / EQUIVALENT TRAINING:

RTIs must have successfully completed a recognized federal firearms instructor training program, or equivalent deemed acceptable by the TSA. Examples of a recognized federal firearms instructor program include certified instructor graduates of Federal Law Enforcement Training Center (FLETC), Firearms Instructor Training Program (FITP), FBI/DEA Firearms Instructor Training Program, and US Secret Service Firearms Instructor Training Program.

RTIs must have successfully completed a recognized law enforcement instructor development course such as the FLTEC Instructor Development Course (IDC) or the FAMS IDC.

RTIs must successfully complete an instructor qualification program (IQP), established by TSA/FAMS and will be responsible for achieving and maintaining specialized training knowledge in all required subject areas.

EXPERIENCE:

RTIs must have a minimum of 5 years of formal experience as an instructor in ALL of the following law enforcement disciplines: firearms, defensive tactics/measures, and use of force.

Employees will come into contact with ammunition, simunitions, and other potentially dangerous items. Employees will be required to handle weapons and ammunition in the course of their duties. Exposure to high volumes of noise due to the firing of weapons will occur and employees are required to wear hearing protection in the form of foam ear plugs as well as external hearing protection. Exposure to expelled gun-powder as a result of fired ammunition is expected, and the employees must wash hands after handling ammunition. description:
Join a Team Supporting Heat Networks Across Residential Developments Throughout the UK


Established in 2009, Insite Energy specialises in Heat and Cooling Networks (also known as communal energy or district heating schemes), providing metering, billing, installation, retrofit and maintenance services to residential developments across the UK.



Our Maintenance Team supports the day-to-day operation of these networks, covering everything from heat generation within the plant room through to the Heat Interface Units (HIUs), heat meters, PAYG devices and associated systems installed within residents' homes.



As a Gas Safe Heat Network Engineer, you'll play a key role in maintaining, commissioning, fault-finding and improving these systems, helping to ensure reliable and efficient service for both clients and residents.


Why Join Insite Energy?



At Insite Energy, you'll join a specialist team working within a growing area of the UK's energy sector.

What many engineers enjoy about this role is the variety. Rather than focusing on a single product or system, you'll work across commercial plant, communal heating infrastructure, domestic heating equipment, metering technology and PAYG systems. You'll be involved in installation, commissioning, maintenance and fault-finding activities, giving you broad exposure across the lifecycle of a heat network.


Our Maintenance Team works closely with colleagues across operations, metering, delivery and client services, as well as contractors, consultants and supply partners. With around 90 employees, we're large enough to operate nationally, but still small enough that people know one another, collaborate closely and have a direct impact on the service we deliver to clients and residents.


For engineers who enjoy technical variety, practical problem solving and being part of a supportive team, this is an opportunity to develop specialist expertise within an increasingly important part of the UK's energy infrastructure.


Where Do You Fit In?



As a Gas Safe Heat Network Engineer, you'll be responsible for the installation, maintenance and efficient operation of heat network equipment across a range of residential developments and construction projects.



Working closely with supply partners and internal teams, you'll carry out maintenance, repairs, commissioning activities and commercial gas safety checks, while supporting the ongoing performance of domestic and commercial heat networks.



The role combines planned maintenance, reactive fault-finding, installation work and technical problem-solving across both occupied residential properties and multi-million-pound construction developments.



What You'll Be Working On



You'll support and maintain a wide range of equipment including:

  • Boilers
  • Chillers
  • Fan coil units
  • Heat Interface Units (HIUs)
  • Pumps
  • Heat exchangers
  • Pressure vessels
  • Valves and two-port valves
  • Heat meters
  • PAYG devices
  • Metering systems
  • Low Temperature Hot Water (LTHW) systems
  • Chilled water systems


Key Responsibilities



  • Carry out responsive and planned maintenance of heating and cooling systems serving private and social housing developments.
  • Diagnose faults, undertake repairs and complete renewal works.
  • Conduct planned preventative maintenance activities.
  • Complete commercial gas safety inspections and checks.
  • Maintain boilers, pumps, heat exchangers, pressure vessels and associated plant equipment.
  • Service, maintain and replace Heat Interface Units (HIUs).
  • Install, replace and commission heat meters and PAYG metering equipment.
  • Maintain and support metering and billing infrastructure.
  • Use laptops and tablets to commission equipment, update records and maintain systems.
  • Troubleshoot technical issues and coordinate with contractors, consultants and other trades.
  • Conduct site surveys and support installation activities on new developments.
  • Represent Insite Energy professionally when working with clients, principal contractors and supply partners.
  • Support the ongoing operation and optimisation of domestic and commercial heat networks.
  • Assist with design, installation, maintenance and troubleshooting activities across communal heating systems.



What We're Looking For



Essential Qualifications:



  • Commercial & Domestic Gas Qualifications:
    COCN1, CIGA1, ICPN1, TPCP1/1A, CCN1, WAT1, CKR1, HTR1, CPA1 (with a minimum of six months remaining prior to renewal).
  • Plumbing and Heating Certification:
    NVQ Level 2 or higher in plumbing and heating is essential.
  • Experience:
    Knowledge of heating control systems and prior experience in service and maintenance environments, particularly within district/community heating schemes, large-scale plant rooms, or energy centres.
  • Industry Knowledge:
    Understanding of communal/district heating schemes and experience working within the service industry.


Desirable Qualifications and Experience:



  • NIC 18th edition in domestic wiring (or equivalent) preferred, but not required.
  • Smart Metering Experience: Previous experience with smart metering systems, RF networks, or similar field-based technologies is preferred.
  • SMSTS or SSSTS Health & Safety certification is desirable.

Additional Requirements:

  • Clear Driving Licence: A valid, clear UK driving licence.
  • DBS Clearance: Basic DBS clearance (Disclosure and Barring Service).
  • Work Eligibility: Must be eligible to work in the UK.
  • References: Two satisfactory professional references.
  • Must hold or be able to obtain a CSCS card.



Working Arrangements:

  • Field-based role.
  • Occasional visits to our London and Peterborough offices.
  • Travel across the UK required.
  • Occasional overnight stays away from home.
  • 37.5 hours per week - Monday to Friday, 09:00-17:30.


Benefits:


  • 25 days annual leave plus bank holidays.
  • Birthday leave.
  • 4% matched pension contribution.
  • Employee Assistance Programme (EAP).
  • Two paid Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) volunteering days each year.
  • Regular company social events, including Summer and Christmas celebrations.


About Insite

Established in 2009, Insite Energy is a dynamic, fast-growing company that provides services to heat network suppliers in the UK. The services provided include metering & billing of residential customers, the installation (and retrofit) of credit billed and pay-as-you-go equipment, and ongoing maintenance and management of the heat network schemes.


We pride ourselves on our commitment to working as one team to put the customer and client first, delivering a reliable, competitive, and professional service. With just over 90 current employees, we are small but mighty, delivering more by working together.

At Insite Energy, we embrace diversity and inclusion. We value all backgrounds, identities, and experiences. We're committed to providing equal opportunities for all and offering reasonable adjustments to ensure accessibility and inclusivity throughout the application process and in the workplace.

Community - Innovation - Excellence - Sustainability

title: Spacecraft Systems Responsible Engineer
description:
At Relativity Space, we’re building rockets to serve today’s needs and tomorrow’s breakthroughs. Our Terran R vehicle will deliver customer payloads to orbit, meeting the growing demand for launch capacity. But that’s just the start. Achieving commercial success with Terran R will unlock new opportunities to advance science, exploration, and innovation, pioneering progress that reaches beyond the known.

Joining Relativity means becoming part of something where autonomy, ownership, and impact exist at every level. Here, you're not just executing tasks; you're solving problems that haven’t been solved before, helping develop a rocket, a factory, and a business from the ground up. Whether you’re in propulsion, manufacturing, software, avionics, or a corporate function, you’ll collaborate across teams, shape decisions, and see your work come to life in record time. Relativity is a place where creativity and technical rigor go hand in hand, and your voice will help define the stories we’re writing together. Now is a unique moment in time where it’s early enough to leave your mark on the product, the process, and the culture, but far enough along that Terran R is tangible and picking up momentum. The most meaningful work of your career is waiting. Join us.

About the Team:

The Interplanetary Sciences Program was established to expand access to scientific exploration across our solar system. Its mission is to make planetary research faster, more affordable, and more capable than ever before by rethinking how science missions are designed, built, and operated. The program aims to enable scientists to send instruments to distant worlds without decades of development or prohibitive costs. By creating a sustainable model for interplanetary exploration, we are transforming space science from an occasional event into a continuous process of discovery that accelerates knowledge, broadens participation, and inspires the next generation of explorers.

About the Role:

The Interplanetary Sciences Program is developing a privately funded science mission to Mars targeted for 2028. This mission will map shallow subsurface ice and geology, characterize Martian weather, enable next generation onboard processing and communication, and demonstrate a new philanthropic public-private partnership model for space science.

As the Spacecraft Systems Responsible Engineer within the Interplanetary Sciences Program at Relativity Space, you will own the end-to-end definition, integration, and delivery of the spacecraft bus and its interaction with mission payloads. You will serve as the technical and programmatic focal point ensuring that spacecraft-level requirements, interfaces, and performance budgets (power, mass, thermal, comm, etc.) are properly defined, tracked, and met throughout the mission lifecycle.

You’ll collaborate across internal teams and with external spacecraft bus providers to ensure mission success, from design and procurement through integration, test, launch, and operations. This position blends systems engineering, vendor management, and hands-on mission execution, offering a high degree of ownership and impact.

About You:

  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, or a related technical discipline
  • 7+ years of experience in spacecraft or satellite systems engineering, integration, or mission design
  • Proven ability to manage complex systems multiple vendors and customers
  • Strong understanding of spacecraft subsystems (power, thermal, comms, ADCS, propulsion, etc.) and their interdependencies
  • Experience leading cross-functional teams through integration and test, launch campaigns, or mission operations
  • Excellent communication, negotiation, and leadership skills with the ability to interface across technical and programmatic boundaries

Nice to haves but not required:

  • Experience with end-to-end mission development, including payload-to-spacecraft integration
  • Familiarity with NASA or commercial spacecraft systems engineering processes in an applied / New-Space manner is a plus
  • Experience supporting launch and early operations of spacecraft missions
  • Prior work with deep-space or interplanetary spacecraft systems

Compensation is only one part of our total rewards package. Relativity Space offers competitive salary and equity, a generous PTO and sick leave policy, parental leave, an annual learning and development stipend, and more! To see some of the benefits & perks we offer, please visit here.

title: Member Rights and Benefits Consultant
description:
HealthPartners is hiring a Member Rights and Benefits Consultant. This position is responsible for understanding, investigating, presenting, resolving and effectuating the timely resolution of member grievances, dispute resolution process and/or appeals. The consultant may focus on thoroughly investigating member requests, supporting the formal complaint and appeal resolution process, mitigating risk by identifying compliance concerns and/or providing customer service and member education. The consultant makes sure that the outcome is fair, equitable and in alignment with all federal and state regulations and accreditation standards. Develop relationships with internal and external departments in order to effectively resolve member concerns. Each complaint must be documented clearly, thoroughly, timely and accurately on HealthPartners Customer Service System in order to ensure accurate tracking, reporting and outcomes.


ACCOUNTABILITIES:

The consultant may be responsible for any of the following responsibilities:

  • Investigate member concern and ensure that all necessary documents are compiled, reviewed and presented to appropriate decision maker.
  • Research, understand and ensure compliance with all federal, state, Medicare and Medicaid regulatory requirements and accreditation standards. Responsibilities also include ensuring HealthPartners policies match those of the appropriate regulatory agency.
  • Develop partnership with other areas such as legal, medical directors, medical policy, pharmacy, behavior health, government programs, etc., in order to work efficiently and effectively to resolve member concerns.
  • Communicate response to member or their authorized representatives and physician within internal and regulatory timeframes. Letter must include member friendly language (service recovery) and meet all federal and state requirements. Must use appropriate laws (federal, state) to support decision.
  • Advise and assist members in pursuing their appeal options.
  • Document complete complaint file. Each file must include accurate documentation of the complaint, timeliness and outcome. All files must comply with regulatory and organizational rules. Files are subject to subpoena and are used for reporting, audits and 2nd level appeals etc.
  • Prepare case file, support and present case for each complaint that involves a second level complaint. Second level review may include, Member Appeals Committee, State fair hearings, MAXIMUS, External Review etc.
  • Provide data for the quality assurance process to assist in identifying trends and areas where quality improvement strategies should be focused.
  • Accurately record complaint in HealthPartners Customer Service System. Provide necessary documentation for data collection effort used to analyze member concerns and to report on them to the Board of Directors, Minnesota Department of Health CMS, DHS, Medical Directors, Government Programs and other interested departments/agencies.
  • Provide information regarding the actions taken on specific cases to various departments.
  • Provide technical expertise to legal staff on actions taken in response to cases that are the subject of litigation or regulatory dispute.
  • Investigate and respond to regulatory agency inquiries, including the Minnesota Department of Health, Attorney General’s Office, Department of Human Services, Centers for Medicare and Medicaid, StratisHealth and the Minnesota Department of Commerce. Provide accurate and detailed information that represents HealthPartners’ policies, procedures and actions taken in response to specific member complaints.
  • Consultants work with various internal departments to develop and implement benefit changes, contract provisions and policies to ensure regulatory compliance and improved member satisfaction. Resource for member advocates such as Legal Aid, regulators and Ombudsman’s office.


The consultant may perform any of the following duties:

  1. Investigate and respond to written or oral member complaints. Complaints may be standard or expedited. Investigate information necessary to make a decision. Review information with the appropriate medical administrative department head and other concerned parties.
  2. Provide customer service to members, their representatives, and providers on the Medical Appeal Line.
  3. Assess Appeal Line calls and written complaints and appeals to determine the most appropriate process for handling and resolution to improve the member experience.
  4. In cases where the answer provided by Member Services is partially or wholly adverse to the member’s request, inform the member of options for further consideration. This may include the Board of Director’s Member Appeals Committee, written reconsideration, Minnesota Department of Health, Minnesota Department of Commerce, MAXIMUS, State fair hearing and Plan Administrator. Options vary depending on the contract.
  5. In cases where the complaint decision is in the member’s favor, ensure the decision is quickly and appropriately effectuated within regulatory timeframes.
  6. Participate with Member Services Supervisors in an internal complaint review committee.
  7. Consult with Member Services Representatives to provide advice concerning problem-solving specific issues and information regarding the complaint process.
  8. Participate in business continuity planning and implementation.
  9. Other duties as assigned by management.


REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS:

  • BA/BS or similar experience in a related field plus 2 years experience in a customer service position in a health related industry involving customer contract, problem resolution and written communication with customers.
  • Excellent oral and written communication skills. Ability to express ideas clearly. Ability to communicate HealthPartners policy and procedures.
  • Ability to understand and explain complex medical policies and services. This must include proficiency with medial terminology and ability to summarize medical records and reports.
  • Advanced problem solving and investigative skills, with the ability to develop creative solutions for complex problems. Willingness and ability to model outstanding customer service and service recovery.
  • Ability to identify problems, to do in-depth investigation, develop and assess alternative courses of action, and make sound and timely decisions. Ability to develop working relationships with a number of internal departments in order to resolve issues.
  • Ability to negotiate with members, internal departments or providers in difficult situations.
  • Proficient at a number of computer software programs.


PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Work experience in a managed-care setting involving significant contact with members and providers.
  • Professional writing experience beyond an educational setting.
  • Experience interpreting regulatory/statutory guidelines.
