title: Sr. Lead, Audience Insights & Analytics
description:
Teamwork makes the stream work.

Roku is changing how the world watches TV

Roku is the #1 TV streaming platform in the U.S., Canada, and Mexico, and we've set our sights on powering every television in the world. Roku pioneered streaming to the TV. Our mission is to be the TV streaming platform that connects the entire TV ecosystem. We connect consumers to the content they love, enable content publishers to build and monetize large audiences, and provide advertisers unique capabilities to engage consumers.

From your first day at Roku, you'll make a valuable - and valued - contribution. We're a fast-growing public company where no one is a bystander. We offer you the opportunity to delight millions of TV streamers around the world while gaining meaningful experience across a variety of disciplines.

What you'll be doing

  • Generate insights for major TV tentpole moments around viewership and shifts from linear to streaming. Analyze viewer flow and cross-app behavior around large-scale cultural and sports events to produce standardized, recurring readouts used across the advertising organization.
  • Identify opportunities to create new ad product packaging based on streaming behavior observed on platform.
  • Build segments of Roku users based on first-party platform signals (e.g., sports fans, viewing behavior, ad affinity) to be used for advertisement targeting and audience intelligence.
  • Profile consumers of different streaming apps, including audience demographics, channel overlap, advertisement affinity, and habitual usage. Provide deepdive audience insights to stakeholders across marketing and sales, based on demographic and behavioral data, to drive interest and adoption of Roku advertising.
  • Analyze consumer behavior across the streaming ecosystem and tell the macro state of streaming story via licenses to third-party measurement tools. Quantify Roku's scale and influence relative to individual streaming apps. Combine first-party behavioral and ads data with third-party dataset integration - including Nielsen, ComScore, or VideoAmp - to create benchmarks and competitive claims. Complementing this with 1P data will allow for analysis and quantification of Roku’s scale and influence relative to individual streaming apps at the macro level.

You are required to have

  • Master’s degree or foreign equivalent in Math, Computer Science, Business Analytics, Management, or related field.
  • 3 years of experience in the position or a related occupation.
  • Will accept a Bachelor’s or foreign equivalent in Math, Computer Science, Business Analytics, Management, or related field and 5 years of progressive experience in the position or a related occupation.
  • Must have at least 3 years of experience in each of the following:
    1. Big Data technologies and frameworks to process and analyze large datasets (billions of rows of data, daily), including data visualization, statistical analysis, relational database querying, and data cleansing.
    2. SQL, including common table expressions (CTEs), query optimization; and building aggregations/derived datasets to extract and shape first-party platform data.
    3. Python or R and visualization/business intelligence (BI) tools (Tableau or Looker) to deliver analyses, dashboards, and executive-ready materials.
    4. Combining first-party (IP) behavioral/ads data with third-party (3P) dataset integration, including at least one from the following: Nielsen, ComScore, or VideoAmp to create benchmarks, competitive claims, and subscription, acquisition, churn context in the media & entertainment industry.
    5. Building standardized metrics, benchmarks, and repeatable “playbooks” that scale insights across the M&E landscape – across streaming, linear, PVOD and theatrical lines of business.
    6. Leverage Data exploration and data mining techniques to identify and extract datasets from multiple internal and external sources.
    7. Apply data cleaning, data transformation, and statistical analysis using Microsoft Excel, including pivot tables, VLOOKUP, INDEX/MATCH, nested formulas, and conditional formatting.
    8. Utilizing data visualization to design charts, graphs, and dashboards that transform raw, varied datasets into clear, compelling narratives.
    9. Communicating findings through analytical storytelling, distilling technical insights into actionable recommendations for cross-functional teams in media strategy, content acquisition, and market analysis.
    10. Operating as insights lead across multiple cross-functional teams (e.g., Marketing, Product and Partner Growth) to drive alignment and adoption of insights across a vertical such as Media & Entertainment, or Enterprise equivalent.
    11. TV or streaming industry experience, including Nielsen (media measurement, consumer insights, advertising analytics and market research services), MMP partners like Kochava or Branch (analytics and reporting solutions) and MTA partners solutions like Appsflyer (marketing analytics and attribution).

Up to one day per week telecommuting may be permitted.

What's Roku's approach to hybrid working?

Roku fosters an inclusive and collaborative environment where teams generally work in the office Monday through Thursday. Fridays are generally flexible for remote work, except for employees whose specific roles or assigned office location require five days' a week attendance.

What are some of the benefits?

Roku is committed to offering a diverse range of benefits as part of our compensation package to support our employees and their families. Roku welcomes applicants of all backgrounds and provides reasonable accommodations and adjustments in accordance with applicable law. If you require reasonable accommodation at any point in the hiring process, please direct your inquiries to EmployeeRelations@Roku.com.

What should I know about Roku's culture?

Roku is a great place for people who want to work in a fast-paced environment where everyone is focused on the company's success rather than their own. We try to surround ourselves with people who are great at their jobs, who are easy to work with, and who keep their egos in check. We appreciate a sense of humor. We believe a fewer number of very talented folks can do more for less cost than a larger number of less talented teams. We're independent thinkers with big ideas who act boldly, move fast and accomplish extraordinary things through collaboration and trust. In short, at Roku you'll be part of a company that's changing how the world watches TV.

We have a unique culture that we are proud of. We think of ourselves primarily as problem-solvers, which itself is a two-part idea. We come up with the solution, but the solution isn't real until it is built and delivered to the customer. That penchant for action gives us a pragmatic approach to innovation, one that has served us well since 2002.

Leading a team of four designers and copywriters, you’ll combine creative flair with marketing and commercial understanding to build brand love, support revenue and enhance the customer experience. This is a hands-on leadership role, shaping creative direction while bringing your own design and artworking expertise to the team.


Day to day
• Lead, coach and develop our creative team, setting clear direction, managing workloads and supporting individual performance and growth.
• Turn business objectives and customer insight into compelling concepts, stories and creative across campaigns and channels.
• Set high standards for design and execution, reviewing work with a sharp eye for typography, layout, imagery and detail.
• Get hands-on with design and artworking, supporting complex briefs and helping the team meet deadlines.
• Guide creative agencies, providing brand and art direction to deliver consistently strong work.
• Present ideas through pitches, mood boards and storyboards, bringing stakeholders with you and securing approvals.
• Help evolve our brand, photography, video and tone of voice guidelines, exploring fresh approaches across platforms and markets.
• Partner with the Brand Content Manager on photography commissioning, art direction and asset selection, building a versatile bank of creative assets.

About you
You’re an experienced creative with a strong design eye, original ideas and a portfolio that shows outstanding craft. You know how to balance creative ambition with commercial priorities, and you’re as comfortable developing people as you are refining artwork.
You’ll bring:
• Practical design experience, with a strong portfolio demonstrating excellent typography, layout and visual judgement.
• Proven people management experience, setting creative direction, coaching talent and managing performance.
• Marketing and commercial understanding, with the ability to translate objectives into effective creative.
• Confidence building relationships, presenting ideas and constructively challenging feedback while protecting brand standards.
• Experience balancing multiple briefs, stakeholder needs and approval processes within a large organisation.
• Full working knowledge of Adobe InDesign, Illustrator and Photoshop.



Experience within an in-house creative team for a consumer brand is strongly preferred. A relevant design degree or equivalent professional experience is welcome, alongside motion design or editing skills.


Accessibility and inclusion
We’re committed to making our recruitment process accessible. If you need reasonable adjustments or additional support, you can let us know in your application.
If you’d prefer to speak to someone directly before or during your application, interview or assessment, please contact our recruitment team at recruitment@fly.virgin.com.
We know every role and candidate is different, so we’ll discuss the adjustments available for the role and at each stage of recruitment, and how best to support you.
At Virgin Atlantic, we’re proud to be an equal opportunities employer and welcome applications from everyone. Whatever your background, identity, experience or perspective, we’d love to hear from you.

title: Executive Director, Global Data and Analytics
description:
Revolution Medicines is a global, commercial-state oncology company dedicated to discovering, developing and delivering innovative medicines for patients with RAS-addicted cancers. Leveraging its differentiated RAS(ON) tri-complex inhibitor platform, the company is advancing a broad, integrated portfolio of oral RAS(ON) inhibitors designed to directly target the active, cancer-driving state of RAS. Founded on rigorous scientific inquiry and a willingness to challenge long-held assumptions, Revolution Medicines is committed to changing the trajectory of disease for patients with RAS-addicted cancers worldwide.

Our people are united by a shared way of working: follow the science, challenge assumptions, act with urgency and hold ourselves to a high standard of rigor—all in service of patients.

The Opportunity

Reporting to the Vice President, Global Analytics & Insights, the Executive Director, Global Data & Analytics will build and lead capabilities in disease and customer analytics, data governance, commercial data systems, portfolio analytics and reporting. The role will develop the team, tools and data foundations needed to support decisions from early development through commercialization across an expanding portfolio and geographic footprint.

This leader will partner with regional teams to identify shared needs, develop capabilities at global scale where this improves efficiency and impact, and facilitate support, reuse and knowledge sharing for capabilities built regionally. Working with Disease Area Insights, Forecasting and Information Systems, the Executive Director will translate business priorities into practical analytical solutions and trusted information for decision making. This position is based at our headquarters in Redwood City, CA.

Responsibilities:

  • Set the global Data & Analytics strategy and capability roadmap with regional partners and Information Systems. Identify unmet needs, prioritize investments and sequence development around business value, readiness and opportunities to create scale across disease areas and regions. Balance new capability development with capacity for ongoing delivery, maintenance and user support.

  • Build, coach and develop the Data & Analytics team and its leaders. Establish clear accountabilities, align resources with priorities and manage functional budgets, vendors and delivery.

  • Coordinate with regional analytics leaders to agree where global leads, jointly develops, supports or facilitates information sharing. Tailor support to local capabilities and needs, with clear ownership, funding, capacity and service expectations. Agree readiness criteria and continuity of support for transitions as capabilities evolve.

  • Develop shared analytical capabilities, reusable methods and tools where common needs justify global investment. Create forums and practical mechanisms to share regional innovations, expertise and lessons learned, enabling adaptation and adoption across markets.

  • Lead shared disease analytics capabilities and agreed analyses to understand patient populations, diagnosis and biomarker testing, treatment pathways, utilization and gaps in care. Integrate relevant data sources with regional expertise to inform disease area strategy, early product assessments, launch planning and lifecycle decisions.

  • Advance shared customer analytics methods, tools and specialist support to understand healthcare professional and account needs, behaviors and engagement. Partner with regional Analytics & Insights, Commercial and Commercial Excellence teams on segmentation, customer journeys and measurement of commercial activities. Agree ownership for each initiative, with regional teams leading market-specific application and recommendations unless otherwise agreed.

  • Provide analytical foundations, reusable methods and agreed analyses for portfolio assessments with Forecasting and Disease Area Insights, including overlapping populations, treatment patterns and product interactions. Supply inputs to Forecasting-led scenario quantification and Disease Area Insights-led commercial evidence assessments, contributing to the integrated A&I recommendation led by the Vice President, with transparent assumptions and limitations.

  • Lead the business approach to global performance reporting and dashboards with regional partners. Agree a core set of metrics and definitions, integrate regional inputs and validate outputs with the responsible teams before leadership reporting. Explain market differences and comparability limitations to give leadership a coherent view of disease, customer and portfolio performance.

  • Lead the commercial business contribution to data governance in partnership with Information Systems, regional teams and relevant enterprise functions. Agree data ownership, stewardship, quality standards, definitions, access and appropriate use within enterprise governance, reflecting local requirements and designated data owners’ accountabilities.

  • Define and coordinate business requirements and priorities for shared commercial data systems, integration and analytical platforms with regional teams. Partner with Information Systems, which leads technical architecture, delivery and operation under agreed governance. Evaluate reuse of effective regional solutions and agree migration or exceptions before connecting global and regional capabilities.

  • Coordinate data sourcing and vendor strategy across regions and functions with Procurement and relevant data owners. Assess coverage, quality, licensing and analytical suitability; agree funding and participation for shared investments while respecting market differences, regional contracting responsibilities and permitted use.

  • Evaluate and introduce advanced analytics, automation and AI where they address material business needs. Pilot approaches, validate outputs and scale effective solutions with appropriate oversight, adoption support and measurement of impact.

  • Partner with business leaders to translate questions into analytical plans and actionable recommendations. Establish quality assurance, documentation and training that strengthen analytical rigor, user adoption and informed interpretation of results. With regional teams and Commercial Excellence, develop shared approaches to testing and learning and evaluation of incremental commercial impact where feasible; incorporate findings into subsequent decisions.

  • Travel domestically and internationally as needed, typically up to 25–30%.

Required Skills, Experience and Education:

  • Bachelor’s degree in a quantitative, scientific, technology or business discipline and 15+ years of relevant biotechnology, pharmaceutical or consulting experience.

  • Experience leading teams and managers, developing talent and building data and analytics capabilities in a growing organization, including sustained adoption, operational support and measurable business value.

  • Oncology experience and strong understanding of pharmaceutical disease and customer analytics across development, launch and commercialization.

  • Experience developing and scaling new analytical capabilities, including translating business needs into roadmaps, prioritizing investments and driving adoption.

  • Experience coordinating global and regional teams with differing capabilities, balancing shared solutions with local needs and influencing without direct authority.

  • Expertise in healthcare and commercial data sources, analytical methods, performance measurement and reporting, including sound judgment about data quality and limitations.

  • Experience establishing data governance and partnering with technology teams on data integration, analytical platforms and commercial systems.

  • Strong business acumen and ability to communicate analytical findings, uncertainty and recommendations clearly to senior leadership and cross-functional partners.

Preferred Skills:

  • Advanced degree in analytics, data science, statistics, information systems or business.

  • Experience launching targeted oncology therapies globally and building capabilities across markets with different data availability and operating models.

  • Experience applying advanced analytics, AI and automation to pharmaceutical business questions and measuring the value of new capabilities.

title: Senior Design Manager in Corsham, Wiltshire
description:
Senior Design Manager | £80m Data Centre Development

£85,000 – £95,000 + Excellent Benefits Package
Spring Park, Corsham, Wiltshire
️ Data Centres | Mission Critical | Design & Build | Major Construction Projects

Walker & Sloan are working with an outstanding specialist construction contractor to recruit an experienced Senior Design Manager for a flagship £80 million data centre development at Spring Park, Corsham.

Our client is a highly respected design, construction and engineering business with over 40 years of specialist experience delivering technically complex projects across the Data Centre, Defence and Energy sectors.

With an exceptional reputation, established client relationships and an exciting pipeline of major developments, the business continues to strengthen its position within the rapidly expanding mission-critical construction market.

This appointment represents a fantastic opportunity to take a leading role in the design delivery of a significant, multi-stage data centre development, working alongside an experienced project leadership team.

For an ambitious Senior Design Manager looking to make a genuine impact on a major construction project, this is an opportunity not to be missed.

The Opportunity

As Senior Design Manager, you'll take ownership of the design management process on a major £80 million data centre development, ensuring that all design information is coordinated, technically compliant and delivered in line with the construction programme.

The project is currently progressing through Stage 4 design, with enabling works scheduled for Q4 2026 and main construction works commencing in Q2 2027.

You'll play a pivotal role in managing the transition from detailed design into construction, working closely with consultants, specialist subcontractors, project teams and key stakeholders to ensure the successful delivery of this technically demanding development.

This is a position offering significant autonomy, technical responsibility and the opportunity to influence design strategy, buildability and project outcomes from an early stage.

The Role

You'll lead the coordination and management of multidisciplinary design activities, ensuring architectural, structural, civil and MEP design packages are fully integrated and aligned with project requirements.

Working closely with the Project Director and wider delivery team, you'll oversee design programmes, manage technical submissions and approvals, coordinate design workshops and proactively identify potential design risks before they impact construction.

You'll also take a leading role in managing consultant and subcontractor design performance, ensuring information is delivered to the required quality, programme and technical standards.

With the complexities associated with major data centre developments, you'll be instrumental in driving collaboration between design and operational teams, resolving technical challenges and ensuring design solutions support efficient construction, commissioning and eventual handover.

You'll also provide guidance and leadership to junior members of the design team, supporting their professional development and contributing to a culture of technical excellence.

About You

You'll be an established Senior Design Manager or experienced Design Manager with a strong background delivering major construction projects for a recognised main contractor or specialist design and build business.

You'll possess excellent technical knowledge, strong leadership capabilities and the confidence to manage complex multidisciplinary design packages.

Experience within Data Centres, Mission Critical, Defence, Pharmaceutical, Industrial or technically demanding Commercial Construction environments would be particularly advantageous.

You'll ideally demonstrate:

*

Proven experience managing design delivery on major construction projects

*

Strong understanding of multidisciplinary design coordination, particularly MEP interfaces

*

Experience managing design consultants, specialist subcontractors and technical stakeholders

*

Excellent knowledge of Building Regulations, CDM and construction design processes

*

Strong programme management, technical assurance and problem-solving capabilities

*

The ability to lead design teams and communicate effectively with senior project stakeholders

A relevant degree, HNC or equivalent qualification in Construction, Engineering, Architecture or a related discipline would be advantageous.

Previous data centre experience would be highly beneficial, although candidates from other technically complex construction sectors are strongly encouraged to apply.

What's on Offer?

*

£85,000 – £95,000 basic salary

*

Car allowance (where eligible)

*

Competitive pension scheme

*

BUPA Healthcare & Cash Plan

*

Electric vehicle scheme

*

Cycle to Work scheme

*

Eyecare vouchers

*

25 days annual leave plus Bank Holidays and your birthday off

*

Opportunity to lead design delivery on a flagship £80 million data centre development

*

Exposure to complex engineering, MEP and mission-critical infrastructure

*

Long-term career progression within a highly respected specialist contractor

*

An exciting pipeline of future projects across the data centre, defence and energy sectors

Interested?

If you're an experienced Senior Design Manager looking for your next major project, this represents an exceptional opportunity to join a growing specialist contractor at an exciting stage of its development.

You'll have the chance to take genuine ownership of the design process, influence the delivery of a landmark data centre development and establish yourself as a key member of a highly experienced project team.

Apply today or contact Walker & Sloan for a confidential discussion.

title: Supervisor, Operations Incinerator
description:
Stericycle is now part of WM. To learn more about WM's acquisition of Stericycle, CLICK HERE to read the press release.


Flexible Schedule: 5/8s Monday-Friday.

What is the value of a WM job? The value of a WM job is more than a paycheck. It’s a way to create opportunities for you and your family.
We Are Stable: Our WM team is home every day, and our team members perform essential and meaningful work.
We Are Committed to Growth: Annual Education Assistance Benefit available for team members.
We Are Investing in You: Amazing Medical, Dental & Vision, 401K with match, discounted stock options, dependent day care, and more!
Who are we? #WeAreWM

Ready to roll with us? Click Apply to join the WM (formerly Waste Management) team today


I. Job Summary

Ensures that the directives of the company and facility manager are followed with regards to establishing, monitoring, and maintaining process productivity and efficiencies on each of the operating shift at the incinerator plant. Reviews and monitors daily operations activity of the DEA controlled substance program to include documentation, practices and procedures. Ensures the plant is in compliance with regulatory agencies including in-house policies related to the DEA driven programs. Monitors and ensures that all other regulatory and safety compliance polices are strictly adhered to. Fosters a One Team, One Goal production culture.

II. Essential Duties and Responsibilities

  • Ensure the incinerator employees and shift leads maintain productivity standards in all phases of their operations. Review shift productivity to identify maximum efficiencies and operational opportunities.
  • Manage all Incineration personnel and ensure they perform their tasks safely while utilizing all PPE and other safety equipment at all times.
  • Manages and maintains regulatory compliance within the plant and plant yard. Maintain and order incinerator processing supplies consisting of PPE, uniforms, cleaning material, processing chemicals, etc., to ensure that adequate inventories are always available.
  • Initiate actions to ensure timely resolution of identified hazards or unsafe conditions or practices.
  • Responsible for the hiring, training and development of Incineration personnel. This also includes ensuring that all monthly and other required employee training, including safety and compliance training, is maintained and up to date.
  • Manages and maintains a high standard of operational excellence in order to maintain a high level of customer satisfaction, either internally or externally. Coordinate customer needs by adhering to a defined processing schedule.
  • Interface proactively with personnel to achieve business goals.
  • Perform facility audits, review of all applicable regulatory paperwork, e.g., Title V or other permit or company specific records, etc.).
  • Manages and monitors daily performance of incinerator employees, directly or within guidance, providing feedback (including growth opportunities). Influence hiring and firing decisions and disciplinary procedures. Assist in resolving plant problems and issues between sales, drivers, and plant/maintenance team.
  • Works with Facility Manager to ensure budget compliance for the operation of the plant process.
  • Coordinates with maintenance concerning shutdown scheduling and maintenance needs.
  • Works directly with the Facility Manager and the Maintenance Manager to identify opportunities for operational improvements as well as identifying short-term and long-term opportunities.
  • Vigorously supports WMHS's commitment to safety, compliance, and corporate cultural initiatives, and supports all policies and procedures established within the policies and procedures manual.
  • Maintain documentation of compliance activities, such as complaints received or investigation outcomes.
  • Participate in the year-end physical count and compile reconciled data.
  • Conduct periodic internal reviews or audits to ensure that compliance procedures are followed. Conduct or direct the internal investigation of compliance issues when needed.
  • Perform other duties and responsibilities, as assigned.


III. Qualifications

A. Required Qualifications

  • Associate's Degree or the equivalent from a two-year college.
  • 3 years demonstrating the ability to manage people in a manufacturing environment, demonstrating the ability to provide safe and regulatory compliant work conditions for all employees.

title: Dean of College of Health and Sciences
description:
FLSA Status: Exempt
Grade: 16


Position Summary
The Dean of the College of Health and Sciences provides strategic, academic, and administrative leadership for the college encompassing seven undergraduate degree programs and one graduate degree program across four academic units: Biological and Environmental Sciences, Physical Sciences, Mathematics and Computer Science, and the School of Nursing. The College employs approximately 44 full-time faculty members and is supported by administrative and technical staff.


The Dean is responsible for advancing the College's academic mission through leadership in academic program
development, faculty and staff development, student success, research and scholarly activity, external partnerships,
resource management, and fundraising. The Dean fosters an environment of interdisciplinary collaboration, innovation,
and academic excellence while ensuring that the College's programs and activities support the strategic priorities of East Central University.


The Dean also provides administrative oversight of the Center for Undergraduate Research and Learning (CURL) and the McNair Scholars Program and works collaboratively with the Oka Water Institute and other university and community partners to advance research, educational opportunities, and regional engagement. The Dean's office is located in the Hays STEM Center, a new facility designed to expand STEM education to meet state workforce needs in healthcare and other critical occupations.


Essential Job Duties
• Provide strategic leadership and vision for the College, establishing priorities and advancing initiatives that support the mission and strategic goals of East Central University.
• Provide administrative oversight and leadership for the College's four academic units: Biological and Environmental Sciences, Physical Sciences, Mathematics and Computer Science, and the School of Nursing.
• Lead the development, implementation, evaluation, and continuous improvement of undergraduate and
graduate academic programs, ensuring program quality, relevance, and alignment with workforce needs and institutional priorities.
• Oversee curriculum development and revision, degree requirements, articulation agreements, catalog descriptions, and academic policies in collaboration with department chairs, faculty, and university leadership.
• Monitor program effectiveness, enrollment trends, student learning outcomes, and workforce and disciplinary developments to inform academic planning and resource allocation.
• Support academic program accreditation, professional standards, assessment, and compliance with applicable institutional, state, and disciplinary requirements.
• Encourage interdisciplinary collaboration across academic departments and programs, including opportunities for collaborative teaching, research, and student engagement.
• Supervise department chairs, faculty members, and College support personnel.
• Conduct performance evaluations and make recommendations regarding hiring, promotion, tenure, retention, and other personnel decisions in accordance with university policies and procedures.
• Support faculty efforts to secure external funding, develop research and scholarly collaborations, and incorporate research and experiential learning into undergraduate and graduate education.
• Provide administrative oversight and strategic direction for the Center for Undergraduate Research and the McNair Scholars Program, supporting opportunities for undergraduate research, scholarly engagement, graduate school preparation, and student achievement.
• Collaborate with the Oka Water Institute to advance shared research, educational initiatives, faculty engagement, and interdisciplinary opportunities, including coordination of shared faculty appointments.
• Foster opportunities for experiential learning, internships, clinical and field-based experiences, undergraduate research, and other high-impact educational practices.
• Develop, manage, and evaluate College budgets, including the allocation of resources for personnel, instructional activities, equipment, laboratory operations, technology, and other academic needs.
• Oversee the effective management, maintenance, and utilization of College facilities, laboratories, instructional equipment, and other resources in collaboration with appropriate university personnel.
• Identify opportunities to leverage institutional resources, external funding, grants, and partnerships to support the College's academic and strategic priorities.
• Develop and lead fundraising initiatives in collaboration with the ECU Foundation.
• Cultivate relationships with alumni, community members, industry representatives, professional organizations, governmental agencies, and other stakeholders to advance the College's mission and secure financial and programmatic support.
• Collaborate with university leadership and other academic and administrative units to advance institutional initiatives and strengthen the University's relationships with regional and statewide partners.
• Create and coordinate recruitment, outreach, and engagement activities that promote the College's academic programs and attract prospective students.
• Serve on university committees and participate in institutional planning and decision-making as appropriate.
• Perform other duties as assigned by the Provost or designee.


Omission of specific statements of duties does not exclude them from the position if the work is similar, related, or a
logical assignment to the position.


Qualifications
• Doctorate degree in a relevant academic discipline
• 3-5 years of academic administrative experience
• 3 years of managerial experience preferred

Licenses/Certifications
• None


Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities
• Demonstrated ability to provide strategic leadership and vision in an academic environment
• Strong financial management and budgeting skills with experience in resource allocation
• Excellent interpersonal and communication skills with ability to build relationships with diverse stakeholders
• Proven ability to develop and implement academic programs and policies
• Strong organizational and administrative skills with attention to detail
• Demonstrated commitment to academic excellence and student success
• Experience in fundraising and donor relations preferred
• Must have a strong work ethic and lead by example
• Must be a professional, credible and respected representative of the institution internally and in the community

title: VP of Strategic Programs
description:
About the role

TrueComp is seeking a VP, Strategic Programs to serve as chief of staff to the CEO. This role owns the company’s value creation plan and operating cadence, leads customer journey design and reporting, and sets the strategy and roadmap for Revenue Operations.

The VP, Strategic Programs will build the operating foundation for TrueComp’s next stage of growth: a clear plan, consistent KPIs and definitions, and reporting for each function. The ideal candidate brings experience from PE-backed software companies, is equally comfortable setting strategy and building the model or dashboard themselves, and can influence senior leaders without formal authority.

This role reports to the CEO and works closely with Sales, Marketing, Product, Finance, and the COO. RevOps execution is primarily outsourced today; to begin, this role sets the roadmap and manages those partners.

What you'll do

Value Creation Plan and Operating Cadence

  • Turn the board-approved value creation plan into initiatives with clear owners, milestones, and KPIs, and keep progress honest.
  • Design and run the operating rhythm: weekly leadership meetings, monthly operating reviews by function, quarterly business reviews, and annual planning.
  • Build a KPI tree that connects ARR growth, NRR, GRR, and EBITDA to the drivers each leader owns. Every leader should have a scorecard they can defend.
  • Partner with Finance on board materials and the operating narrative, and prepare the CEO for board meetings and investor reviews.
  • Stand up and run high-priority cross-functional initiatives when the business needs them, then hand them off cleanly.

Customer Journey Design and Reporting

  • Map the end-to-end customer journey, from first touch through close, onboarding, adoption, renewal, and expansion.
  • Set stage definitions, entry and exit criteria, and handoffs across Marketing, Sales, Customer Success, and Product. Each function still runs its own stages.
  • Instrument every stage in our systems so we can see conversion, velocity, time to value, adoption, and customer health.
  • Connect journey data to NRR and GRR, and surface leading indicators of churn and expansion early enough to change the outcome.
  • Work with Customer Success and Product to act on what the data shows.

RevOps Strategy and Roadmap

Do you find yourself constantly looking for more and better information? Do you want a job where you can use your knowledge and research skills to improve national security? From design to deployment, we deliver customized solutions by connecting global talent with innovative client projects. Our model allows you to work on international challenges, collaborate with diverse teams, and grow your career while being part of a company that values expertise, creativity, and impact.

Project Overview: In this role, you will be an essential part of a high-impact team focused on advanced data analytics, statistical engineering, and the development of code-first dashboards. You will join a collaborative environment dedicated to transforming enterprise data into actionable insights through rigorous statistical methodologies. The project involves working deeply with Snowflake, authoring complex SQL queries, and building robust RShiny applications. As a Senior Data Analytics Engineer, you will take true ownership of your code, apply college-level statistics to ensure high-accuracy data processing, and help transition legacy BI environments into modern, code-driven solutions.

Key Responsibilities

  • Advanced Data Analytics: Author, optimize, and maintain complex, high-accuracy SQL queries against enterprise data warehouses (Snowflake) to extract and transform critical business data.
  • Code-First Dashboard Development: Design, build, and deploy interactive, code-first dashboards primarily using RShiny (and occasionally Streamlit), moving away from traditional drag-and-drop BI tools.
  • Statistical Programming: Apply college-level statistical methods—including linear regression, frequentist methods, and control limits—using R (tidyverse) and Python to derive deep analytical insights.
  • Code Ownership & Version Control: Maintain strict version control using GitLab. Ensure true code ownership by independently understanding and explaining 100% of the codebase (AI-assisted coding is permitted, but blind "vibe coding" is strictly prohibited).
  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Actively participate in Agile ceremonies and collaborate with stakeholders to translate business requirements into governed metrics, semantic layers, and robust statistical models.

Must-Have Skills

  • Experience Level: 5+ years of advanced, senior-level data analytics and statistical engineering experience.
  • Advanced SQL: Proven track record authoring complex, high-accuracy SQL queries against enterprise data warehouses.
  • Data Warehouse & Version Control: Hands-on production experience with Snowflake and GitLab.
  • Code-First Dashboarding (RShiny Mandatory): Practical experience building code-first dashboards using RShiny and Streamlit (strict filter: if a candidate only has one, it must be RShiny; BI-only tools or other dashboard frameworks are not accepted).
  • Statistical Programming (R & Python): Strong proficiency in R (tidyverse) as the primary language, alongside Python (candidates exceptionally strong in R / tidyverse without Python may still be considered).
  • Statistical Foundations: College-level statistics through linear regression, including a solid understanding of frequentist statistical methods and control limits.
  • True Code Ownership (No "Vibe Coding"): Must be able to explain 100% of their own code independently without relying on an AI agent; while AI-assisted coding is encouraged, pure AI-generated "vibe coding" without deep comprehension is not acceptable.
  • Schedule & Ceremony Overlap: Must be available to attend daily/weekly Agile ceremonies scheduled before 12:00 PM CT (US Central Time).

Nice-to-Have Skills

  • Posit Connect: Experience deploying, hosting, and managing RShiny applications on Posit Connect (formerly RStudio Connect).
  • People Analytics / HR Domain: Prior analytical experience working with People Analytics, HR data, or workforce metrics.
  • Tableau: Familiarity with Tableau to reference and transition legacy dashboards.
  • Agentic Analytics: Experience structuring governed metrics, semantic layers, or documentation to enable AI agentic retrieval and exploration.

Time Zone & Collaboration: This role is 100% remote from LATAM and requires mandatory alignment to US Central Time (CST / UTC-5) working hours. Specific flexibility and availability are required to attend daily/weekly Agile ceremonies scheduled before 12:00 PM CT, alongside collaborative sessions within standard business hours.

title: Director, Digital & Search
description:
Who We Are

Finance leaders choose Billtrust to get paid faster, control costs, and maximize customer satisfaction. As the leader in B2B accounts receivable workflow and payment software, we provide the world’s leading brands with AI-powered solutions across the full AR lifecycle—from invoice presentment and payment processing to cash application and collections. With over 2,600 global customers, more than $1 trillion in invoice dollars processed, and a proprietary network of 13 million buyers, Billtrust delivers business value through deep industry expertise and a culture relentlessly focused on meaningful customer outcomes.

We’re an AI-first company, not just in what we build for our customers, but in how we work. Across every function, our teams use AI tools daily to work faster, make better decisions, and deliver higher-quality outcomes. We hire exceptional people, give them cutting-edge AI capabilities, and measure success by the impact they create. If you want to do the best work of your career at the frontier of AI and fintech, Billtrust is the place to do it.

Customers

We relentlessly increase value for customer and do the right thing for them.

Action

We make ‘thoughtfully fast’ decisions, act quickly, cut through red tape, deliver progress not perfection, take ownership and accountability.

Team Spirit

We put the team ahead of ourselves, foster trust and respect, collaborate with passion, despise toxic politics, value our differences, and celebrate together.

Innovation

We challenge the status quo, experiment thoughtfully, and are novel and brilliant in what we create.

Excellence

We love to win, but we hate losing even more. We aspire to be the best and take pride in our work. When we fall short, we own it and come back stronger.

About the Role

The Director, Digital & Organic Search is a critical role responsible for creating and driving Billtrust’s digital, web, search, AI Overviews (AIO), and LinkedIn/Facebook strategy across the organization. You will leverage AI tools and co-worker agents to analyze performance, test new approaches, and accelerate execution, focusing your expertise on strategic direction, channel decisions, and how Billtrust is positioned in organic search and AI search (Google AI Overviews and AI Mode, ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Copilot).

This is a strategy creator and driver role, not a manager of a system that already exists. You will stay at the cutting edge of AI, push the entire marketing team to adopt the latest technology, and continuously track and adjust our approach based on performance. As search and discovery shift toward generative AI, you will define how Billtrust shows up wherever our buyers look for answers. Billtrust.com is the hub that every search, AI, LinkedIn, and social effort points back to, so you will also work closely with Billtrust.com’s web development team to ensure the site performs and Billtrust shows up well. This is a hands-on role: you will set the strategy and stay in the work alongside agency (as needed) and internal partners.

What You’ll Do

Digital, Search & AI Visibility Strategy

  • Create and own the enterprise digital, organic search, AIO, and LinkedIn/Facebook strategy, defining where and how Billtrust shows up across every channel our buyers use to discover and evaluate us, with the exception of peer review sites (e.g. G2).
  • Define how Billtrust is positioned, referenced, and recommended in LLMs and AI-driven search experiences, continuously testing and refining our approach as generative search evolves.
  • Develop standard definitions and goals around AI-driven search as platforms evolve
  • Set the social strategy, including which channels we should and should not be on, the role each plays in brand and pipeline, and how LinkedIn is used as a core channel.
  • In collaboration with our PR team, extend Billtrust’s presence beyond owned channels into the earned and community sources LLMs draw from, including Reddit, Substack, review and comparison sites, analyst coverage, and third-party listings.
  • Unify digital ownership across the organization, serving as the single point of accountability for Billtrust’s digital footprint, with one strategy, one roadmap, and one measurement view across Marketing, Marketing Operations, Demand Generation, Product Marketing, Analytics, and Global teams.
  • Bring a proactive point of view to annual planning and executive discussions on AIO, GEO, and LLM visibility, with clear recommendations on priorities and investment.
  • Other duties as assigned.

Website & Digital Foundation

  • Develop the AEO strategy, while partnering with Billtrust.com web development on execution to ensure the marketing website, as our digital front door, is at the highest degree of readiness for AI-driven search, including organic traffic, conversion, technical SEO, and structured data.
  • Ensure that the content architecture aligns site structure and content to the questions finance buyers ask in search and LLMs.
  • Partner with Web Development, Design, and Content on platform decisions, releases, and continuous optimization.

AI Leadership & Innovation

  • Stay at the forefront of AI and emerging search technology, evaluating and piloting new tools, platforms, and agents, and turning what works into repeatable practice.
  • Push the entire marketing team to use the latest AI technology, coaching teams, sharing playbooks, and raising the bar on what AI-first marketing looks like at Billtrust.
  • Partner with Product Marketing, Content, Demand Generation, Brand, Product, Engineering, Customer and Sales to ensure our AI-search and social positioning reflects our differentiation and resonates with finance leaders.

Partners, Agencies & Team

  • Evaluate, select, and manage agency and technology partners, holding them accountable for measurable results.
  • Recommend the right mix of in-house, agency, and global team resources, and how the function should grow as the strategy matures.

Performance Measurement & Optimization

  • Define the measurement framework for digital, search, AI visibility, and social, tying leading indicators to pipeline and revenue outcomes.
  • Track performance continuously and adjust strategy quickly, shifting investment, channels, and content based on what the data shows.
  • Use AI tools and co-worker agents to surface insights, monitor visibility and share of voice in search and LLMs, and automate reporting, so your time goes to decisions and executive communication.

What Success Looks Like in Year One

  1. A baseline, then a monthly read, of Billtrust’s share of AI answers to a fixed set of finance-leader questions, against named competitors.
  1. Organic and AI-referred traffic and conversion on the pages that drive pipeline.
  1. Organic-sourced and influenced pipeline, reported from the CRM.
  1. A clean technical search baseline through site migrations and major releases.

What You’ll Bring

Required Skills:

  • 12+ years of experience in digital marketing, search (SEO/SEM), and social strategy, ideally in a B2B environment.
  • Proven track record of creating and driving digital and search strategy from the ground up, rather than administering an existing program.
  • Hands-on experience with AI-driven search, including AIO, generative engine optimization, and positioning a brand within LLMs.
  • Deep expertise in LinkedIn and B2B social strategy, including channel selection, organic and paid approaches, and audience development.
  • Hands-on experience with website strategy and performance, including CMS platforms, site migrations, and technical SEO.
  • Strong analytical skills with a demonstrated ability to track performance, draw insights, and adjust strategy quickly.
  • Track record driving AI adoption across a team or function, including influencing peers and leaders to change how they work.
  • Excellent communication skills, with the ability to translate complex strategy into clear direction for executives and cross-functional partners.
  • Experience selecting, directing, and managing agency partners to deliver measurable results.
  • Hands-on approach: comfortable doing the work, not only directing it.

Preferred Skills:

  • Experience in B2B SaaS, fintech, or payments marketing.
  • Experience building AI agents or automated workflows into marketing operations.
  • Experience developing attribution or visibility metrics for AI search and LLM-driven discovery.
  • Experience supporting account-based marketing to enterprise finance buyers.
  • Experience leading cross-functional initiatives without direct authority.
  • Experience with multilingual or global search strategy.
  • Experience with Webflow.

The expected base salary range for this position is $191,000 - $226,000 annually.
Compensation may vary depending on several factors, including a candidate’s qualifications, skills, experience, competencies, and geographic location. Some roles may qualify for extra incentives like equity, commissions, or other variable performance-related bonuses. Further details will be provided by our Talent Acquisition team during the interview process.

What You’ll Get

At Billtrust, we believe your total rewards should reflect the impact you make. Our benefits package includes comprehensive health coverage, competitive retirement, generous PTO and parental leave, flexible work options, and meaningful investment in your professional development. We’re building something special and we want you to feel supported while doing it.

title: Director, Planning and Performance
description:
Revolution Medicines is a global, commercial-state oncology company dedicated to discovering, developing and delivering innovative medicines for patients with RAS-addicted cancers. Leveraging its differentiated RAS(ON) tri-complex inhibitor platform, the company is advancing a broad, integrated portfolio of oral RAS(ON) inhibitors designed to directly target the active, cancer-driving state of RAS. Founded on rigorous scientific inquiry and a willingness to challenge long-held assumptions, Revolution Medicines is committed to changing the trajectory of disease for patients with RAS-addicted cancers worldwide.

Our people are united by a shared way of working: follow the science, challenge assumptions, act with urgency and hold ourselves to a high standard of rigor—all in service of patients.

The Opportunity

This is a unique opportunity to play a critical role in advancing Revolution Medicines' commercialization strategy during a period of significant growth. We are seeking an experienced and highly collaborative Director, Planning & Performance to build and lead the commercialization planning, performance management, and operating-governance capabilities that enable consistent execution across global, regional, and local teams.

This role sits within the Global Commercialization Effectiveness & Operations (CE&O) function and reports to the Executive Director, Global Commercialization Effectiveness. The Director, Planning & Performance will own the annual commercialization planning cadence, performance review rhythm, operating calendar, decision rights, core processes, and vendor governance.

In close partnership with Commercial, Medical, Finance, Global Analytics and Insights, Supply Chain, Regulatory, Market Access, and regional teams, you will create the governance needed to make timely, high-quality decisions. You will define and continually improve the global-regional-local operating model, with clear accountability, handoffs, and escalation paths.

Operating in a build-while-scaling environment, you will bring clarity, discipline, and insight to a complex commercialization organization. As the capability matures, this role may expand to include people leadership responsibilities.

What You'll Do

  • Own the end-to-end annual commercialization planning cadence, integrating strategic planning, brand and tactical planning, resource planning, and budgeting.

  • Establish planning standards, templates, milestones, and governance that align global, regional, and local plans and make interdependencies, trade-offs, and decisions visible.

  • Partner with Finance to ensure the commercialization plans translate into a robust budget, forecast, and financial tracking process; including periodic re-planning and prioritization as assumptions change.

  • Design and lead the commercialization performance-management framework, including KPIs, targets, dashboards, review materials, action tracking, and a consistent rhythm of business reviews.

  • Partner with Finance and Global Analytics and Insights to define the data, reporting, and analytical infrastructure required for reliable, decision-ready performance management.

  • Facilitate global, regional, and local business performance reviews; ensure insights translate into clear decisions, corrective actions, accountable owners, and follow-through.

  • Define and operationalize the global-regional-local commercialization operating model, including roles, decision rights, handoffs, escalation pathways, and key governance forums.

  • Establish and maintain the commercialization operating calendar, including planning cycles, governance forums, performance reviews, and key cross-functional milestones.

  • Develop and maintain SOPs, process flows, RACI frameworks, and other practical tools that create consistent ways of working without adding unnecessary complexity.

  • Identify operational gaps and friction points across teams; lead practical improvements that strengthen execution, reduce duplication, and improve organizational effectiveness.

  • Establish vendor-governance standards for commercialization capabilities, including planning, service reviews, scope management, performance assessment, risk management, and value realization.

  • Create clear performance narratives and recommendations for senior leadership that connect market results, execution progress, risks, and investment decisions.

Who You Are

You are a seasoned commercialization operations and planning leader who thrives in complex, cross-functional environments. You excel at creating practical structure amid ambiguity, bringing diverse teams together around a common operating rhythm, and maintaining focus on the decisions and actions that matter most.

You combine strong planning, performance-management, and governance experience with sound judgment, analytical rigor, and a collaborative, solutions-oriented approach. You can influence without authority, communicate effectively with senior leaders and working teams, and translate complex business information into clear, actionable priorities.

Required Skills, Experience and Education:

  • Bachelor's degree with 10+ years of relevant experience in biotechnology, pharmaceuticals, healthcare, or a related industry.

  • Significant experience leading commercialization planning, budgeting, forecasting, performance management, business operations, strategy, or related cross-functional initiatives.

  • Demonstrated experience designing and managing annual planning and performance-review processes within a global pharmaceutical or biotechnology organization.

  • Strong business and analytical skills, including the ability to define meaningful KPIs and translate complex data into clear insights, recommendations, and action plans.

  • Experience working across global and regional operating models and coordinating geographically dispersed stakeholders.

  • Proven ability to establish governance, clarify decision rights, and drive adoption of new processes and ways of working.

  • Experience partnering with senior leaders and teams across Commercial, Finance, Medical Affairs, Market Access, Regulatory, PDM, and other cross-functional areas.

  • Proven ability to influence without authority and drive alignment across diverse stakeholder groups.

  • Track record of thriving in a fast-paced, evolving environment with a proactive, collaborative, and solutions-oriented mindset.

  • Excellent communication, facilitation, interpersonal, organizational, and attention-to-detail skills.

Preferred Skills:

  • Advanced degree (MBA, MS, PhD, or equivalent).

  • Oncology or specialty-pharma commercialization experience.

  • Experience establishing a commercialization operating model or planning and performance capability in a growth-stage organization.

  • Experience supporting commercialization across multiple markets, regions, or indications.

  • Experience with commercial analytics, dashboarding, or technology-enabled planning and performance-management tools.

Drives completion of programs to aggressive development and delivery timelines while operating within contractual, budget, resource, technical, and quality requirements. Owns portfolio-level risk management and ensures risks, issues, and opportunities are identified, escalated, and resolved appropriately. Partners with engineering, supply chain, operations, contracts, finance, quality, and business development leadership to ensure alignment of resources and priorities.

Serves as a senior customer interface and communicates program and portfolio status to internal and external stakeholders, including senior government and industry customers. Negotiates scope, schedule, resources, priorities, and contractual commitments to ensure program success. Develops and mentors program leadership and establishes a high-performing organization capable of executing increasingly complex and large-scale programs.

In addition to program execution responsibilities, the Head of Programs leads strategic capture and business development efforts to expand the portfolio. This includes shaping opportunities well in advance of formal solicitations, developing competitive technical and management approaches, and partnering with business development, engineering, contracts, and pricing teams to position Booz Allen for successful bids. The role drives early and meaningful engagement with senior government and industry stakeholders, orchestrates cross-functional capture teams, informs price‑to‑succeed strategies, and ensures proposal development reflects both client mission needs and Booz Allen’s differentiated capabilities. The Head of Programs strengthens relationships across the acquisition and contracting community, contributes to win strategies and teaming decisions, and advances growth through disciplined capture planning, solutioning, and preparation for new pursuits.

  • Experience in managing full program lifecycle activities including design, development, integration, test, qualification, and delivery

title: Senior Manager -Materials Management
description:
Primary Purpose:

The Sr. Manager – Materials Management is responsible for leading enterprise-wide materials management strategy and execution to ensure safe, reliable, and cost-effective operations across the company. This role provides leadership for inventory optimization, warehouse operations, materials planning, and master data governance to ensure the right materials are available to support Operations and Maintenance while minimizing total delivered cost and working capital. This position also includes materials management support for capital projects (pipelines and facilities), pipe & materials inspection teams, ensuring project material readiness, effective staging and warehousing strategies, and alignment between project delivery teams and enterprise supply chain standards. In an oil & gas environment, this role is critical to improving asset uptime, enabling on-time project execution, ensuring strong internal controls, and standardizing materials management practices across terminals, plants, pipelines, and field locations.

We are seeking a proven, results-driven leader to drive operational excellence across materials management functions, build high-performing teams, and partner with Procurement, Maintenance, Operations, Project Delivery, Finance, and HSE to implement scalable processes, tools, and performance management systems. This role will lead transformation initiatives such as inventory reduction, critical spares programs, warehouse productivity improvements, project material controls, and ERP enablement while maintaining compliance with company policies and regulatory requirements.

Sr. Manager – Materials Management Job Responsibilities

  • Develop and lead the enterprise materials management strategy including inventory planning, warehousing, and materials governance aligned to business priorities, reliability goals, and capital project delivery requirements.
  • Lead and coach materials management teams across multiple locations; establish clear expectations, accountability, and development plans.
  • Own inventory optimization programs (e.g., min/max, ROP, safety stock, lead time governance, critical spares strategy) to improve service levels and reduce working capital.
  • Ensure warehouse operations excellence across receiving, put-away, picking, issuing, returns, staging/kitting, and material traceability; drive productivity and safety improvements.
  • Establish and enforce item master and materials data governance, including standardization, cataloging, and controls for master item creation and changes.
  • Provide materials management leadership for capital projects (pipelines and facilities), including materials inspection personnel, project material planning, expediting coordination, warehousing/staging plans, surplus management, and closeout/disposition processes.
  • Partner with Project Delivery teams to define and implement project material controls (e.g., material status reporting, consumption tracking, heat/lot traceability where required, and alignment to project schedules).
  • Partner with Maintenance and Operations to improve material readiness for work execution, turnaround/outage support, and emergency response requirements.
  • Collaborate with Procurement and Strategic Sourcing to align material strategies, supplier performance, stocking agreements, and contracts that impact inventory, project execution, and service levels.
  • Lead KPI development and performance management (e.g., inventory turns, service level/fill rate, stockouts, aged/obsolete inventory, cycle count accuracy, warehouse productivity, and project material availability).
  • Oversee cycle count programs, physical inventory execution, and variance resolution; ensure audit readiness and compliance with internal controls and SOX-related requirements where applicable.
  • Lead continuous improvement initiatives using Lean/Six Sigma principles; standardize SOPs and deploy best practices across sites and project teams.
  • Sponsor and manage technology enablement initiatives (ERP improvements, WMS/barcode/mobile solutions, analytics) including business case development, implementation support, and adoption.
  • Manage materials management budgets, including labor, warehouse services, and related operating expenses; identify cost savings opportunities including project-related logistics and warehousing efficiencies.
  • Provide regular updates to leadership on performance, risks, and progress against transformation goals; escalate issues as needed with recommended actions.

Job Requirements

Education

  • Bachelor’s degree from an Accredited Institution in Supply Chain, Business, Engineering, Logistics, Finance, or related field, or equivalent experience.

Experience / Specific Knowledge

  • Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain, Business, Engineering, Logistics, Finance, or related field preferred but not mandatory.
  • 8–12+ years of experience in materials management, maintenance supply chain, warehousing, inventory planning, and/or project materials management (oil & gas or heavy industrial preferred).
  • 3–7+ years of people leadership experience, including leading multi-site teams and influencing cross-functional stakeholders.
  • Demonstrated experience supporting capital projects (pipelines and facilities), including material staging, logistics coordination, project material controls, and closeout processes.
  • Strong working knowledge of inventory optimization concepts (min/max, ROP, safety stock, critical spares) and warehouse operations best practices.
  • Experience with ERP systems (Oracle Cloud, SAP MM, Maximo or similar) and master data governance; WMS and barcode/mobile enablement experience preferred
  • Demonstrated ability to build KPI-driven operating rhythms and deliver measurable improvements in service level, working capital, project readiness, and productivity.
  • Knowledge of internal controls, audit requirements, and inventory accounting fundamentals
  • Strong communication, executive presence, and change leadership skills in a fast-paced operational environment.

Competencies, Skills & Abilities:

  • Excellent communication skills and capable to animate diverse and demanding stakeholders to foster collaboration across Operations, Maintenance, Procurement, Project Delivery, Finance, and HSE.
  • Strategic and analytical thinker with strong conceptual skills; able to develop business cases and translate strategy into executable roadmaps.
  • Strong leadership capability with proven ability to coach teams, drive accountability, and build a high-performance culture.
  • Ability to structure and prioritize multiple initiatives across sites and capital projects while maintaining focus on safety, compliance, and operational continuity.
  • Strong problem-solving, conflict resolution, and decision-making skills, including ability to operate effectively under pressure.
  • Customer service mindset with a sense of urgency and “can-do” disposition; responsive to operational and project needs while maintaining governance and controls.
  • Demonstrated continuous improvement mindset; capable of driving standardization and sustainable change.
  • Ability to maintain confidentiality when appropriate and exercise sound judgment with sensitive operational, project, and financial information.
  • Must be able to perform all essential and marginal functions of the job.
  • Must be able to work with a team, take direction from senior leadership, focus attention on details, follow work rules and adhere to established work schedules.
  • Ability to successfully perform multiple tasks with strict deadlines, including support of turnarounds/outages and emergent operational events.
  • Job level commensurate with experience and skill sets; Must possess and maintain a valid driver´s license and a driving record satisfactory to the company and its insurers.

Preferred Education, Experience, Certifications, Competencies, Skills & Abilities

  • Experience designing and implementing end-to-end maintenance supply chain capabilities including critical spares governance, BOM alignment, catalog enablement, and kitting/staging.
  • Experience deploying warehouse technology solutions (WMS, barcode/RFID, mobile receiving/issuing) and advanced analytics/Power BI.
  • Strong proficiency in Oracle Cloud and/or SAP MM environments, including global templates, governance, and shared services models.
  • Experience with project controls integration (schedule alignment, material status reporting, and coordination with construction management) preferred.
  • Experience and knowledge of industry best practices in pipe & materials management processes & procedures, to include pipe yard & warehouse operations

title: MFLC Counselor: Short Term or As Needed Coverage - NB Kitsap, Washington
description:
Description

Make a difference in the lives of our military Service Members and their families with your expertise in counseling and mental health – without the fuss of insurance, treatment plans, or overhead. Military and Family Life Counselors (MFLCs) are the first line of defense for our Service Members’ mental health, and we need flexible, ready-to-serve counselors willing to jump in at a moment’s notice.

Leidos seeks passionate licensed mental healthcare providers ready to embrace a flexible PRN-type schedule, stepping in where needed across military installations and communities to safeguard and enhance mental well-being. MFLCs proactively provide counseling services, preventative in nature, to address and provide solution-focused approaches to issues before they become greater challenges. Interested counselors may support either adults or minors in a wide variety of assignments including but not limited to being embedded with a military unit, supporting military families, or working within a school setting.

What is the Mission Ready Reserve (MRR)? Mission Ready Reserve MFLCs are trained and available counselors ready to serve when called upon. Working as a Mission Ready Reserve MFLC allows counselors to focus wholeheartedly on their passion for helping others, unencumbered by administrative burdens. MRR counselors are assignment-ready and taking an assignment is at the discretion of the MRR counselor.

The need at NB Kitsap is: Adult Positions and CYB Positions.

Adult Counseling:

Adult MFLCs provide support, including counseling, consultation, and outreach to eligible Service Members and adult family members. Counseling provided through the MFLC program is an adjunct and supplemental to the formal military behavioral and physical health treatment system. Adult counseling service is needed on military installations, either at community service buildings or embedded with a unit. The focus is on enhancing operational readiness and increasing individual and family resiliency by offering support on issues such as:

  • Relationships
  • Stress management
  • Parenting and parent-child communications
  • Child behavioral issues
  • Frequent relocations and deployments
  • Financial and budget issues
  • Job stress

Child and Youth Behavioral (CYB) Counseling:

CYB-MFLCs provide support, including counseling, consultation, and outreach to eligible children, youth, parents, staff, and faculty. Counselors may observe, participate, and engage in activities with children and youth; provide coaching, guidance, and support to staff and parents; and model behavior management techniques for staff and parents. CYB counseling services may be needed at installations, Child Development Centers (CDCs), Department of War Education Activity (DoWEA) schools, summer schools, camps, and programs DoW-wide, addressing issues such as:

  • Identifying feelings
  • Bullying
  • Conflict resolution
  • Self-esteem
  • Managing anger and aggression
  • Separation from parents
  • Problem-solving
  • Coping with deployment and reunification
  • Transition and moving
  • Sibling and parental relationships
  • Time management

MRR MFLC Service Oriented Model:

  • The Mission Ready Reserve model allows you to focus on your counseling and the military Service
  • Members and the families you will be supporting
  • No insurance to file
  • No progress notes required
  • No treatment plans to develop
  • Intuitive reporting tools

MRR MFLC will also benefit from:

  • Unlimited and free CEUs through a Leidos affiliate
  • Reimbursement for job-related license renewal fees
  • Eligibility to participate in 401K retirement plan
  • Access to health and wellness programs with cashback incentives
  • Access to Leidos’ Employee Discount Program and exclusive discount marketplace

MRR MFLC responsibilities include:

  • Face-to-face counseling to military Service Members and their families (individual, couples, family, and children)
  • Recommending appropriate referrals and handoffs based on your experienced differential clinical skills to military and community resources according to the needs of military Service Members and their families
  • Offer presentations to address social skills development and social emotional learning that is crucial for early childhood development
  • Build rapport with Service Members, spouses, and children by attending installation and community events
  • Help families and children with challenges that are particular to the military community, transitions, reoccurring moves, frequent separations, deployments, and more

Environment:

At the direction of the Department of War (DoW), duties are performed in multiple indoor locations (approximately 60%) and outdoor locations (approximately 40%). The indoor locations are located on a military installation, a school setting, or a child development center (CDC) setting controlled by the DoW. title: Project Manager
description:
The issue


We are passionate about supporting businesses in their energy transition through the development of solar projects, helping them reduce their carbon footprint, optimize energy costs and strengthen their energy independence.



The Project


We are currently looking for a Project Manager to join a major utility-scale solar PV project in Ireland.



Overview of the role


• Lead the construction of the 162 MWp solar PV plant from mobilisation through commissioning.

• Oversee civil works, structures, module installation, DC/AC cabling, inverters, substations, grid connection and commissioning.

• Coordinate site teams, subcontractors and suppliers.

• Monitor construction schedule, progress, productivity, costs and contractual matters.

• Ensure compliance with Irish PV standards, HSE and quality requirements.

• Manage site documentation, reporting, variations, punch lists and contractual follow-up.

• Coordinate testing, commissioning, handover and final acceptance.

• Act as the main site interface with the client and project stakeholders.



Requirements


  • Proven experience as Project Manager leading large-scale projects ranging from 80 to 100 MW, including solar PV plants and electrical substations.
  • Experience on projects across Europe is acceptable, provided the candidate also has knowledge of Irish labour law and PSCS (Project Supervisor Construction Stage) health and safety regulations.
  • Proven ability to manage and coordinate 3 to 7 subcontractors and joint venture partners.
  • Strong project leadership skills, acting as the central point of coordination, overseeing all stakeholders and ensuring successful project delivery from start to finish.
  • Fluent English is mandatory.

About Our Team

Our employees thrive in a culture that's fast-paced and ego-free, where innovation and collaboration are encouraged at every turn. We are an organization that provides federal agencies instant access to experienced and talented professionals who understand their unique challenges and know the most efficient ways to address them. We are continually investing in resources and talent, so we stay prepared with specialized teams in place who are experts in creating tailored technologies.
